stories.title: No UP minister’s child studies in a govt school:Where do ministers’ children study? Bhaskar investigation reveals
stories.summary: “Council schools have been transformed. Their infrastructure is now 96% better than before,” claims Uttar Pradesh Basic Education Minister Sandeep Singh. Yet, not a single minister in the Yogi government sends their children to these schools. None of their children study in the UP Board system either. So, where do the children of Uttar Pradesh ministers study? Dainik Bhaskar investigated to find out. Dainik Bhaskar collected details about the families of the state’s ministers and the Assembly Speaker. The findings show that 18 ministers have children or school-going grandchildren, and all of them study in convent or reputed private schools. There are 38 ministers whose children have already completed their education or whose grandchildren are not yet school-going. Four ministers are either unmarried or married but do not have children. They don’t even prefer UP Board English-medium schools The investigation found that ministers do not prefer government schools for their children. They also do not opt for English-medium schools affiliated with the UP Board. Instead, their children study in schools affiliated with the CBSE or ICSE boards. Of the 18 ministers with school-going children or grandchildren, the children of 17 ministers study in CBSE schools. Only the grandchildren of Dr. Sanjay Nishad study at an ICSE-affiliated school. Now, find out which schools the ministers’ children study in… He has three granddaughters and two grandsons. Four of them are studying. The elder son, Dr. Dushyant, has two daughters, aged 6 and 10. The second son, Prashant, has a 4-year-old daughter and a 10-year-old son. All four are studying at Bareilly Convent School. The third son, Yashwant, has a young son who does not attend school yet. Arun Kumar is a resident of Bareilly. Of the two sons of his son, Dr. Varun, Shaurya is in play school, while Mihan (6) is studying at Chitkara International School. Minister of State Sanjay Singh Gangwar is from Pilibhit. His 5-year-old son, Mir Singh Gangwar, is studying at Delhi Public School in Pilibhit. The school is affiliated with the CBSE. The Cabinet Minister has one son and two daughters. All of them are married. He has one grandson and one granddaughter, who are studying at a prestigious convent school in Lucknow. Nitin Agarwal is from Hardoi. He has government accommodation in Lucknow. His one son and two daughters are studying at a convent school in Lucknow. Minister of State Baby Rani Maurya's son, Abhinav Maurya, has two sons studying at Delhi Public School in Agra. This school is affiliated with the CBSE. Minister of State Dinesh Khatik's family lives in Meerut. His two children study at the renowned K.L. International School there. The school is affiliated with the CBSE. Minister of State Somendra Tomar's two children study at Meerut's Dewan Public School, while one of his daughters is living in Delhi and pursuing her graduation. The son is in high school. He is studying at GD Goenka School in Lucknow. The daughter has passed the intermediate examination and is studying at a boarding school in Dehradun. One daughter has completed her education. Minister of State Pratibha Shukla has two grandsons. Both are studying at a convent school in Kanpur Nagar. This school is affiliated with the CBSE. His son has completed Class 12 from a private school. He is now going abroad for further studies. Satish Mahana has one grandson and one granddaughter. His grandson is 14 years old and studies at a public school in Kanpur. His granddaughter is pursuing higher education. Minister Daya Shankar Singh's two daughters are studying at a private school in Lucknow under the CBSE board. Since the divorce, both daughters have been living with their mother, Swati Singh. Kunwar Brijesh Singh has two children-a son and a daughter. Both are currently studying at a boarding school in Dehradun. Two of Hansraj's three sons are married. He has one grandson, who is studying in nursery at a public school near their home. Minister Sanjay Nishad has three sons. His eldest son has two children, one of whom is studying in the third grade. Praveen, his second son, has a son studying in the third grade and a daughter studying in Class 2. This means all four of Minister Nishad's grandchildren are studying under the ICSE board at City Montessori School in Lucknow. O.P. Rajbhar has three grandsons. His eldest grandson is 6 years old and is studying at G.D. Goenka World School, Ansal, Lucknow. The other two grandsons are still young.

stories.title: Raksha Bandhan on 28 August, auspicious time till 9 am:No Bhadra this year, avoid cartoon-themed Rakhis; know how to perform Rakhi puja
stories.summary: Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated this year on Friday, 28 August. Several auspicious combinations are forming during the festival this time. The full moon (Purnima) will begin on 27 August and continue until 9 am on 28 August. Since the Hindu calendar gives importance to the Udayatithi, or the date prevailing at sunrise, Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on 28 August. The most auspicious time to tie Rakhi will be before 9 am. However, Rahu Kaal will prevail from 9:45 am to 12 pm. There will be no Bhadra on Raksha Bandhan this year, allowing sisters to tie Rakhi to their brothers without any restrictions. Astrologer Shriram Sharma said Sukarma Yoga will begin around 9 am. Religious rituals and other auspicious activities performed during this period are considered especially fruitful. This year's Raksha Bandhan will also fall under Shatabhisha Nakshatra, which is associated with mental peace. According to astrologers, these auspicious combinations make this year's festival favourable for stability and strength in the bond between brothers and sisters. Tie Rakhi during the morning Purnima is more auspicious According to Girish Guru, a priest of Mangala Gauri in Varanasi, the festival of Raksha Bandhan can be celebrated throughout the day, excluding Rahukal, as there is no influence of Bhadra during the day. However, tying the Rakhi during the Purnima Tithi is considered extremely auspicious. The best time to tie the Rakhi is from 6:00 AM to 9:45 AM. After this, Rahukaal begins, and one should avoid tying the Rakhi during that time. Following this, there is another auspicious time to tie the Rakhi from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM. Rakhi can also be tied after 2:00 PM; there is no fault in doing so. Auspicious work done during Sukarma Yoga is fruitful Astrologer Shriram Sharma stated that this year, a combination of Sukarma Yoga is also forming on Raksha Bandhan. Religious and auspicious activities performed during this yoga yield good results. In such a situation, it is considered auspicious for a sister to tie a protective thread (Raksha Sutra) on her brother's wrist and pray for his long life, happiness, and prosperity. Meanwhile, the Shatabhisha Nakshatra brings mental peace and health benefits. If a sister prays for her brother's longevity during this Nakshatra, the brother's health remains good. Tying a Mauli or Silk thread is auspicious According to astrologers, Chinese rakhis (which feature cartoons) should not be tied to either younger or older brothers. It is a mere show. Tying a Raksha Sutra made of traditional Mauli or silk thread is considered more auspicious. You can gift a toy to your younger brothers as a token of love. Earlier, a Raksha Sutra was made by dyeing raw cotton thread in yellow. Brahmins would also tie this same Raksha Sutra to their patrons, wishing them a long and healthy life. How to perform Rakhi puja On the day of Raksha Bandhan, meditate on God after taking a bath. Apply a tilak to your brother, perform aarti, and tie the protective thread (rakhi) while wishing for his long life. Sisters should observe a fast before tying the rakhi to their brothers. According to tradition, the sister prays for her brother's happiness, prosperity, and longevity, while the brother takes a vow to protect his sister. Shravani is celebrated on the day of Rakhi itself According to astrologer Shriram Sharma, the Shravani festival is also celebrated on the day of Raksha Bandhan. It is considered a major festival for Brahmins. On this day, Brahmins perform penance after bathing and religious rituals. In fact, the primary duty of Brahmins is to conduct prayers and religious rituals. In such a situation, special rituals are performed on the Shravani festival to atone for mistakes made knowingly or unknowingly throughout the year. After bathing in the Ganga, a pledge is taken through a Yajna, so that one may be liberated from the sins incurred knowingly or unknowingly. In Indian tradition, separate major festivals are also considered for the four main Varnas. The Shravani festival is celebrated on the day of Raksha Bandhan itself. In Varanasi, a large number of Brahmins gather at the Ganga ghats on this day to perform religious rituals related to bathing, atonement, and Yagnopavit (sacred thread ceremony).

stories.title: UP to get 5 new link expressways:80% land acquisition complete, work to begin before elections; know which cities will benefit
stories.summary: The foundation stone for 5 new link expressways will be laid. The target is to complete all of these within 3 years before the 2027 assembly elections in UP. The districts of Farrukhabad, Bulandshahr, Etawah, Agra, and Noida in Western UP will benefit the most from this. Jhansi and Jalaun in Bundelkhand will also receive significant benefits. The government has allocated ₹18,400 crore in the supplementary budget for their construction. Once these are built, the number of expressways in UP will increase to 20. The government's plan is to present UP's identity in the elections as the 'state with the highest number of expressways in the country'. Know about the 5 new link expressways This link expressway will start from Sector-21, Noida (near Film City) and connect to the Ganga Expressway near Syana via Bulandshahr. Its construction will provide better connectivity to industrial sectors 28, 29, 32, and 33 of the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA). Connectivity from Noida, Bulandshahr, Khurja, Syana, and surrounding areas to Jewar Airport will become easier. Cargo movement from the airport will increase. Access to Agra, Greater Noida, and the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway will become more convenient. It will take only 35-40 minutes to reach Noida from Bulandshahr by car. Its starting point will be at approximately the 24.8 km mark of the Yamuna Expressway. It will pass through 8 villages in Noida and 48 villages in Bulandshahr. About 20 km of its stretch will be in the New Noida region. This link expressway will connect the Agra-Lucknow Expressway in Etawah to the Ganga Expressway in Hardoi. Its biggest benefit will be for Farrukhabad, which until now was not directly connected to any major expressway network. Finished goods from Farrukhabad's potato production and textile printing industries will reach the Delhi-Lucknow markets faster. Vehicles coming from Agra or Delhi will be able to directly access the Ganga Expressway to head towards Purvanchal or Western UP. Once the Farrukhabad Link Expressway is built, it will take only 1 hour to reach Hardoi from Etawah by car. Preparations are also underway to build logistics parks in Khimsepur and surrounding areas of Farrukhabad. This expressway will directly connect Jhansi to the Bundelkhand Expressway. Once the Jhansi Link Expressway is built, it will be possible to reach Delhi from Jhansi in 4 hours. It will pass through 63 villages in Jhansi and Jalaun districts, as well as the Garautha, Tahrauli, Moth, and Sadar tehsils. The construction of the Jhansi Link Expressway will begin near Phoolpura village in Jalaun on the Bundelkhand Expressway. It will be built up to Pipra in Jhansi. The Jhansi Link Expressway will pass through the Bundelkhand Industrial Development Authority area and the Defence Corridor. This will benefit the industrial units located there. This is being built to connect the Agra-Lucknow Expressway with the Purvanchal Expressway. It will start near Mohan Road (Lucknow) and connect to the Purvanchal Expressway near Gosaiganj (Lucknow). Currently, vehicles traveling from Delhi or Agra to Ayodhya, Azamgarh, and Ghazipur have to pass through Lucknow city. This takes an extra one and a half to two hours. After the new link expressway is built, vehicles will be able to go directly towards Varanasi. This will reduce travel time by 2 hours. It will take only 20 to 25 minutes by car to reach Raebareli Road from Mohan Road. This will connect the Bundelkhand Expressway to Chitrakoot Dham. With the construction of this link, devotees coming to Chitrakoot from Delhi-NCR, Lucknow, and Agra will get direct connectivity. The journey from Delhi to Chitrakoot is expected to be completed in about 6 hours. It will start from the Bundelkhand Expressway near Bharatkoop and go up to Ranipur Bhatt/Ahmadganj on the Bedi Puliya-Ramghat road. The construction of the expressway will make it easier to reach Ramghat, Kamadgiri, and the ghats of the Mandakini River. This will boost religious tourism. Additionally, it will also help in taking Chitrakoot's wooden toys and local handicrafts to larger markets. 80% of the land for the expressway acquired from farmers The Uttar Pradesh Expressways Industrial Development Authority (UPEIDA) is working on 5 new link expressways. UPEIDA ACEO Haripratap Shahi says the land acquisition process is almost in the final stage. The foundation stone will be laid as soon as the government gives the signal. 80 to 92% of the land acquisition work for all five link expressways has been completed. Tenders have been issued, and construction will begin after the work is allotted to the companies. 'The construction of link expressways will benefit the BJP' Senior journalist Ratanmani Lal says, 'The expansion of the expressway and highway network has brought a major change in UP's image across the country. A good road network is always seen as linked to the state's development. When transport is efficient and affordable, investments come into the state. Naturally, employment will also increase. In such a situation, it can be said that the BJP will get a direct political benefit from these foundation stone laying ceremonies held before the elections. At the same time, the areas through which these link expressways will pass will also see economic benefits.'

stories.title: Bihar worker dies by suicide in cowshed:Took extreme step over family problems; had started job just 20 days ago
stories.summary: Wednesday morning, the body of a labourer was found hanging inside a cowshed in Parmanandpur, under the Shivpur police station area of Varanasi, triggering panic among local residents. They immediately informed the police. Police reached the spot and identified the deceased as Sanoj Sharma, a resident of Rahta village under Kumarkhand police station in Bihar’s Madhepura district and son of the late Damodar Sharma. Sanoj had arrived in Varanasi around 20 days ago to work at the cowshed and help with household chores. Family found him hanging when they went to give breakfast According to homeowner Shiv Shankar Pandey, Sanoj fed the animals and got them milked at the cowshed on Wednesday morning, as usual. He then went to bathe and wash. At around 8:30 a.m., when family members went to the cowshed to give him breakfast, they found him hanging from an iron angle fixed to the tin shed with a rope. They immediately informed the police. Shivpur police reached the spot around 10 a.m. The police brought down the body and sent it to the mortuary for a postmortem examination. Sanoj was married and had children. His family in Bihar has been informed about his death over the phone. Police investigating the reason behind the death According to police, the exact circumstances surrounding Sanoj’s death are yet to be ascertained. Officers reached the spot, conducted an investigation and questioned nearby residents for information. A forensic team also collected evidence from the site. Police brought the body down, completed the inquest proceedings and sent it to the morgue for a postmortem examination. Sanoj’s family members in Bihar were informed about the incident over the phone. Sanoj was married and had young children. Police said further legal action will be taken after his family reaches Varanasi and submits a written complaint.

stories.title: Ganga water enters school, 50 bighas of crops submerged:Children shifted to nearby school; flood threat rises in Katri villages
stories.summary: As the Ganga’s water level rises in Kanpur, flood concerns are growing in the Katri region. Water has entered Lodhwakheda village near the Ganga Barrage, with nearly two feet of water accumulating outside the primary school and some water reaching the school premises. For the safety of the children, classes are now being held at a nearby upper primary school. See 2 pictures... Water enters vegetable fields and guava orchards Apart from Lodhawakheda, Ganga water has also started reaching Chainpurwa and Devnipurwa. Around 50 bighas of crops in the Katri region have already been submerged. Vegetable fields and guava orchards have also been damaged. Villagers say the water level is rising rapidly. The water level rises faster at night, raising fears that floodwater could soon enter homes in the villages. Water rose at night, crops submerge Kusuma, a resident of Chainpurwa, said the water level rose significantly during the night, submerging standing crops in the fields. “Given the rate at which the water is rising, we fear it may soon reach our homes. We are increasingly worried as the water continues to rise, but this is a problem we face every year.” Water level rising for more than two days Nikhil, a resident of Lodhwakheda, said the Ganga’s water level has been rising continuously for the past two days. Water has entered both the premises and the building of the primary school, while nearby guava orchards and vegetable fields have also been submerged. As the river continues to rise, concern among residents of the Katri region is growing. Villagers are keeping a close watch on the water level, while the administration is also monitoring the affected areas.

stories.title: Heavy rain warning in 31 UP districts:Nepal floods trigger state alert; villages being evacuated in Maharajganj, Kushinagar
stories.summary: Flooding in Nepal has triggered an alert in Uttar Pradesh, with the impact expected to be felt in several districts. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has put Maharajganj and Kushinagar, both bordering Nepal, on high alert. All 36 gates of a barrage have been opened, causing the water level of the Gandak River to rise rapidly. DMs, SPs and other officials in both districts are on the ground. Sirens are being sounded to alert villagers, while police teams are urging people to stay away from the riverbanks and move valuables to safer places. Meanwhile, 19 districts in the state are already affected by flooding. In Badaun, the Ganga and Ramganga rivers have crossed the danger mark. A house was swept into the Ganga after being hit by erosion, while the Ramganga is flowing over the Badaun-Shahjahanpur highway. In Chandauli, the Musakhand and Latifshah dams are full, prompting officials to open their gates. The Sukwa-Dhukwan dam in Jhansi has overflowed, while a portion of the Tamolin Purwa embankment on the Sharda River in Lakhimpur has been breached. In Lalitpur, the Khedar River is flowing about three feet above a bridge, and the Sirsi bridge is also submerged. The water levels of the Ganga in Varanasi and the Yamuna in Prayagraj are currently stable, but all the ghats remain submerged. With cremation grounds underwater, last rites are being conducted on roads and rooftops. 31 districts under heavy rain warning today The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh today, Thursday, with heavy rain expected in 31 districts. Since Wednesday morning, intermittent rain has been reported in 35 cities, including Ghaziabad and Jhansi. Kanpur witnessed heavy rain from around 12:30 a.m. to 1 p.m., leaving roads and streets waterlogged. Lucknow also received heavy rain from around 4 p.m. See pictures of the rain and floods… Weather scientist Atul Kumar Singh said, A low-pressure area near the Bay of Bengal, along with active monsoon winds over Uttar Pradesh, could bring heavy to very heavy rainfall over the next 24 hours. The spell of rain is expected to continue for the next 2–3 days.

stories.title: Murder ransom accused freed in 24 hours:Convoy outside Lucknow jail, garlands and video shoot; 14 cases filed
stories.summary: Hazratganj police claimed to have solved the murder for ransom case involving Nadwa College Maulana Irfan Ahmad Rizvi in Lucknow on 21 August. ADCP Jitendra Dubey announced the details at a press conference, after which the accused were produced in court and sent to 14 day judicial custody. However, within 24 hours, three accused Mohammad Farhan Siddiqui, Sohel Ahmad Siddiqui and Aman Qureshi were granted bail. Police learned about their release after a video surfaced showing the trio being welcomed outside the jail. The three were garlanded, filmed and then left for home in a convoy. Police said more than 24 cases have been registered against them. According to police sources, the court did not seek a police report or case diary before granting bail, nor did the police receive any notice to present their side. The bail bonds were also allegedly not verified. Police have now started looking into the matter again. See 2 pictures of the accused leaving jail… Video made outside the jail All three accused walked out of jail just 24 hours after being sent into judicial custody. They recorded a video outside the jail and uploaded it to Facebook. The video shows them being garlanded as a song plays in the background: “How can I praise myself now... I fear the Almighty.” Police learned about their bail only after seeing the video. The incident has also raised questions about the speed with which bail was granted. ADCP Central Jitendra Dubey said, “It is a court order, so it is difficult to comment on it. The police are conducting their investigation.” Here is the timeline of the entire case… 21 August: The ACJM-2 court sent the accused to 14-day judicial custody. 21 August: The ACJM-3 court, acting as the CJM, granted bail to Aman Qureshi, Sohel Ahmed Siddiqui and Farhan Siddiqui. 23 August: All three accused were released from jail. 2 accused have more than 14 cases registered against them More than 14 cases involving serious charges have been registered against Farhan Siddiqui and Suhail Ahmad Siddiqui at various police stations in Lucknow. Despite this, both managed to secure bail and were released within 24 hours of being sent to jail. How the case was uncovered On August 18, Hazratganj police arrested Mohammad Shahid and Mohammad Zamir with a stolen Passion Plus motorcycle. During questioning, the two allegedly revealed that they had been offered ₹2 lakh to kill a person. They said they had also been given a pistol and shown a photograph of the intended target to identify him. Aman’s arrest unraveled the entire chain Based on information provided by Shahid and Zamir, police began searching for Aman Qureshi. Using surveillance, five police teams arrested him from Laxman Mela Park at around 2:15 a.m. on 21 August. During questioning, Aman allegedly told police that advocates Sohail Ahmed Siddiqui and Farhan Siddiqui, residents of Chowk, had asked him to arrange young men to kill Irfan. They had also given him Irfan’s photograph. He was instructed to use a separate mobile phone and SIM card to conceal his identity. According to police, preparations for the murder had been underway for about a month. Murder plot linked to ₹6 crore property dispute According to police, Bilal Hashmi, manager of Jamia Al Noor Al Salamia madrasa, had allegedly plotted Irfan Ahmed’s murder over a dispute involving property worth ₹6 crore. Two shooters were reportedly hired for ₹2 lakh. Police said the area was surveyed before the planned attack using a stolen motorcycle. Six accused have been arrested in the case, and police have recovered a pistol, five cartridges and the stolen motorcycle.

stories.title: Sisters tie rakhis on brother’s dead body:Came to Varanasi for Raksha Bandhan; ‘He gifted us every year, this year’s surprise is unbearable’
stories.summary: Three sisters who came to Varanasi to tie a rakhi on their brother’s wrist for Raksha Bandhan never imagined they would instead have to bid him a final farewell. They had already bought the rakhi, but their brother died after suffering an electric shock from a government water cooler. Three days before Raksha Bandhan, the sisters applied tilak to his body, tied the rakhi on his wrist and tearfully said goodbye. Dainik Bhaskar spoke to the grieving sisters about their loss. They said, “Every year, our brother would surprise us with a gift. This year, he gave us a surprise we cannot bear. We will never forget it for the rest of our lives. The festival that was meant to fill our home with happiness and laughter has been replaced by cries. My brother was a bodybuilder and had won a gold medal. He was running a gym until recently. Who will take care of our family now?” MLA Neelkanth Tiwari installed the water cooler Incident took place in Kali Mahal, Chetganj, where 50 year old Triloki Modanwal, alias Mantu, died of electrocution. He ran The Fitness King Gym in Ramkatora. Triloki was the third of four brothers and three sisters. All three sisters are married, while the brothers’ families had already divided their ancestral property. Triloki is survived by his wife, Rajkumari, two sons and two daughters. His elder daughter, Pratibha, is married. His elder son, 25, has completed his LLB and is scheduled to get married in November. His younger son is 17, while his younger daughter is 15. Triloki’s brother Vinod said that his brother had kept the gym closed on Tuesday due to heavy rain. He was at home in the morning when he went to the nearby intersection, as he usually did, to switch on the water cooler’s motor. The cooler was meant to fill with water so that people passing by could drink cold water throughout the day. However, Triloki suffered an electric shock and died. According to Vinod, the water cooler had been installed using the MLA fund of Dr. Neelkanth Tiwari, the South City MLA. Sister tell, Every year, brother would say, “Apply the tilak straight” Triloki’s younger sister Nivedita said, “I had come home for Raksha Bandhan. I had already bought a rakhi of my brother’s choice and was planning to order his favorite sweets too. He was very fond of Raksha Bandhan and would eagerly wait for us to tie the rakhi every year.” She said tearfully, “My brother would even joke with us about the tilak and rakhi. If the tilak was crooked, he would say, ‘Apply it straight, and tie the rakhi properly too.’ Every year, we brought him his favorite sweets and a rakhi. This time too, we had bought the rakhi in advance. But we never imagined we would have to tie it on his wrist like this.” Sister says, ‘It is unbearable that my brother betrayed us this time’ Triloki’s second sister, Soni, said tearfully, “Every Raksha Bandhan, my brother would give his sisters some new gift. For him, Raksha Bandhan was not just a festival but a day to celebrate with his sisters. If any of us could not come to tie him a rakhi, he would complain.” Soni said that this year too, they had expected to tie the rakhi on their brother’s wrist, apply tilak and receive a surprise gift from him, just as they did every year. “But this time, my brother betrayed us. The surprise he left us with is something our family cannot bear. We have paid a very heavy price for this gift.” Daughter says, ‘Dad said he would make laddoos when he came home’ Triloki’s younger daughter, Sonam, said, “My maternal aunt had a son 25 days ago. This time, she came with her son to tie a rakhi to my father. We had brought and kept all the ingredients needed to make Sothora laddoos for her. Dad said he would come home in the evening and make the laddoos, but he never came.” Sonam said her mother often remained unwell, so her father also took care of the household. “He helped with everything, from cooking to other household chores. Now that he is gone, who will take care of our home?” Daughter says, ‘My elder brother is getting married in November; why did Dad leave us?’ Triloki’s daughter Sonam said, “My elder brother’s wedding is scheduled for November. Dad had already started preparing for it, and the family had begun discussing the arrangements. He was excited about the wedding. But he left us without even seeing my brother get married.” Triloki had won the Mr. North India title His brother Gautam said Triloki had several achievements in bodybuilding. He had won the Mr. North India title and also secured a gold medal in a bodybuilding competition. He later stopped participating in competitions as he grew older. He was also invited to serve as a judge at bodybuilding competitions. Despite his achievements in sports, his family is now left with little more than assurances. Leaders have promised financial assistance and said a cheque would be provided, but the family says it does not want just financial aid. Keeping the children’s future in mind, they are demanding that at least one family member be given a job.

stories.title: Rakhis that grow into tulsi plants:Gorakhpur sisters to tie eco-friendly seed-paper rakhis to brothers on Raksha Bandhan
stories.summary: Eco-friendly Rakhis made from seed paper are being prepared in Gorakhpur this Raksha Bandhan. Embedded with Tulsi seeds, these rakhis can be planted in soil after the festival instead of being stored away or thrown out. With soil and moisture, the paper decomposes and the seeds sprout into Tulsi plants, turning a rakhi into a lasting symbol of sibling love and harmony. Dr. Aiman Tanveer, a professor in the Department of Biotechnology at DDU who makes these seed-paper rakhis, said, “We have prepared these eco-friendly rakhis using waste materials available at home. Tulsi seeds have been embedded in them.” After use, the rakhis can simply be buried in a flowerpot or any patch of soil. Within a few days, the paper begins to decompose, allowing the seeds to come into contact with soil and moisture and eventually sprout into plants. Started with Tulsi seeds Dr. Aiman said, “Although seed paper can be made with seeds of various plants, they have initially chosen Tulsi seeds for the rakhis because they felt they were the most suitable.” Tulsi holds special significance in Hinduism, making it a meaningful symbol of the love and harmony between brothers and sisters. The plant is also valued for its health benefits, adding to the usefulness of these eco-friendly rakhis. Takes 2–3 days to prepare She explained that making the rakhis involves several steps. First, waste paper such as invitation cards, old newspapers and other discarded paper is torn into small pieces and soaked in warm water for a few hours or overnight. The water is then drained, and the paper is turned into pulp. Cornflour, a binding agent and seeds are added and mixed thoroughly. The mixture is then shaped into small rakhi pieces. Once dry, they are colored and threaded to complete the rakhis. The entire process takes around 2–3 days. Priced at ₹50 He said the seed-paper rakhi is currently priced at ₹50. Around 15–20 rakhis have been sold so far. Considering this is their first attempt, the response has been encouraging. Plants take the same time to grow as regular seeds He said plants grown from these seed-paper rakhis will take roughly the same time to grow as those grown from regular seeds. To plant the rakhi, it simply needs to be pressed into the soil. Seed-paper rakhi is chemical-free Dr. Aiman said the rakhi is completely chemical-free. A special enzyme is used to protect the embedded seeds from damage, while the material does not harm the soil. According to him, the initiative can help reduce waste, protect the environment and promote sustainable practices.

stories.title: Over 100 leopards terrorise Moradabad:3 women killed, 20 mauled in 22 days; DFO says harder to capture than tigers
stories.summary: Leopard movement is not unusual in Moradabad’s villages bordering the buffer zone of Jim Corbett. But the fear gripping the area for the past 22 days is unprecedented. In this period, leopard attacks have killed three women and injured more than 20 farmers, leaving nearly one lakh people across around 50 villages bordering Uttarakhand living in fear. Announcements are being made continuously from temples and mosques, urging farmers not to venture into their fields. Fear has become so intense that many parents have stopped sending their children to school. A forest officer estimates that more than 100 leopards are present in the district. Around 50 forest officials and experts are camping in the affected areas, while 29 cages have been installed at different locations. So far, 11 leopards have been captured, and thermal drones are being used to track their movement. What is life like in these villages, located about 50 km from the district headquarters, where people are now afraid to step outside? What do the villagers have to say? Read the full report— Changed leopard behavior leaves forest experts puzzled One thing is common in the leopard attacks reported in Moradabad over the past 22 days: the animals have been targeting people’s necks, often without any apparent provocation. Experts say such behavior is unusual for leopards. Moradabad Divisional Forest Officer (DFO) Dr. Vinay Kumar Pandey said, “With the help of experts, we are trying to understand the leopards’ behavior. For now, it appears they attack when they see a person approaching them. From the leopard’s perspective, this could also be an act of self-defense.” Leopards spotted roaming near city and highways The Forest Department has captured 11 leopards, including a cub, in Moradabad over the past 20 days. Despite this, leopard attacks continue to be reported almost every day, indicating that a large number of leopards are still roaming the district’s forests. Some have even been spotted near the city and along highways. Forest officials estimate that around 100 leopards could be present in the district. DFO says, ‘This is a traditional leopard habitat’ Moradabad DFO Dr. Vinay Kumar Pandey says leopards have historically lived in this area bordering Uttarakhand. The region once had vast grasslands and dense forests, where farmers rarely ventured. Citing the Moradabad Gazetteer, he says the area has traditionally been a leopard habitat. The presence of leopards here is therefore not new. However, the grasslands have now been replaced by sugarcane fields, providing leopards with cover to move around. The DFO says the area has also not experienced flooding this year because of low rainfall. In previous years, flooding would keep people out of sugarcane fields and forests during this period, resulting in fewer encounters and leopard attacks. This year, with no flooding, farmers have continued to move around their fields, increasing the chances of encounters with leopards. Tigers easier to capture, leopards harder to track Forest experts say that once a tiger is located, tracking and capturing it is relatively easier. Leopards, however, are much harder to locate because of their exceptional ability to hide. They can squeeze themselves behind even the smallest object and remain almost completely undetectable. A leopard can flatten its body against the ground and stay motionless. Even in an open field, it can press itself behind a small bush and remain invisible despite being just a few feet away. Experts say leopards can also survive for several days without drinking water while remaining in hiding. Even in urban areas, a leopard crouching behind a small roadside stone or a piece of scrap can be difficult to distinguish from its surroundings. By keeping its head and neck close to the ground, it can remain virtually undetected. Leopard sightings spread beyond 50 villages Leopard attacks have primarily sparked fear across 50 villages in Moradabad bordering Uttarakhand. However, the animals’ range is now gradually expanding. After being spotted in the Thakurdwara and Dilarpur areas, leopards have now also been seen in Kanth and Chhajlet. A leopard was also spotted near the TMU underpass along the Delhi-Lucknow National Highway, in the area adjoining Moradabad. Mithilesh said, “The livelihood of us villagers depends on farming and animal husbandry. That is why we are forced to risk our lives even to collect fodder and go to our fields. We have requested the Forest Department to capture the leopard as soon as possible and free the village from this atmosphere of fear.” Manisha said, “The Forest Department is not placing bait inside the cages, so leopards come close but do not enter them. Forest Department staff are also not visiting the site to monitor the situation. Villagers are having to arrange and keep watch on the cages themselves. We all have just one request, the leopards should be captured as soon as possible.”

stories.title: Bank manager wife killed in Lucknow:SBI officer husband beats her at office gate, shoots her in forehead when employees rush over
stories.summary: Dainik Bhaskar has obtained exclusive CCTV footage of the murder of Divya Mishra, a relationship manager at ICICI Bank in Lucknow. In the footage, Divya is seen entering the bank. Her husband, Manas Bajpai, stops her at the gate. An argument ensues between them. Then Manas starts beating Divya. Seeing the assault, the bank guards and employees rushed to save Divya. Meanwhile, Manas shot Divya in the forehead. As soon as the shot was fired, the guards and employees backed away. After this, Manas ran towards his house. He reached his house, 2 km away, where he also murdered his sister Sheeba and finally shot himself. See 2 pictures Shot amidst the crowd Most of the CCTV cameras installed in the bank are angled inwards. One CCTV camera is angled outwards. The incident has been captured in it. It is visible that vehicles are coming and going outside the bank. There is a crowd on the road. Manas commits the crime without caring about any of this. According to CCTV, Divya is entering the bank at 12:20 PM on Thursday. Manas stops her outside the bank and beats her. Within 1 minute, he shoots her and flees. After he leaves, the bank guards and other employees reach Divya. After killing his wife, he killed his sister and then committed suicide. After killing Divya, Manas reaches his house in Husadiya around 12:30 PM. According to eyewitnesses, Manas was drenched in sweat. After going inside, he first closes the room door. Then he plays Hanuman Chalisa loudly on the TV. After this, he shoots and kills his sister Sheeba. Then he shoots himself and commits suicide.

stories.title: 5-year-old girl falls into 50-ft-deep well:Cop descends with oxygen cylinder tied to his leg; rescues her on fourth attempt
stories.summary: A 5-year-old girl fell into a 50-foot-deep well in Farrukhabad. The girl was clearly visible when looking down from above. But due to the fear of poisonous gas, no one was able to gather the courage to go down. Some villagers tried to descend with the help of a rope. But they came back up due to suffocation. Constable Manoj tried to descend into the well three times, but he also came out due to suffocation. The fourth time, he descended with an oxygen cylinder tied to his leg and brought the girl out. The rescue operation lasted 3 hours. The incident took place on Thursday at 2 PM in the Kaimganj area. First, see 2 pictures Now the full incident in detail Pawan Kumar, a resident of Jahanpur village, lives with his family. This includes his wife Sapna, elder daughter Ananya, second daughter Lavanya, and youngest daughter Saumya (5), while his younger son is Sivay. Saumya is the third among her four siblings. Her father Pawan works in a private company in Delhi. Elder daughter Ananya had gone to the primary school located in Rasidabad Ballabh with her younger sister Saumya to study. After school was dismissed, both sisters were returning home. During this time, there was a swing on a platform near Dinesh's house in the village. After swinging for some time, both sisters reached the platform. After this, Saumya jumped onto the well's slab. The slab suddenly broke, and the child fell into the approximately 50-foot deep well. Hearing her sister Ananya's screams, nearby villagers arrived at the spot. Soon, a large crowd gathered near the well. Villagers tried to pull the child out, but the rescue was difficult because the well was very old and narrow. Officials arrived at the scene Upon receiving information about the accident, SDM Abhishek Verma, Tehsildar Harshit Singh, CO Rajesh Kumar Dwivedi, and Inspector Crime B. Yadav reached the spot with police force. The fire brigade and CHC health team were also called. A rescue operation was launched to pull the child out in the presence of officials. Due to the narrowness of the well, Pranshu, in charge of the fire brigade team, also tried to go inside, but was unsuccessful. When called from above, the child asked for water Soumya's mother, Sapna, who arrived at the scene, was distraught and crying. During the rescue operation, hearing the child's voice somewhat eased the worries of those present at the scene. When called from above, Soumya asked for water from inside. After this, the policemen sent water down twice using a kamandal (a water pot) with the help of a rope. The child drank the water. This further strengthened the hope of her being safe. After this, Constable Manoj Kumar, stationed at the police station, attempted to descend into the well. He descended a short distance three times and came back up. After this, Manoj descended into the well with an oxygen cylinder for safety and reached the child. After much effort, he safely brought Soumya out after about three hours. When constable Manoj brought the girl out of the well, the policemen, officers, and villagers present at the scene breathed a sigh of relief. The girl was immediately taken to the CHC by ambulance. Doctors sent her to Lohia Hospital after examination At the CHC, Medical Superintendent Dr. Vipin Kumar and Dr. Amresh Kumar examined the student. According to the doctors, the girl's condition is currently stable. She was also given oxygen. For better treatment and monitoring, the student was referred to Lohia Hospital. Scuffle between a soldier and a constable while dispersing the crowd Upon receiving information about the girl's rescue, a large number of villagers had gathered at the spot. Policemen were repeatedly trying to move people away from around the well so that the rescue team would not face any difficulty in working. During this, a soldier from the village clashed with a constable. A scuffle broke out between the two. Other policemen present there intervened, separated them, and calmed the situation. After the child was safely brought out, the family members and villagers breathed a sigh of relief. Policeman Manoj Kumar played an important role in this rescue operation, which lasted for about three hours. His courage in descending into the well and bringing the child out was praised by the people present at the spot. SDM Abhishek Verma said that after a three-hour rescue operation, the child has been safely pulled out of the well. She has been sent to Lohia Hospital for better treatment. He informed that the child opened her eyes and also conversed after coming out of the well.

stories.summary: To further strengthen law and order in UP, 23 new IPS officers have been given regular postings. These include 12 officers from the 2023 batch and 11 from the 2024 batch. The DGP office issued the posting orders for the officers on Thursday evening around 6 PM. All officers have recently returned after completing their training from the Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel National Police Academy (NPA) in Hyderabad. After training, they have been posted as Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) and Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) in various districts and police commissionerates of the state. IPS Dinesh Godara has been sent to Ayodhya. He secured the 150th rank in the UPSC Civil Services Examination 2022. He is originally from Nagrasar village in Bikaner district of Rajasthan. Dinesh completed his B.Tech (Chemical Science and Technology) degree from IIT Guwahati. After engineering, he received a job offer of 18 lakh rupees annually from a multinational company, which he left to prepare for administrative services. Training was ongoing in Hyderabad All these young IPS officers were undergoing their training at NPA (NPA) in Hyderabad from June 22 to August 21. As soon as the training was completed, DGP Headquarters issued orders for them to enter the field. Their first deployment in districts and commissionerates will further sharpen policing. -

stories.title: BJP MLA says she was stopped from praying at temple:Claims she was insulted for being a Pasi; wife of former Union minister Kaushal
stories.summary: Allegations of caste-based discrimination have surfaced during a foundation stone laying ceremony at the Sheetala Temple in Kakori, Lucknow, on Wednesday(19 Aug). Local MLA Jaydevi Kaushal alleged, “The temple administration did not treat her with due respect and excluded her from the worship rituals.” The MLA had attended the ceremony held for the renovation of the temple, for which she claims to have helped secure funds from the Tourism Department. According to her, despite her efforts, she was not included in the puja during the foundation stone laying and ground breaking ceremony and was instead asked to stand aside. She said, “She was hurt by the treatment.” MLA said- I got the money sanctioned for the temple MLA Jaydevi Kaushal said, “I got ₹1 crore sanctioned for the renovation of the Sheetala Devi temple. When I went there to perform the puja, I was treated with hostility and felt insulted. I am a two-time MLA and had made repeated efforts to get funds sanctioned for this very temple. Yet, when the opportunity came to perform the puja, I was not allowed to participate. I consider this an insult." She added, “I believe I was stopped from performing the puja because of caste discrimination, as I belong to the Pasi community. At the very least, they could have allowed me to participate in some way, especially since I am the local MLA.” Continuing, "I worked to get the funds sanctioned for the temple’s renovation, yet I was not even allowed to light an incense stick. I will certainly raise the issue of the insult meted out to me.” When asked about her son’s social media post regarding the incident, the MLA said, “We are not aware of it. We went there for the programme and then had to leave for another engagement.” MLA’s son and husband post about the incident Following the MLA’s allegations, her son Vikas Kishore posted about the incident on social media. He stated, “The puja was being conducted by priest Shailendra Bajpai, while the mantras were being recited by temple manager Ramakant Gupta.” The foundation stone laying and groundbreaking ceremony was attended by MLA Jaydevi Kaushal, Nagar Panchayat President Rohit Sahu, BJP District Office Secretary, Mandal President Vipin Rajput, Councillor Representative Lavkush Yadav, temple manager Ramakant Gupta, priest Shailendra Bajpai and several others. ‘There was no such intention, she did not perform the puja herself’ Temple manager Ramakant Gupta, “There was no such intention or sentiment, the MLA herself chose not to perform the puja. Even the event was not large enough to require chairs, and there was limited space at the temple." When the MLA was asked to break the coconut and offer flowers, she herself said, “You perform the puja; we have to leave for another programme.” Gupta said, “The coconut and flowers were then offered and the puja was performed for the temple’s renovation work.” He added, "When the MLA was leaving, prasad was also placed in her car." The temple manager denied the MLA’s allegations of caste discrimination, saying there has never been any restriction on people from any caste or community at the temple. He also expressed gratitude to the MLA for getting funds sanctioned for the temple’s renovation. Video of MLA being offered coconut also surfaces Following the incident, an 8-second video has surfaced showing the priest offering a coconut to MLA Jaydevi Kaushal. In the video, the priest can be heard saying, “Please take it, MLA ji, touch it.” A woman’s voice then responds, “No, we have already touched it. You perform the puja.” People had gathered to protest Upon receiving information about this incident, Azad Samaj Party's district president Ajay Bharti reached Sheetla Temple with his workers and staged a protest. As soon as the information was received, Kakori Inspector Satish Rathore reached the spot with police force and pacified the protesters by counseling them.

stories.title: Head constable suspended for puncturing bike with needle:Youth carried 2 passengers; locals call it police high-handedness
stories.summary: A head constable was suspended in Vrindavan on Thursday (20 Aug) for allegedly puncturing a motorcycle tyre with an awl after stopping a young man who was riding with two pillion riders. The action came after a video of the incident surfaced online, prompting allegations of police high-handedness, following which an inquiry was ordered and the constable was suspended. The young man was travelling with two pillion riders when the head constable stopped him on the road. Instead of issuing a challan, the policeman allegedly pierced the front tyre with an awl three times. During the incident, the biker repeatedly pleaded with the policeman to let him go, but his request was allegedly ignored. A video of the incident surfaced online, following which social media users accused the police of high-handedness. SSP Shlok Kumar assigned the inquiry to Sadar Circle Officer Varun Mishra. He submitted his inquiry report to the SSP in the morning, following which the SSP suspended Head Constable Sunil Kumar Yadav. See the full incident in 3 pictures… Read the details… The incident took place on August 16. Mathura-Vrindavan was crowded due to Hariyali Teej, Independence Day and the weekend. Police personnel had been deployed in the Vrindavan Kotwali area to manage the crowds. During this time, three people arrived on a motorcycle near the Ramanreti police post. Head Constable Sunil Kumar Yadav stopped the rider. The youth explained why he was carrying two pillion riders on the motorcycle and requested to be let off. However, Sunil allegedly ignored his request. The head constable then began piercing the motorcycle's front tyre with an awl. Claim that the tyre was pierced three times In the video, Head Constable Sunil Yadav can be seen repeatedly piercing the tyre with an awl. It is claimed that he pierced the front tyre three times, causing it to go flat. Local residents said motorcycle riders in Vrindavan carry passengers around for sightseeing. They also alleged that arbitrary amounts are collected from devotees. It could not be confirmed whether the people travelling on the motorcycle were locals or from outside the area. Sadar CO Varun Mishra said Head Constable Sunil Kumar Yadav, posted at Vrindavan police station, was found guilty during the inquiry. The inquiry report has been sent to senior officers. He said, "Sunil Kumar Yadav has been suspended. Further departmental action is being taken in the matter." Social media users ask, is this how traffic enforcement is carried out? Social media users have questioned the action by Vrindavan police. They said traffic violations are normally dealt with through a challan or action as prescribed under the rules and questioned whether puncturing a tyre in this manner was justified. One user took a dig at the police in an X post, writing: UP Police has developed a new technology to take action against those who do not follow traffic rules. Police personnel can use a sharp instrument to pierce a bike tyre as many times as they want. Police are testing it in Vrindavan, Mathura.

stories.title: MSc student found dead in lover’s bathroom:Victim had been missing for 3 days in Varanasi after leaving home for college
stories.summary: The body of an MSC student, missing for 3 days in Varanasi, was found on Thursday afternoon at 1:30 PM in her lover's bathroom. Searching for her daughter, the mother reached her lover's room. As soon as she opened the gate, a strong foul smell emanated. Inside, in the bathroom, she found her daughter's decomposed body. The student's mother immediately informed the police. The student's mother told the police that on August 17, her daughter went to college but did not return. After much searching, when nothing was found, a complaint was lodged at the police station. When the police put the student's mobile on surveillance, the location was found near Malviya Inter College in Bachhaon. When the police reached the spot, the room's gate did not open. On Friday morning, the student's mother reached her lover's maternal grandparents' house. From there, she got the key to the room. After this, when she reached the location again, the incident was discovered. Police, who arrived on receiving the information, have sent the student's body for post-mortem. Meanwhile, the student's lover is absconding. The incident is from the Rohania area. 3 pictures related to the incident Now the full incident in detail The student was the only daughter of her parents The student has been identified as Shreya Upadhyay, daughter of Sunil Upadhyay. Sunil, a resident of Marui-Jamuni village in Rajatalab, runs a cloth shop in Chandapur, about 4 km from his home. Shreya was his only daughter. She was studying in MSC First Year at Jagatpur PG College. According to the police, Shreya's lover Vivek Chaubey, a resident of Niyar village in Cholapur, has his maternal grandparents' home in Jamuni village. Vivek has two maternal uncles. The elder maternal uncle lives in Niyar and the younger maternal uncle lives in Sikhad village of Mirzapur. Vivek used to visit Niyar frequently. During this time, he met Shreya. Gradually, friendship developed between them, which then turned into a love affair. After this, they started meeting frequently. Vivek mostly lived in a rented room in Bachhanv. Room Key Found in Lover Vivek's Bag On August 20, Shreya's mother and her cousin brother reached Vivek's uncle's house in Sikhad village, Mirzapur. When they inquired about Vivek there, they found out he was missing. During this time, a bag belonging to Vivek was found there, which contained his room key. Shreya's mother took the room key and reached Bachchhav. As soon as she put the key in the lock, the door opened. A strong foul smell was coming from the room. When they went inside, they saw Shreya's dead body lying in the bathroom. After this, they immediately informed the police. ACP Alok Priyadarshi said- The student's body has been taken into custody and sent for post-mortem. A case has been registered based on the complaint of the family members. The girl's lover is being searched for.

stories.title: Champat Rai claims Ram Mandir panel chief acted arbitrarily:Nripendra Misra ignored advice and chose his own people
stories.summary: After resigning from the Ayodhya Ram Temple Trust, Champat Rai on Thursday released a second letter, spanning 9 pages. In it, he made several claims regarding the role of Nripendra Misra, the chairman of the temple construction committee and a former IAS officer. Champat Rai said, the trust formed for the construction of the Ram Temple had 15 trustees, and Nripendra Misra was made the chairman of the construction committee. At Misra's suggestion, Larsen Toubro (LT) was given the responsibility for temple construction. Additionally, the selection of a Noida-based Design Associate firm for work related to building design and construction was also done by Nripendra Misra. The firm's head has been identified as Jai Kaktikar. Champat Rai alleged that Nripendra Misra included people of his choice in the temple construction committee. He claimed that some of these individuals visited Ayodhya only once or twice during the six-year period. However, former NBCC Chairman Anoop Mittal consistently attended construction committee meetings with Nripendra Misra. Champat Rai claimed in his statement that decisions related to the temple's construction were made in committee meetings, but in many cases, changes were made later, and Nripendra Misra's decisions were prioritised. According to him, Nripendra Misra's preferences were also given prominence in the selection of people and companies involved in the construction. He also claimed that in many cases, suggestions or decisions of other committee members were not given due importance. Champat Rai resigned from the post of General Secretary on June 26 after the case of offering theft came to light. The resignation was accepted at the trust meeting on July 6. On the same day, Champat Rai issued a letter making serious allegations against trustee Anil Mishra. Now read the main points of the letter sequentially- The struggle to acquire the temple land began after 1528 The letter stated that after the Ram Janmabhoomi temple was demolished by Babur's armies in 1528, the struggle to acquire the temple land continued on behalf of the saints of Ayodhya, local kings-princely states, and the householder society. This struggle ended after the local community occupied the site in 1949. Between 1950 and 1989, four lawsuits were filed in local courts. These lawsuits were fought by the petitioners at their own level. Later, a three-member bench of the Lucknow Bench of the Allahabad High Court heard the case. During the hearing, which lasted for about 15 years, all three judges independently wrote their judgments, and the total judgment was about 8,500 pages long. Attempt at mediation in 2019, Supreme Court hearing lasted 40 days The Supreme Court attempted to resolve the dispute through dialogue. For this, a three-member mediation committee was formed, consisting of retired judge FMI Kalifulla, senior advocate Sriram Panchu, and spiritual guru Sri Sri Ravi Shankar. Several rounds of meetings were held from March to July 2019, but no solution could be found. Subsequently, from August 6, 2019, a five-member Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court began regular hearings. During the hearing, which lasted for about 40 days, arguments from the lawyers of the parties were heard for approximately 175 hours. On November 9, 2019, the Supreme Court delivered a unanimous verdict, after which the path for the construction of the Ram Temple was cleared. Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust formed on the instructions of the Supreme Court Following the instructions of the Supreme Court, the central government formed an independent trust named Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra. A total of 15 trustees were arranged in it. One seat was reserved for Nirmohi Akhara and one for Scheduled Caste/Tribe representation. Additionally, the District Magistrate of Ayodhya, and IAS officers as representatives of the Uttar Pradesh government and the central government, were made ex-officio trustees. A senior administrative officer was given the responsibility for the management of the temple construction committee and temple-related works. Currently, Nripendra Misra is handling this responsibility. Selection of LT based on Ashok Singhal's suggestions The suggestions related to temple construction by the late Vishwa Hindu Parishad leader Ashok Singhal were conveyed to Nripendra Misra. Based on these suggestions, Larsen Toubro (LT) was selected for the temple construction. Additionally, considering the need for an equivalent institution for construction monitoring and project advice, Tata Consulting Engineers (TCE) was chosen as the Project Management Consultant. The Noida-based firm Design Associate and its head, Jai Kaktikar, were given the responsibility for designing other buildings in the temple complex. International Ramkatha Museum to open to the public by December 2027 Along with the temple construction, the Trust plans to develop a museum. Ayodhya's International Ramkatha Museum is the property of the Uttar Pradesh government. Nripendra Mishra felt that running two separate museums in a small city would not be practical. Following this, an agreement was reached between the Uttar Pradesh government and Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra, and the museum building was given to the Trust on a 30-year lease. The museum will have 20 galleries. The IIT Madras team has arrived in Ayodhya and started work on the museum. The museum will be opened to the general public by December 2027. The 70-acre complex of the birthplace has been divided into two parts Mention of arrangements related to darshan (viewing) at Ram Temple

stories.title: 5-foot iron rod driven into cousin’s ear, killing him:Sambhal dispute over children’s fight; doctor says 4 inches entered brain bone
stories.summary: A young man was killed in Sambhal after his cousin allegedly attacked him with a 5-foot-long iron rod, driving it through his ear. The rod penetrated around 4 inches and became lodged in his skull. Doctors removed the rod during an operation, but around four hours later, the man's condition deteriorated. He was referred to Delhi but died on the way at around 2.30am on Wednesday. The incident took place in the Rajpura police station area, around 30km from the district headquarters. The victim, Kanhaiya, underwent surgery at Acharya Hospital in Bulandshahr. Doctors said the rod fractured his skull and caused a brain injury, while a blood clot also developed. According to police, the incident followed an argument between two cousins over a dispute involving their children. See photos- Know the full story- Kanhaiya and Badan Singh, residents of Chaupur Danda village under Rajpura police station, are cousins and neighbours. Their houses face each other, with a narrow path of around 4 to 5 feet between them. A few days earlier, their families had argued over a dispute involving their children. On Tuesday evening, the two sides confronted each other again over the same issue. The argument escalated, with both sides allegedly throwing bricks and stones. During the clash, a young man from Badan Singh's family arrived carrying an iron rod. He initially tried to attack Kanhaiya with it before allegedly driving the rod into his ear. Kanhaiya collapsed with serious injuries, while the accused fled. His family took him to the Gunnaur Community Health Centre, where he received first aid before doctors referred him to Aligarh Medical College. Two-hour operation carried out in Bulandshahr The family took Kanhaiya to Aligarh late on Tuesday night. As his condition failed to improve, they brought him to Acharya Hospital in Bulandshahr. Doctors found that the rod had penetrated around 4 inches through his ear and become lodged in the skull bone. They said pulling it out directly could have proved fatal. The protruding section was therefore first cut off using a grinder, after which doctors removed the portion lodged inside during an operation lasting around two hours. Doctor: Rod fractured skull and caused brain injury Dr Ashish Acharya of Acharya Hospital said Kanhaiya was in an extremely critical condition when he arrived. According to the doctor, the rod entered through the ear, travelled around 4 inches into the head and became embedded in the skull bone. It fractured the bone and caused a brain injury. He said there was an immediate risk of death if the rod had been pulled out directly. It was therefore cut first and then removed surgically. Kanhaiya's condition initially improved after the operation, but deteriorated again later in the evening due to blood clotting in the brain and the fractured bone. He was referred to Delhi but died on the way. Three live videos of clash emerge Three live videos related to the dispute between the two sides have also surfaced. Police are examining these videos along with other evidence as part of the investigation. The footage is being used to establish the roles of both sides during the assault and stone-pelting. One accused arrested, two others being sought Rajpura police station in-charge Sandeep Chaudhary said- Kanhaiya's mother, Kamlesh, had lodged an FIR against Badan Singh, Brijpal and Lakshmi for assault. After Kanhaiya's death, a murder charge was added to the case. Badan Singh, son of Leeladhar, has been arrested. Two other accused are being searched for. Kanhaiya supported family through farming and labour Kanhaiya worked in farming and daily-wage labour to support his family. His wife is Kranti Devi. They have a 7-year-old daughter, Chanchal, and a 4-year-old son, Vivek. Following Kanhaiya's death, his wife, children and other family members are devastated and have been crying inconsolably.

stories.title: Parents sentenced to life imprisonment in Ayushi Yadav murder case:Daughter killed at home after love marriage, body dumped in suitcase in Mathura
stories.summary: In the high-profile Ayushi Yadav murder case in Mathura, her parents have been sentenced to life imprisonment. The Mathura Court delivered its verdict on Wednesday, four years after the murder. In court, Ayushi's father Nitesh Yadav said in his defence that he had killed his daughter but that his wife was not at fault. He then fell silent. Her mother, Brajwala, stood with her head bowed. While pronouncing the sentence, the judge said the murder of a daughter was an “extremely cruel and heinous” crime and that there was no justification for taking a lenient approach towards the convicts. The judge also observed that failing to punish the guilty would send the wrong message to society. Ayushi, 22, was shot dead by her father with a revolver at their home in Delhi four years ago. The alleged reason was that she had secretly married a young man from Rajasthan. After the murder, her father placed her body in a red suitcase and dumped it near the Yamuna Expressway in Mathura, around 150km from Delhi. Her mother, Brajwala, was also involved in the disposal of the body. After it was discovered, police began investigating the case and brought Brajwala and Ayushi's brother Ayush to Mathura, where they identified the body. Police subsequently arrested both parents. See photos- Government lawyer Mukesh Goswami said- After completing the investigation, police filed a charge sheet against Nitesh Yadav and Brajwala. During the hearing, the prosecution presented witness statements and other evidence before the court. Based on the evidence, the court found both guilty and pronounced the sentence. Nitesh Yadav was fined ₹7,000, while Brajwala was fined ₹6,000. Studying BCA and had married a man from another caste Ayushi was a resident of Badarpur, Delhi, and was studying for a BCA at Global College. She had cleared the NEET exam but did not participate in counselling. Her parents tried to persuade her to attend counselling, but she refused. Ayushi had married Chhatrapal Rajput, a resident of Bharatpur, Rajasthan, at an Arya Samaj temple. Her parents opposed the marriage. After the wedding, Ayushi never went to her husband's home and continued living with her parents. During interrogation, her father reportedly said that Ayushi had begun opposing everything the family told her to do. On the afternoon of November 17, 2022, she had an argument with her mother. When Nitesh learned about it, he tried to reason with her. When she did not listen, he shot her with his licensed revolver in a fit of rage. Ayushi died at the scene. Father bought polythene and packed body into suitcase After killing Ayushi, her father bought polythene from a shop near their home. That afternoon, he wrapped her body and placed it inside a suitcase. At around 3am, he put the suitcase in the car. At 5am on November 18, they reached a deserted spot near the Yamuna Expressway in Mathura, around 150km away. They dumped the suitcase there and returned towards Delhi at around 7am. The father drove the car, while the mother sat in the front passenger seat. Mother and brother identified body and broke down At around 2pm, a passer-by spotted the body and informed police. When officers opened the suitcase, they found the body of a young woman. She was wearing black shorts and a grey half-sleeved T-shirt bearing the words 'Lady Days'. She had long black hair, while a kalawa (sacred thread) and a black thread were tied around her left wrist. Several injury marks were visible on her body. Police formed 14 teams involving 100 personnel to establish the woman's identity. They examined footage from around 300 CCTV cameras, covering the area from the crime scene to the toll plaza, but were initially unable to identify her. Police then activated their network of informers. An informer subsequently reported that a girl from Morband, Badarpur, had been missing for two days. A police team reached the girl's home and brought her mother and brother to the Mathura post-mortem house. Both identified the body as Ayushi's. After identifying her, the mother and brother embraced each other and broke down in tears.

stories.title: Gen Alpha students protest in Lucknow:No buckets for bathing in hostel; Physics and Maths teachers on leave since 6 months
stories.summary: Gen-Alpha students studying at Jai Prakash Narayan Sarvodaya Vidyalaya in Para, Lucknow, have taken to the streets to raise concerns about problems at the school and hostel. After the boys protested on August 14, girl students scaled the school boundary on August 17, walked around 3km through the rain and blocked the road. Their concerns go beyond the absence of Physics and Maths teachers. They include basic hostel facilities such as buckets for bathing, as well as issues related to food, electricity, medical treatment and the timely resolution of complaints. A Dainik Bhaskar team visited the school and spoke to students and their guardians. Several concerns about the school's arrangements emerged during the interaction. Students said even minor problems are not resolved promptly, while some guardians claimed that their children frequently fall ill. Around 300 students from Classes 6 to 12 study and live at the school. The two-day protests have therefore raised questions not only about education but also about hostel and healthcare facilities. Bhaskar tried to inspect the arrangements, but the administration did not allow photographs or videos to be taken inside the campus. Read full report- See 3 pictures of the protest ‘Our concerns are not heard on time’ Anamika, a student at the school, said they often have to wait a long time even when dealing with minor problems. Complaints do not receive an immediate response, she said. Several students also expressed dissatisfaction with the behaviour of some teachers. According to them, teachers do not always respond properly to their concerns, while reaching the responsible authorities can also be difficult. The students said their frustration increased because their complaints remained unresolved for extended periods. Students also raise concerns about food Improving the quality of hostel food was one of the students' major demands during the protest. Shivani, a student, said there are frequent problems with the food. Some parents outside the school, speaking on condition of anonymity, also claimed that their children repeatedly fall ill. They said some children become ill within 15 to 20 days. However, the exact reason has not been established. Whether the illnesses are linked to water, food, hostel cleanliness or living conditions can only be determined through an investigation. Sick children taken outside for treatment and then returned According to family members, when a child falls ill, the school informs the family. The child is then taken outside the school for treatment and returned to the campus afterwards. This raises several questions: if children are repeatedly falling ill, what investigation has the school conducted to establish the cause? When was the water tested? Were food samples collected? Is a record of the children's medical history being maintained? The answers to these questions are currently unclear. No Physics or Maths teachers Around 300 students from Classes 6 to 12 study at the school. The shortage of teachers is one of their biggest concerns, particularly the absence of Physics and Maths teachers. Questions have also been raised over the overall staffing position: how many teachers are sanctioned for the school, how many are currently working, and how many posts are vacant? If a teacher is on extended leave, another issue is why an alternative teaching arrangement has not been made. Principal Secretary Anurag Yadav said— I have personally spoken to all the children. The Physics teacher is on maternity leave, while the Maths teacher is currently on leave. This may have happened today because of a lack of communication with the school administration. The children may have seen students from the neighbouring school doing this and thought, ‘We should do it too.’ The children are very good. Students also unhappy with some teachers The students' complaints are not limited to the number of teachers. Some also said they were unhappy with the behaviour of certain teachers and felt their concerns were not properly heard. The first protest took place on August 14, when boys raised the issue of the teacher shortage. Three days later, on August 17, the girl students also came out of the school to protest over their demands. School denies permission for photographs and videos The Dainik Bhaskar team attempted to inspect the school's facilities, but the administration refused permission to take photographs or videos inside the premises. As a result, photographs of the hostel, kitchen, bathrooms, water facilities and other arrangements could not be obtained. The complaints raised by the students and parents therefore require the department to conduct its own detailed inspection of these facilities to establish the actual situation.

stories.title: Class 10 student allegedly murdered, body hidden:Angry crowd protests on road for 6 hours in Gorakhpur; FIR against 2 friends
stories.summary: A huge uproar erupted in Pathra on Wednesday after 10th-grade student Prince Kumar (16), who went to bathe in the Rapti river in Gorakhpur, went missing. The student's family has accused two friends who went with him of murdering him and throwing his body into the river to hide it. The search for the student in the Rapti river is ongoing with the help of divers. Meanwhile, angry people blocked the main road on Wednesday at 3 PM. The commotion continued for about 6 hours, during which a long queue of vehicles formed. Police from several stations, including SDM Sadar and CO Cantt, reached the spot. After the officials intervened and explained, the blockade ended around 9 PM. Know the full story Prince, son of Satyapal Nishad, a resident of Semra Devi Prasad Chhotka Pathra in Ramgarhtal area, was studying in class 10 at MG Inter College. On Tuesday afternoon, he returned home after school. Around 3:30 PM, two of his friends, residents of Chakra Doyam in Rajghat area, arrived at his home on a scooter. Both took Prince with them towards the Rapti river. According to the friends, Prince drowned in deep water while bathing in the river. After that, both of them took his clothes and mobile phone and returned home, informing the family about the incident. Old dispute came to light Police started searching the river with the help of SDRF, but no trace of the student was found until Wednesday night. His slippers were found near the river bank, and clothes and a mobile phone were recovered from Amrutani. The family says that there was a dispute between Prince and the two friends about three months ago. A dispute also came to light three days ago and on the day of the incident. Based on this, the family expressed suspicion of murder. SP City Nimish Patil said, An FIR has been registered against both accused on the complaint of the student's mother, Subhavati Devi. SDRF and police teams are searching for the student in the river. This matter is being investigated thoroughly.

stories.title: PAC deployed again in Lucknow to seize buffaloes:Force from 3 police stations also deployed; civic body seized 200+ buffaloes a day ago
stories.summary: The Lucknow Municipal Corporation has once again launched a crackdown on illegally operated dairies in the Para area. On Thursday morning, the civic body’s cattle-catching team reached Pink City near Mohan Road along with police personnel from three police stations and one company of PAC. Personnel wearing helmets, carrying lathis and dressed in bulletproof jackets surrounded the dairies, after which the municipal team began impounding buffaloes. 200+ buffaloes seized earlier The Municipal Corporation had carried out a similar operation on Tuesday, when more than 200 buffaloes were seized and sent to the Kanji House in Thakurganj. The latest action follows an attack on the enforcement team on August 16. Operators of illegal dairies allegedly attacked the team with bricks, stones and thick iron chains used for tying buffaloes. A sub-inspector was seriously injured after being beaten on the head. See 2 pictures- Buffaloes moved out in trucks Around 100 personnel from the Municipal Corporation’s ETF force, along with police from Thakurganj, Para and Saadatganj police stations, are involved in Thursday’s operation. The drive is being carried out in Para Pink City, Buddheshwar Vihar and Gaddiyana. Officials say many dairy operators have already fled the area after moving their buffaloes. Animal Welfare Officer Dr Abhinav Verma said several illegal dairy operators removed their animals in trucks following Tuesday’s action. The operation began at 6 am, and by 8.30 am, officials had found only 10 buffaloes.
