stories.title: Cremations held on rooftops and streets in Kashi:Dam overflows in Sonbhadra, 14 gates opened, cobra enters Lakhimpur school; rain alert in 68 districts today
stories.summary: Monsoon rains continue across Uttar Pradesh, with heavy rain intermittently lashing Prayagraj for the past four days. Flood-like conditions have developed in Daraganj and Kareli, with water entering several houses to a depth of up to 5 feet. The Allahabad High Court has directed Prayagraj DM Manish Verma to ensure that water is drained from urban areas within 24 to 48 hours. On Thursday morning, clouds covered more than 40 cities, including Ayodhya and Jaunpur. The Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a rain alert for 63 districts today, including a red alert for heavy rain in 9 districts. Meanwhile, flood-like conditions have been reported in 13 districts, affecting 173 villages and more than 84,000 people. Mandakini crosses danger mark in Chitrakoot The Mandakini river has crossed the danger mark in Chitrakoot, submerging all the steps at Ramghat. Police have erected barricades along the river and are continuously making announcements over loudspeakers, urging devotees not to go near the water. Ganga enters 100+ temples in Varanasi; cremations held on roofs and in lanes In Varanasi, rising Ganga waters have entered more than 100 temples built along the ghats. The cremation grounds at Manikarnika and Harishchandra Ghats have also been submerged. Cremations at Harishchandra Ghat are now being carried out in the lanes and on the steps, while at Manikarnika Ghat, cremations are being performed on the rooftop. People are having to wait 3 to 4 hours for cremations. Around 5,000 people have been affected by flooding in Bahraich. SDM Monalisa Johri reached the affected areas by tractor to assess the situation. 5-foot cobra enters Lakhimpur Kheri primary school A 5-foot-long cobra entered a primary school in Lakhimpur Kheri. The principal called a snake catcher, who safely caught the snake and released it into the forest. For the first time, all 14 gates of the Kanhar Dam in Sonbhadra were opened simultaneously. The dam's water level has risen due to continuous inflow from Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, prompting authorities to open all the gates. Pictures of rain and flood- According to Lucknow's meteorologist Atul Kumar Singh- Moist winds are coming from the Bay of Bengal. Its effect is being felt in UP. Due to this, the spell of rain has started. This trend will continue till August 25.

stories.title: Mary Kom’s coach says, ‘I wore school uniform to weddings’:Went abroad first with father’s PF money; now gets Dronacharya Award
stories.summary: We are three brothers and two sisters. My father worked at BLW (Banaras Locomotive Works) and earned just ₹3,000 a month. Kaveri Government School was next to our house, where uniforms were provided. We wore those uniforms to school and even to weddings and festivals. We felt embarrassed, but we had no other option. That was when I decided to change my life. These are the words of boxer Chhotelal Yadav, Mary Kom’s coach, who hails from Kashi. After recalling his childhood, Yadav remained silent for a while, looking at the medals kept in his room. Yadav has now been selected by the Government of India for the prestigious Dronacharya Award, recognising his contribution to boxing and coaching. In this context, Dainik Bhaskar visited Chhotelal Yadav's home to learn his story of struggle. They also learned about his training sessions with Mary Kom and other boxers. Read the story, from a school uniform to a gold medal Couldn't buy jeans due to lack of money Chhotelal says, It was difficult for my father to raise a family of 7 people. We didn't have clothes to wear. When I first went to Uzbekistan to play, I asked my father for money. My father withdrew 5 thousand rupees from his PF and gave them to me.When I was selected in the Indian Army, I asked my father to get me jeans. But, due to lack of money, he couldn't get them. My hardships have made me strong. Whatever I did, I did it first for myself, then for the country. Used to go to arena with grandfather Chhotelal said, I was interested in playing. I used to go to the arena with my grandfather. There, people said that wrestling has nothing, run. I also started running, started running.One day I received information that there was a swimming trial in Sigra. I went there. I ran there. I came first there. After that, I was selected there and went to Pune.When I went to Pune, first I did swimming. I swam for 6 months initially and won gold in swimming in the Maharashtra District. But, my senior said that my body was not for swimming, but for boxing. At this, I had to change myself from swimming to boxing. After that, I dedicated myself to boxing. Training Mary Kom since 2015 Chhotelal Yadav says, Since 2015, I have been training Mary Kom. In 2015, Charles was a coach. I trained Mary Kom as an assistant coach with him. From 2016 to 2022, I gave her single-handed coaching. I was her personal coach. Along with Mary, I have also trained children. Most challenging thing He further says, The most challenging thing with Mary was that she was already a champion. For me, keeping a champion a champion was a challenge. There was also an age factor. In such a situation, I had to train her very smartly. All her children were born through operations. Therefore, I had to train her according to the operations, so that she wouldn't get injured. This was not just her test, but mine too. If I didn't perform, they would have also removed me. Mary is a boxing legend Chhotelal Yadav said, She is such a player that she remains very focused during training. She responds with her performance, not with words. She is a boxing legend. She is such a player who trains even after losing and even after winning.In 2017, Mary had a tournament in Mongolia. This was her first tournament under my training, but she lost in the quarter-finals. The next day, I thought she would be tired and wouldn't come for training, but she did.We worked a lot together. Two months after that, the Asian Championship was in Vietnam. In that, she defeated the same girl she had lost to and won gold in the Asian Championship. The day after winning, she came for training again. At that time, she was also a Member of Parliament. Currently a Subedar in Indian Army Chhotelal Yadav said, I am currently a Subedar in the Indian Army. I am training the women's team at the Army Sports Institute, Pune. Colonel Manoj and I started the women's team in the Army in 2022 after talking to our officers. For this, I had to struggle a lot, I had to fight a lot.Our women's team has 4 girls who were recruited as Havaldars (sergeants). They box on behalf of the Indian Army. Jasmin is the first girl who joined the Army women's team. After her, Sakshi and then Arundhati joined. He says, After the opening of this company, women got an opportunity to play from the Army. The women's boxing team was started in the Army. After its inception, many other things started in the Army. Currently, a girls' company has opened at the Institute, Pune. Training for all these things like weightlifting, boxing, archery has started there. If you play under pressure, you don't perform well Chhotelal Yadav says, When I was young, I used to go to the akhara (wrestling arena) in Banaras with my grandfather. My grandfather was a wrestler, and because of him, I wrestled. But, what I learned from Banaras is to stay cheerful. As long as you are training, stay completely focused. But, when you are fighting in the ring, fight with enjoyment, enjoy it.Only a Banarasi can do this. Because the more you enjoy playing, the better you perform. If you play under pressure, you don't perform well. Know more about Chhotelal, Mary Kom's coach Subedar Chhotelal Yadav, a resident of Pahari village in Varanasi, was born on May 5, 1988. He has been associated with the Army Sports Institute, Pune, of the Indian Army. After winning several medals at national and international levels as a boxer, he stepped into the world of coaching. He completed his Boxing Coaching Diploma from NIS Patiala in 2014-15. After that, he served as Mary Kom's personal coach from 2015 to 2022. Currently, he is the coach of the Elite Women's Boxing Team at the Army Sports Institute, Pune.

stories.title: Mother says, ‘They offered ₹8 crore to settle son’s murder’:‘Nothing matters more than a child’; 10, including former SP MLC, get life
stories.summary: My son was killed in the temple. We were at home. We are very satisfied with the verdict that has come after six years. We faced many difficulties. One son was murdered, while the other kept attending court hearings. We were pressured to compromise. Some offered ₹7 crore, while others offered ₹8 crore. But there is no compromise greater than one’s child. As she said this, tears welled up in the eyes of Sarla Chaubey, mother of advocate Manjul Chaubey. 10 sentenced to life imprisonment In the case involving the murder of Manjul Chaubey and his teacher sister Sudha Chaubey in Auraiya, the court has sentenced 10 people, including former SP MLC Kamlesh Pathak, to life imprisonment. The verdict comes six years after the murders and brings relief to the family, which says it faced pressure and repeated attempts to reach a compromise. Family remembers six-year struggle After the verdict, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Narayanpur locality, around 10 km from the district headquarters, and spoke to the family about the long legal battle and their experience during the six years. The family says that despite the difficulties, it remained determined to pursue the case until the court delivered its verdict. Complete incident details Advocate and cousin shot dead in broad daylight In Auraiya, advocate Manjul Chaubey and his cousin Sudha Chaubey were shot dead in broad daylight on January 15, 2020. Their family members were allegedly chased and assaulted, while police personnel were also attacked during the incident. Six years later, on Wednesday, August 19, at around 2 pm, the MP-MLA Court sentenced 10 convicts, including former SP MLC Kamlesh Pathak and his two brothers, to life imprisonment. Dispute over temple land led to enmity Kamlesh Pathak and Manjul Chaubey were friends before their relationship turned hostile over one bigha of temple land. The land was registered in the name of Maniram Bagia. According to the case, Kamlesh Pathak allegedly transferred the land to his own name through a sale deed. Manjul’s family opposed the transfer and got the sale deed cancelled. This dispute reportedly marked the beginning of the enmity between the two families, which eventually led to the double murder. What family members said about the court's decision Manjul Chaubey's house is located in Narayanpur locality. When we arrived, father Shivkumar Chaubey, wife Sarla, and 6-year-old granddaughter Aradhya were sitting in the verandah of the house. Aradhya was two and a half months old at the time of her father's murder. The daughter-in-law and daughter were also sitting nearby. There was satisfaction on everyone's faces regarding the verdict. Father Shivkumar, recalling the incident, says, We used to go to the temple for worship. That day too, we went to worship. These people, I don't know what got into them, started abusing us. They said that you will not worship here, this is our place. Suddenly they brought a gun and started firing. Our son and niece died. Father-in-law Shivkumar says, We are satisfied with the court's decision. We thank the government. The administration also fully cooperated with us in this. I never went to court, but my sons Sanjay and Ashish advocated strongly. They avenged their brother's murder. Went to court for the first time in 6 years The case ran for 6 years after my son's murder, but today was the first time we went to court. We didn't even see the faces of the murderers. We didn't dare to see their faces. We told our sons and came home. We didn't dare to stay there and hear the verdict. Our sons called and informed us about the verdict. Recalling the incident, Shivkumar says, After my son's murder, our daughter-in-law became like a madwoman. She started eating only once a day. Our granddaughter was only two and a half months old at that time. We somehow managed the family. Today, the court has done justice to our family. Mother became emotional remembering the incident The daughter and daughter-in-law were not ready to talk on camera and went inside the house. Mother Sarla Devi became emotional remembering the incident. Then, composing herself, she said, Today I am very satisfied with the court's decision. Many problems came. Many times I received threats. Many times pressure was put to compromise by taking 7-8 crore rupees. But, there is no compromise in the death of a child. Two brothers jointly advocated in court Manjul's family included father Shivkumar, mother Sarla, elder brother Sanjay, and a sister Rashmi, besides his wife Aarti and two-and-a-half-month-old daughter Aradhya. Rashmi is a government teacher and was married at that time. Meanwhile, Sudha's family included father Arvind Kumar, mother Guddi Devi (now deceased), brother Ashish Chaubey, and two sisters. Both sisters were married. Sudha was a government teacher and was to be married. Ashish and Sanjay pursued the case. After the court's decision, Sudha's brother Ashish said, On March 15, 2020, I and my entire family went to Panchmukhi Hanuman Temple for worship. There, Kamlesh Pathak, his brothers Santosh Pathak, Ramu Pathak, their brother-in-law, and other people surrounded and attacked us. In this, our brother Manjul and sister Sudha died. Ashish says, Our elder brother Sanjay Chaubey was shot in the leg. I, my father, and both my sisters were also injured. First of all, I would like to thank the administration, who supported me. They gave me the strength to fight against such a notorious criminal, against whom 80 cases are registered and no one in society dares to speak. I am satisfied with the decision. I had hoped for justice and trusted the court. Today, justice has won. How two close friends became sworn enemies Who is Kamlesh Pathak?

stories.title: YouTubers banned from entering UP govt schools:Restrictions on taking photos, videos; CJP running ‘School Thik Karo’ campaign
stories.summary: The entry of outsiders and YouTubers into Uttar Pradesh government schools is being restricted. On Wednesday, Ayodhya Basic Education Officer (BSA) Lal Chandra issued an order stating that action would be taken against anyone who takes photographs or makes videos inside schools without permission from the competent authorities. The BSA cited the safety and interests of students, saying some people were entering schools, recording teachers and staff and uploading the footage on social media. This was disrupting studies and affecting the dignity of the teaching profession. Similar orders have already been issued in Azamgarh, Ballia, Basti, Balrampur, Shamli and Agra. The officials' orders are being linked to the 'School Thik Karo' (Improve Schools Campaign) of the Cockroach Janata Party. Ayodhya BSA: Officers already deployed to inspect schools BSA Lal Chandra said government and administrative officials have already been assigned to inspect and monitor school arrangements. These officers conduct inspections from time to time, and action is taken according to the rules to address shortcomings identified during inspections. Therefore, outsiders have been prohibited from entering schools to carry out their own inspections or make videos. The order has been implemented with immediate effect across all council schools in Ayodhya district. Officials: People are entering schools to make videos for views Entry banned in 2,400 government schools in Agra On August 13, Agra BSA Rakesh Singh issued an order stating that outsiders had been entering some schools without permission to make videos for social media. Officials said this was disrupting classes and distracting students from their studies. Complaints had also been received about some teachers being harassed and blackmailed. Balrampur order issued on August 17 Balrampur BSA Vikas Chandra Srivastava said two people had recently approached a school seeking permission to make a video. They reportedly said their videos were not receiving enough views and that they wanted to increase the figure to 7 lakh views. According to the BSA, such people enter schools not to suggest improvements but to increase their social media views. He said the learning environment in schools could not be allowed to deteriorate in the race for views. However, the BSA clarified that the order does not amount to a complete ban on the media or all outsiders. Its purpose is to regulate entry into schools and maintain a conducive environment for learning. Ballia also bans unauthorised entry into aided schools Unauthorised entry by YouTubers and people associated with social media channels has been prohibited in both government and aided basic education schools in Ballia. Outsiders will not be allowed to enter school premises without permission. BSA Manish Singh issued the order on August 7. CJP founder launched campaign on August 15 Abhijeet Dipke launched the 'School Thik Karo' (Fix Schools) campaign from his village in Hingoli, Maharashtra, on August 15. He said poor students were suffering because of government negligence and demanded a cap on private school fees. Dipke also said that in the next phase of the campaign, he would visit government schools in other parts of Maharashtra to check whether students were receiving adequate facilities. He expressed his displeasure over the incident in Bengal.

stories.title: Why does Akhilesh want leaders to control statements?:Samajwadi Party chief advises caution; how BJP uses Opposition remarks as a weapon
stories.summary: A statement by Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav has attracted considerable attention. At the party office on August 15, he told workers that there was little time left before the election and warned them against making any statement that could benefit the BJP. The remark has been linked to a statement by Shivpal Yadav. During a visit to Rampur, Shivpal had said that once the SP formed the government, it would “avenge every injustice” done to Azam Khan. He also said Azam would be made Home Minister and all cases against Azam and Sambhal MP Zia Ur Rehman Barq would be withdrawn. So, why has Akhilesh advised SP leaders to be careful about what they say? And what message was he trying to send without naming anyone? Why is Akhilesh trying to control party leaders’ statements? Akhilesh fears that statements by party leaders could derail the SP’s election strategy and shift the focus away from its key issues. There are three main reasons behind his caution. Trying to create a ‘soft Hindutva’ image Senior journalist Siddharth Kalhans says Akhilesh is trying to expand the SP’s support among non-Yadav OBCs and upper castes by combining its PDA — backward classes, Dalits and minorities — formula with a ‘soft Hindutva’ approach. Shivpal’s statement, however, could reinforce the SP’s image of favouring Muslims. The BJP has linked his remarks to Hindu-Muslim polarisation and the law-and-order record of previous SP governments. Akhilesh wants to avoid falling into such a political trap. Does not want any caste or community to feel alienated Akhilesh has also advised party leaders to speak cautiously, taking lessons from the BJP’s defeat in the Bankipur by-election in Bihar. Political analysts believe the BJP lost its traditional seat, which has a sizeable upper-caste population, partly because of dissatisfaction among upper-caste voters. Prashant Kishor had raised the alleged fake encounter of Bharat Tiwari during the by-election campaign. Similarly, in May 2026, party spokesperson Rajkumar Bhati made a controversial remark about Brahmins. The statement drew criticism from the BJP and BSP, as well as SP MLAs. It raised concerns that the party could lose support among Brahmin voters, who account for around 12% of Uttar Pradesh’s electorate. The last four Assembly elections also show the importance of Brahmin support, with the party that managed to attract the community emerging in power. Does not want an anti-SP narrative to take shape A statement by BJP candidate Lallu Singh during the 2024 Lok Sabha election changed the political narrative around the polls. Singh had said that although a government could be formed with 272 seats, such a government would not have enough strength to amend the Constitution. He said more than two-thirds of the seats would be needed and referred to changing several rules, amending the Constitution or creating a new one. The opposition, including the SP, used the remark to build a narrative around the BJP’s ‘400-plus’ target and the alleged threat to the Constitution. The BJP ultimately failed to secure a majority on its own. Akhilesh therefore does not want an unexpected statement by an SP leader to alter the entire election narrative. How does the BJP turn SP leaders’ statements into election weapons? The 2022 Assembly election offers several examples of how controversial remarks by SP leaders and its allies were used by the BJP against the party. August 2021: Freedom fighters compared with Taliban Then-SP MP from Sambhal, Shafiqur Rahman Barq, compared freedom fighters with the Taliban. He said that when India was under British rule, Indians had fought for independence, and the Taliban was similarly trying to free its country. The remark triggered a controversy. Barq later said his statement had been presented out of context. However, during the 2022 election, the BJP repeatedly used the remark to portray the SP as having an anti-national and pro-Muslim mindset. March 2022: ‘There will be an account of officials’ Abbas Ansari, the Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party candidate from Mau, made another controversial statement during the 2022 election campaign. The SBSP was then an ally of the SP. Ansari said he had spoken to Akhilesh and that after the government was formed, there would be no transfers or postings of officials for six months. Those posted in a place would remain there, he said, adding that an “account” would first be settled. Ansari is the son of former MLA and gangster-turned-politician Mukhtar Ansari. The BJP used the statement to attack the SP over law and order during its previous governments and alleged that the party protected figures such as Mukhtar Ansari and Atiq Ahmed. Listen to Abbas's full statement December 2022: Azam Khan’s controversial remark Azam Khan won the Rampur Assembly seat in the 2022 election, but lost his membership after being convicted several months later. During the December 2022 by-election campaign, Azam made a controversial remark while campaigning for the SP candidate. He suggested that under previous governments, people would have had to ask him for permission even before being born. The BJP portrayed the remark as evidence of an anti-women mindset and the arrogance of a “mafia raj”. Azam had also lost his Assembly membership following a controversial remark. During the 2019 Lok Sabha election, he had made an objectionable comment about then-Rampur district magistrate Aunjaneya Singh. The series of controversies contributed to the SP losing the Rampur Sadar seat, which had long been considered Azam Khan’s stronghold. BJP’s Akash Saxena won the seat, becoming the first BJP MLA elected from there. The BJP uses such statements to argue that the SP wants to promote controversial leaders and give them important positions. This helps it build a narrative that the party’s priorities are not development or public issues, but controversial political figures. The BJP then makes such controversies the centre of the political debate, forcing the SP to remain on the defensive. What is the SP’s biggest challenge before the 2027 election? Political analysts believe the SP faces two major challenges, but controlling statements by party leaders is likely to be the more immediate one given the political context and the timing of the election. Siddharth Kalhans says that even if the opposition is strong and united, its strategy can fail if statements by party leaders create a narrative that strengthens the rival party’s agenda. The BJP often builds its election campaign around law and order and polarisation. This is one of its biggest strengths. When SP leaders make statements on sensitive issues, the BJP quickly uses them to go on the offensive. This is why Akhilesh has even said that a printed sheet could be prepared for leaders at every level, telling them exactly what to say — and what not to say. Akhilesh has also made it clear that the SP wants to fight the next election on issues such as fertiliser and DAP availability, unemployment, inflation, poor-quality expressways and reservation. He fears that reckless statements could divert media and public attention from these issues towards individual leaders and controversies. Opposition unity is another challenge Kalhans says the SP and Congress performed well together in Uttar Pradesh in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. A united opposition will again be important in 2027, but bringing different parties together will not be easy. Seat-sharing among the SP, Congress and smaller parties will be a major challenge. With Mayawati becoming more active, there is also a possibility of non-BJP votes being divided. The SP’s ability to unite the wider opposition will therefore depend on the positions taken by other parties. The two challenges, however, are different. Opposition unity can be achieved through negotiations and seat-sharing, while controlling controversial statements is primarily a matter of party discipline. If controversial remarks continue, even a united opposition could struggle to win voters’ trust.

stories.title: No lathi-charge, dialogue to handle Gen Alpha protests:Only young officers to be sent to interact with students; UP govt's SOP for protests
stories.summary: Children aged up to 14, identified as Gen-Alpha, are increasingly taking to the streets in Uttar Pradesh over basic issues such as poor roads to schools, shortage of teachers and inadequate hostel food. On Wednesday, August 19, Gen-Alpha protests were reported simultaneously in Unnao, Hamirpur and Mahoba. Earlier, students had blocked a road in Lucknow and children in Kannauj had locked themselves inside a room in protest against poor-quality hostel food. The protests have presented a new challenge for the administration, as there have been no clear leaders or organisers. Officials have been faced simply with groups of children and the question of how best to respond. The state government is therefore preparing a special Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) to deal with protests involving school students. The SOP will have two main objectives: What will be special about the UP government’s SOP? A BJP state organisation office-bearer said the party and the government’s top leadership had learnt lessons from the incidents at Jantar Mantar and decided to adopt a softer approach. In simple terms, the approach will be ‘dialogue, not lathis’. The move has reportedly received the approval of both the central and state organisations. Whenever Gen-Z or Gen-Alpha students take to the streets, only young officers from the concerned district will be sent to interact with them. They will be expected to speak to the students as friends rather than in an authoritative manner. The officers will listen to their concerns and, wherever possible, resolve the problems on the spot. The aim is to build trust between the younger generation and the government. The SOP is also expected to make it clear that protesting students will not face criminal cases. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has also announced a new Youth Policy aimed at strengthening the government’s engagement with Gen-Z. The policy includes four major initiatives. 1. Youth commission A youth commission will be set up with young people and student representatives, rather than administrative officials, playing a key role. They will be able to directly raise their problems, priorities and policy suggestions with the government. 2. More jobs All recruitment bodies, including the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission (UPPSC), Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission (UPSSSC) and the Education Service Selection Commission, have been asked to fill vacant posts and speed up the declaration of recruitment examination results. 3. Recruitment through an outsourcing corporation The corporation is expected to begin functioning in August, with one lakh new recruitments planned before December. Gen-Z candidates are expected to receive a significant share of these opportunities. Direct recruitment for posts linked to cyber security, including a director of cyber security, chief technology officer and positions related to the State Data Authority, is also expected to be accelerated through the State Transformation Commission. 4. Jobs in high-tech sectors The government plans to create 75,000 direct jobs in sectors such as artificial intelligence, robotics, semiconductors, data centres and cyber security. What does the UP Police SOP say? UP DGP Rajeev Krishna said the younger generation was thinking ahead and had a strong capacity to learn. He said the police would need to understand how young people communicate in order to engage with them effectively. A new SOP is therefore being prepared for the state police. Under the proposed approach: Why are Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha being treated as sensitive groups? Concern over the impact on elections The Uttar Pradesh Assembly election is due in around six months. According to experts, around 80% of Gen-Z are currently voters, numbering approximately 2.07 crore. Meanwhile, children aged 5-14, who fall within Gen-Alpha, will start becoming eligible to vote over the next four to five years. Experts believe that if an anti-government sentiment takes hold among this generation, it could have an impact on future elections. Fear of a negative public message from lathi-charge Police action or physical force against schoolchildren and young people could send a negative message to the public. The government therefore wants such situations to be handled with restraint. Opposition could turn protests into an election issue Student protests can quickly gain support on social media. A demonstration in one city can have repercussions across the state. The Samajwadi Party and Congress have openly supported protesting students, raising concerns within the government that the opposition could turn the issue into an election campaign. Why are children taking to the streets? Local pressure on government schools has weakened Clinical psychologist Dr Krishna Dutt said children from all sections of society earlier studied in government schools, whether they came from poor or affluent families. As education became increasingly privatised, families with greater financial means moved their children to private schools. Government schools were then left largely with children from lower-income families. According to Dutt, this reduced local pressure on the authorities and allowed the condition of government schools to deteriorate. He said the situation would change significantly if government officials also sent their children to government schools. Officials should treat students like their own children Former Basic Education Department director Sarvendra Vikram Bahadur Singh said the way children had protested in Lucknow and Fatehpur suggested that they had not necessarily planned the demonstrations themselves. He said Gen-Z students in these districts could also have played a role. “Children do not generally think in terms of organising protests or sit-ins,” he said. Singh also said education department officials often failed to interact with students in a parental manner during school inspections. Instead, he alleged, many inspections were carried out merely to complete paperwork. From the Red Fort to the RSS, focus shifts towards youth PM Modi’s focus on Gen-Alpha During his Independence Day address from the Red Fort, Prime Minister Narendra Modi described Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha as the backbone of Viksit Bharat 2047. He announced AI training for one crore young people, free online coaching and a nationwide sports talent hunt for Gen-Alpha. RSS calls for new ways of engaging with youth RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat has acknowledged that if young people are raising questions, there could be shortcomings in the system. RSS general secretary Dattatreya Hosabale said the younger generation could not be taught using old methods and that new approaches would have to be developed. ABVP backs students but warns against exploitation ABVP state minister Arpan Kushwaha said there were shortcomings in the education system and that Gen-Z and Gen-Alpha were taking to the streets to demand their rights and protect their future. He said students had access to extensive data and information and that protesting for their rights was legitimate, provided the methods remained lawful. The ABVP, he said, stood with the students, but authorities would also have to ensure that anti-national elements did not exploit their protests.

stories.title: 2,000 students leave hostels in Prayagraj:Beds submerged in rain, food shortage forces exodus; say, ‘We craved even tea’
stories.summary: Heavy rain and widespread waterlogging in Prayagraj have disrupted the lives of thousands of students and families. Around 2,000 students, most of them preparing for competitive exams, have reportedly left the city after water entered hostels, lodges and rented accommodation. Pavnesh Singh, a student preparing for competitive exams, told Dainik Bhaskar that his hostel was flooded and the beds were submerged. Around 35-40 students had already left the hostel and returned home. He said filth had spread throughout the area and that even a posh locality such as Georgetown was facing severe waterlogging. Students from other parts of the city were also leaving because of problems with food, drinking water and studies. When these difficulties began, Pavnesh did not wait for the rain to stop or the knee-deep water to recede. He placed his trolley bag on his head, carried a bag and satchel in his hands, and walked through waist-deep water to leave the hostel. Student Hemant Yadav described a similar situation, saying the accumulated water had blocked the entire route. He feared that exposure to dirty sewer water could lead to illnesses such as typhoid and malaria. With hostels and lodges flooded after the early spells of rain, students fear that continued flooding could force thousands more to leave the city. See 2 pictures- Students leave rooms after even tea becomes difficult to get Around 2,000 competitive-exam students left Prayagraj on Wednesday. Some returned to their villages and towns, while others moved into rooms occupied by fellow students or stayed with relatives. Most of those affected were living on the lower floors of hostels, lodges and rented accommodation. Their rooms were flooded, while knee-deep water blocked the routes from their gates to the roads. Cooking became difficult, travelling outside became almost impossible and even getting a cup of tea became a struggle, prompting many students to leave. Books, beds and household items submerged; bikes and scooters damaged Students living in hostels, lodges and rented rooms maintain small households of their own. Floodwater damaged gas stoves, petromax lamps, heaters, floor mattresses, folding beds, food supplies, chairs, tables and books. Suitcases and bags containing clothes were submerged, while wooden platforms and beds were also covered in water. For many students, their entire household belongings have been damaged. Bikes and scooters have also been submerged, creating another challenge as students try to get their vehicles repaired. Students across 11 areas start looking for safer accommodation Prayagraj has a large population of students preparing for competitive examinations, with several neighbourhoods regarded as student hubs. As waterlogging has spread to areas such as Georgetown, conditions have also begun deteriorating elsewhere. Students living in Allapur, Salori, Chhota Baghara, Bada Baghara, Colonelganj, Shivkuti, Shukla Market, Daraganj, Bakshi Bandh and Rajapur, among other areas, have started looking for safer accommodation and gradually vacating their rooms. 7,000 families forced between flooded homes and rooftops When the Ganga and Yamuna overflow, Prayagraj regularly faces flooding. This time, however, just three days of rain have created a major crisis, with around 7,000 families affected by waterlogging. On the fourth day, many families have been forced into a daily routine of removing water from the lower parts of their homes in the morning and sleeping on rooftops at night. Whenever it rains, they rush downstairs to drain the accumulated water again. Continuous rainfall has flooded lower rooms and kitchens in several areas, including JK Nagar, Gaddha Colony, Shams Nagar, Gaus Nagar, B Block, JK Ashiana and Jafri Colony in Kareli, as well as Islam Nagar. Thousands of houses have also been affected in Rajapur, Allapur, Sadar Bazar, Georgetown, Tagore Town, Mundera, Jayantipur, Naini and Jhansi. Some families have moved to relatives' homes. Mayor visits waterlogged areas after social media trolling Widespread waterlogging across the city, including knee-deep water inside the municipal corporation premises, led to Mayor Ganesh Kesharwani being heavily criticised on social media. On Wednesday, after water levels receded somewhat, the Mayor visited several affected areas to inspect the situation. He live-streamed the visit on Facebook, but several people continued to criticise and taunt him through comments on the live stream. DM and Municipal Commissioner inspect areas on foot after High Court summons After being summoned by the Allahabad High Court, DM Manish Kumar Verma and Municipal Commissioner Seelam Sai Teja inspected waterlogged areas on foot along with other officials. After the inspection, the DM said the municipal corporation was using pumping sets to drain the water. Low-lying neighbourhoods including Georgetown, Tagore Town, Allapur and Kareli have been affected. He said teams from Jal Nigam (Water Corporation) and Ganga Pollution, along with the municipal corporation, were also working on drainage. According to him, water had already been cleared from several neighbourhoods and the remaining areas would be drained soon. The DM attributed the waterlogging to heavy rainfall and choked drains in the affected neighbourhoods. High Court takes suo motu cognisance; officials appear in court The Allahabad High Court took suo motu cognisance of the waterlogging in Prayagraj and heard the matter on Wednesday. Municipal Commissioner Seelam Sai Teja and DM Manish Kumar Verma appeared before the division bench of Justice Ajit Kumar and Justice Garima Prasad. The Municipal Commissioner told the court that a work plan for a permanent solution to the city's waterlogging problem was ready and that an affidavit would be filed on August 20. Additional Advocate General Manish Goyal said the affidavit of the Urban Development Department Secretary would also be submitted. The court directed authorities to drain water from Mori Gate in Daraganj and clear waterlogging from affected areas within 24 to 48 hours. The Municipal Commissioner was ordered to appear before the court again on August 20, while the DM was exempted from personal appearance for the time being. Officials held responsible for city's waterlogging Municipal Commissioner Seelam Sai Teja, Mayor Ganesh Kesharwani and Municipal Corporation Chief Engineer DK Sachan have been held responsible for the waterlogging during the rainfall.

stories.title: Free 3 days bus travel for women on Raksha Bandhan:Male companions to also get discount; Yogi tells private operators not to overcharge
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government has announced free bus travel for women in Uttar Pradesh during Raksha Bandhan. Women will be able to travel free of cost on state-run roadways buses from 6am on August 27 to midnight on August 29. Each woman passenger can also travel with one companion free of charge. The facility will also be available on more than 900 buses operated by the Urban Development Department. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath issued the directions during a meeting with officials on Sunday to review transport and traffic arrangements for Raksha Bandhan. CM says, Raksha Bandhan is on August 28. A large number of women will travel to their maternal homes during the festival. In view of this, women and one companion will be allowed to travel free of cost on UP Roadways buses. Additional buses will also be operated. The CM has directed officials in all districts to hold meetings with bus, taxi and auto-tempo unions by August 25. He said private vehicles must not charge arbitrary fares and passengers should be charged only the prescribed fare. Strict action will be taken against overloading, overcharging and misbehaviour with passengers. Taxi and e-rickshaw drivers will also be verified. Dainik Bhaskar had already revealed this 11 days ago. Extra buses to run as women travel home for Raksha Bandhan Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on August 28, and a large number of women are expected to travel to their parental homes and return during the festival. The Chief Minister directed officials to operate additional buses to meet the expected rush. He also asked officials to hold meetings with bus, taxi and auto-rickshaw unions in all districts by August 25. Transport operators have been instructed to charge only the prescribed fares, while action will be taken against overloading, overcharging and misbehaviour with passengers. Taxi and e-rickshaw drivers will also undergo verification. UP Roadways to run additional buses from August 26 to 31 Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh has directed officials to operate additional buses from August 26 to 31 to ensure smooth travel during Raksha Bandhan. All buses of the state transport corporation will remain operational during this period to manage the expected passenger rush. Officials have also been instructed to ensure cleanliness and adequate drinking water at all bus stations. Better lighting and fan arrangements will be made in waiting rooms, while a 24-hour control room will remain operational throughout the period. Restrictions to be relaxed on select routes during festival rush Transport Corporation MD Prabhu N Singh said, “Restrictions on buses travelling from Delhi towards Ghaziabad, Meerut and Moradabad via Moradabad-Bareilly would be relaxed. Similarly, restrictions on routes from Delhi towards Ghaziabad, Agra and Etawah via Aligarh-Kanpur would also be eased.” He added, “Additional buses will also be deployed for western Uttar Pradesh routes if passenger occupancy reaches 60% at the originating point.” Raksha Bandhan: Roadways employees’ leave cancelled Transport Corporation MD Prabhu N. Singh said restrictions on buses operating from Delhi to Ghaziabad, Meerut and Moradabad via Muradabad-Bareilly will be reduced. Similarly, restrictions on buses running from Delhi to Ghaziabad, Agra and Etawah via Aligarh-Kanpur will also be relaxed. If buses have 60% passengers at the originating point for routes to western UP, additional buses will be operated. No leave for Roadways staff for six days Except in special circumstances such as the death of a family member or personal illness, officials, supervisors, drivers and conductors involved in bus operations will not be granted leave. Officials deployed during the festival will not be allowed to remain absent from their workplace without permission. Violators will face disciplinary action. Employees completing the target will get a bonus MD Prabhu N. Singh said drivers and conductors who complete 1,800 km of bus operations during the six-day festival period will receive an incentive of ₹1,200. Contract drivers and conductors will get an additional 55 paise per kilometre for operating buses beyond 1,800 km during this period. Technical staff who remain present every day at depots and regional workshops during the festival period will receive an incentive of ₹500. Raksha Bandhan to be celebrated on August 28 Raksha Bandhan will be celebrated on August 28 this year. According to the information provided, the festival will be observed without the Bhadra period, allowing sisters to tie rakhi throughout the day. The full moon period will begin at 8.31am on August 27 and continue until 9.18am on August 28. Rakhi can be tied during this period.

stories.title: Fish served at Ajay Rai’s conference in Ayodhya:BJP MLA calls it an insult to Sanatan, organiser says, 'Constitution was followed'
stories.summary: UP Congress President Ajay Rai reached Ayodhya on Sunday. Here, he recited the Hanuman Chalisa at Hanumangarhi. Then he visited Ramlala. After this, Ajay Rai participated in the Congress workers' conference held at Tarun Bazar in the Goshainganj assembly constituency. This is about 38 kilometers away from Hanumangarhi. A fish feast was organized at this conference. This conference was organized by Ram Nihal Nishad, who recently joined Congress from BJP. He said - It is not written anywhere in the Constitution that fish should not be eaten in Sawan. We are following the Constitution. On the other hand, BJP MLA Ved Prakash Gupta said- During the month of Sawan, crores of Sanatanis are engrossed in the worship of Lord Shiva. At that time, consuming fish is an open display of Congress's anti-Sanatan mindset. Congress should understand that the faith of the Sanatan society is not a political laboratory. Visiting Ayodhya, bowing down in temples, and then consuming fish exposes the dual character of Congress. The public will respond to those who toy with Sanatan faith. Earlier, on 11 August, Cabinet Minister Sanjay Nishad in the UP government had called fish vegetarian. He had said - fish prepared without garlic and onion is vegetarian. The emblem of the UP government and the Constitution of India features fish, arrow, and bow. This is the symbol of the Nishad community, of which we are proud. Ram Nihal said, ‘Both types of food were prepared’ Ram Nihal Nishad was the president of the BJP's executive committee. On 23 June, he had joined the Congress. This was his first program after joining the Congress. He is claiming a ticket from the Congress for the Gosaiganj assembly seat. Ram Nihal Nishad informed that two types of food were prepared at the conference held at Arpit Marriage Lawn in Tarun development block. Besides fish, there was also vegetarian food. UP BJP chief says, ‘Insulting Sanatan is Congress’s identity’ UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary criticised the alleged fish feast organised during the welcome of the Uttar Pradesh Congress president in Ayodhya, calling it “condemnable and unforgivable.” He accused Congress of repeatedly hurting the religious beliefs and sentiments of Sanatan followers for “vote-bank politics” and said the event during Sawan showed disrespect for Ayodhya’s sanctity, Kanwariyas and saints. BJP Mahanagar president Kamlesh Srivastava also condemned the event, saying it insulted Sanatan traditions and devotees’ sentiments. He demanded that Congress apologise publicly and stop its “appeasement politics.” He said that the people of Ayodhya will never accept such a mockery of religious sentiments. Meanwhile, BJP District President Radheshyam Tyagi said that Ajay Rai has come to Ayodhya in the holy month of Sawan to visit temples. However, a fish feast was organized at the conference he attended. Former Mayor said - Hurt Hindu sentiments Former Mayor Hrishikesh Upadhyay also accused Congress of being anti-Sanatan. He said - Congress does not even celebrate Hindu festivals. They were calling Lord Ram imaginary; now they come to visit the Ram temple. After this, they hold a Congress conference. Then they work to hurt the sentiments of Hindus. Meanwhile, Congress District President Chetanarayan Singh said- I don't know about the fish feast incident. We went with President Ajay Rai. stories.title: Manoj Tiwari’s brother's last rites performed at Manikarnika Ghat:MP carried his bier, died at AIIMS
stories.summary: Sadhu Sharan Tiwari, elder brother of BJP MP and Bhojpuri actor-singer Manoj Tiwari, passed away on Saturday. He breathed his last at AIIMS, New Delhi, at 1:15 PM. Sadhu Sharan, affectionately called 'Sadhu Bhaiya' by the family, was the eldest of four brothers and one sister. His last rites were performed on Sunday at 5 PM at Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi. Manoj Tiwari also walked on foot during his brother's final journey. Sadhu Sharan Tiwari had retired from the post of General Manager at ONGC. He served in several places, including Kolkata, Nazira-Sivasagar in Assam, and Mumbai. After retirement, he was living at his residence in Chitaipur, Varanasi. Manoj Tiwari described his elder brother as the guardian of the family and his source of inspiration. He said that Sadhu Sharan played a crucial role in advancing his singing career. Journey from IIT-BHU Engineering to GM at ONGC Sadhu Sharan Tiwari was also very good at studies. He obtained an engineering degree from IIT BHU. After this, he started working at Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC). During his job, he worked at various places, including Kolkata, Nazira-Sivasagar in Assam, and Mumbai. After serving for a long time, he retired from the post of General Manager (GM). After retirement, he made Varanasi his home and started living in his house located in Chitaipur. Manoj Tiwari said, ‘He was like a God’ Manoj Tiwari described his elder brother as the guardian and guide of the family. He said that Sadhu Sharan was like God to him. In the family too, his position was that of the eldest member and guide. He also made a significant contribution to Manoj Tiwari's musical journey. He encouraged his younger brother to progress in the field of singing and guided him at every step. According to Manoj Tiwari, Sadhu Sharan inspired him to move forward on the path to success. Recited a poem at the last meeting Manoj Tiwari also recalled his last meeting with his elder brother. He said that Sadhu Sharan's nature was such that he would explain something to him in every meeting. In their last meeting too, he had recited a poem to Manoj Tiwari. At that time, the MP had no idea that this would be his last meeting with his brother. Last rites performed at Manikarnika Ghat After his demise at AIIMS in Delhi on Saturday, Sadhu Sharan Tiwari's body was brought to Varanasi. The last rites were performed at Manikarnika Ghat on Sunday around 5 PM. Manoj Tiwari also participated in the final journey along with family members and close relatives. The MP walked on foot in his elder brother's funeral procession. During this time, there was an atmosphere of mourning among family and acquaintances.

stories.title: Wife slashes husband from chest to private parts:Removes intestines and stuffs them in a sack; half liver and kidney missing
stories.summary: A woman murdered her husband in Kurukshetra, Haryana, cutting him from the chest to the private parts with a sharp weapon. She removed his intestines and put them in a plastic sack. While she was carrying out the crime, the landlord arrived. On seeing him, she jumped from the roof and was later admitted to hospital. The incident took place on Saturday, while photos related to the case surfaced on Sunday. The postmortem also revealed that about half the liver and the right kidney were missing from the deceased's body. The police are now investigating the case of missing organs from the body along with the reason for the murder. It has also come to light that the woman used to practice witchcraft. Living in a rented house for one year The deceased has been identified as Rajesh (40), a resident of Dhampur village in Sitapur district of Uttar Pradesh. He had been living for the past one year in Kurukshetra in a rented house near Raj Palace on Pehowa Road with his wife, Vimala Devi. He worked in water supply at PB RO Water Trading Company located on Pehowa Road. Landlord said - Saw her putting intestines in a sack Landlord Rinku said that on Saturday around 5 pm, he heard Rajesh and Vimla screaming from the room. When he reached the terrace, Rajesh was lying drenched in blood with deep wounds on his stomach. He saw that Vimla was putting Rajesh's intestines, which had come out of his stomach, into a sack. Rinku said that, seeing him, Vimla got nervous and jumped down from the terrace. She got injured from the fall. The police team has found three knives of different sizes at the spot. They had no children after marriage According to the landlord, Vimla also practiced witchcraft, and there were frequent disputes between the husband and wife. They had been married for several years and had no children. However, the real reason for the murder is not yet clear. Forensic expert said - There was a 37-centimeter-long wound Forensic expert Dr. Gaurav Kaushik said that when the body came to him, it did not have half a liver and one kidney. There was a 37-centimeter-long and deep incision on the deceased's stomach. The intestines were protruding from the incision. It is the police's responsibility to recover the deceased's half liver and one kidney. Woman will be questioned after treatment KUK police station in-charge Surendra Sandhu says that after the postmortem, the body has been handed over to the family members. The accused woman is currently undergoing treatment. Once her condition improves, she will be arrested and interrogated.

stories.title: 4 arrested in ₹1.16 billion cyber fraud case:143 NCRP complaints linked to 41 bank accounts; fake firms used to commit fraud
stories.summary: Varanasi's Cyber Crime Police and Chetganj Police have arrested four notorious cyber criminals. Of the four arrested criminals, one is from Sasaram in Bihar, and three are residents of Varanasi. All were involved in cyber crimes worth ₹1 billion 4 crore and were providing accounts and their details to cyber criminals sitting far away by creating fake firms. 143 NCRP complaints have been registered against 41 bank accounts found with them. Currently, police have sent all of them to jail in a case registered at Chetganj police station. After police interrogation, two other criminals, Prateek Tiwari alias Bunty and Romil Verma, are being searched for. See pictures... Arrested from Karaundi area ACP Crime Vinay Dwivedi informed that a case was registered at Chetganj police station, in which information about cyber fraud was given. Based on this case, the cyber crime team and Chetganj police station personnel were searching for the criminals. In this sequence, police received information that some suspicious persons of criminal nature were present near Vivekanandpuri Colony, Karaundi. Acting on this, police conducted a raid and arrested them. The criminals arrested on the spot gave their names as Nitish Kumar Pandey, Dushyant Singh, Himanshu Jha and Rehan. Fraud was being committed in the name of fake firm In this regard, ACP Crime Vinay Dwivedi informed - A special campaign is being run against cyber criminals. Today, on Sunday, the cyber crime team and Chetganj police station have nabbed a gang. This gang was opening bank accounts by creating fake firms in the names of people from Banaras and those coming from outside, luring them with commission. They kept all the details of the accounts that were opened. Through these, all the cyber frauds that are committed through gaming and other methods, the money would come into these accounts. Fraud of more than ₹1 billion 16 crores The ACP further informed - Among the arrested criminals, one Nitish Kumar Pandey, resident of Deehi, Shivsagar police station, Rohtas, Sasaram, who was currently residing in Vivekanandpuri Colony, Chitaipur, revealed - He used to provide all these accounts to the cyber criminals sitting above, and they would send the cyber fraud money into these. A total transaction of ₹1,168,658,321 has taken place in these 41 accounts, on which NCRP complaints have been filed. Sent to jail The ACP informed that, among all these criminals, criminal records have been found against Nitish Kumar Pandey. Criminal records of others are also being searched.

stories.title: Suspended woman sub-inspector speaks out over offensive reel:Says she has been locked in her room for 5-days and is having suicidal thoughts
stories.summary: A female police officer in Meerut, Anu Collis, who was suspended 7 days ago over an objectionable reel, went live on YouTube for the first time on Saturday. She responded to the influencer Amit Kilhor, who had first made her video go viral. Anu said, ''I have been locked in a room for many days. I feel like ending my life, such thoughts are coming to my mind. You know how difficult it is to get a government job.'' Anu was wearing the same dress in which her video had gone viral. She said, ''Amit Kilhor has now deleted that video from his social media account. Now he is apologizing to my brother.'' First, know about Anu... Anu Collis is a UP Police Sub-Inspector from the 2023 batch. She is originally from Prayagraj. In Meerut, she was first posted at Rohta police station, Brahmpuri, and was later posted at the SSP office. On 16 August, 2026 (Sunday), she was suspended with immediate effect on the orders of the then SSP Avinash Pandey in a case of violation of police conduct rules and an alleged objectionable video going viral. Influencer Amit Kilhor had trolled her by sharing a video. He wrote, ''Anu Collis makes her obscene videos by putting QR codes, goes live. She takes funding. After the video went viral, an investigation was launched against Anu. SP Crime Avanish Kumar is investigating this.'' Now read what lady constable Anu said, read verbatim... ''My name is Anu Collis. You may have seen one of my videos on social media. An influencer, Amit Kilhor, shared the video on his Instagram account and tagged the Uttar Pradesh DGP, Chief Minister, my department, and several others. I want to ask Amit Kilhor: Why did you take my personal photos and videos from my social media accounts and share them without my permission? Did you ever ask for my consent? By sharing my personal content without permission, you committed a cybercrime. Why did you delete the video later? You are now calling my brother and apologising, saying it was a mistake. You have ruined my life and destroyed everything I worked for. My 20–25 years of hard work, career, and future have been affected. I have been completely defamed. I was accused of making obscene videos and content. What exactly did you find obscene about my content? What was your problem with it? I am coming live today because no one took my side. My brother put forth his point, but not many people saw it. Obviously, in today's world, who watches what boys have to say? Amit bhaiya, I want to ask you something. If you were so concerned about my department or about me, and you thought I was doing something obscene, then why didn't you file a complaint? You had my number. Why didn't you complain to my department? You could have filed an FIR against me or complained to my department. Why didn't you tell my SSP sir, whom you know very well and for whom you gave a long lecture? What was the problem in doing that? Were you getting fewer views? You took my photo without my permission and put it on your channel just for views.'' This is the frock whose screenshot was taken ''Amit bhaiya, this is the same frock whose screenshot you took. Take the screenshot now. Everyone, take its screenshot and upload it, saying Anu Rani's another obscene video has gone viral. You want to earn views. I bought this frock with my mom from a mall in Agra. My mom liked it a lot. You can see this frock. It is a normal and beautiful frock. My name is Anu Collis. My nickname is Selina. I am an Anglo-Indian girl and Roman Catholic. Wearing such clothes is normal in my house. My parents have no problem, and my brother also has no problem. We wear such clothes here. If you have a problem, then don't watch. Amit bhaiya, what did you gain by ruining my life? I have been in a closed room for five days and am very distressed. I am having thoughts of harming myself. I am receiving death threats. My family is being spoken about inappropriately. Wrong things are being said about my brother too. My mother is very simple, and she is also having to hear a lot.'' You made a video just for views ‘’It is being said that I do sex chat. Does YouTube promote sex chat? If it does, then I am saying that this is my name, and I stand by my words. I am giving it in writing that I will not resign. You can take my screenshot and send it to my department, the cyber police station, or my SSP sir. Send it to whoever you want to send it to.'' Senior Inspector said - You have defamed the department Anu said that today I went to my office. There, I met a very senior inspector whom I respect a lot. But he told me, "You have defamed the department." He said this, even though someone had created a video of him and made it viral using AI. How many people will I have to explain that I am right and that wrong has been done to me? I am silent; it doesn't mean that I am wrong. stories.title: Symbolic funeral procession of upper-caste MPs and MLAs held:Over 300 people take to streets and call themselves ‘constitutional untouchables’
stories.summary: Brahmins and Thakurs associated with the Savarna (upper- caste) Morcha organization staged a strong protest on Sunday in Lucknow. People from other categories also joined them. More than 300 people gathered at Women Power Line intersection around 12 PM and started chanting slogans for UGC rollback. They held placards that read 'Constitutional Untouchables'. After protesting for half an hour at the intersection, they started moving towards Baikunth Dham cremation ground. When such a large crowd took to the streets, all three roads leading from Women Power Line intersection towards Baikunth Dham, Hazratganj, and VIP Guest House were jammed. The protesters also took out a symbolic funeral procession for the Savarna MPs and MLAs. When they reached Baikunth Dham cremation ground, they sat there and chanted 'Hi-Hi' (slogans of condemnation). The protesters said that 'we are constitutional untouchables'. We have been kept away from our interests. Paths are being closed for future generations as well. Only when the UGC chapter is completely closed, and reservation is abolished, should Modiji dream of 2029. During the symbolic funeral procession of upper-caste MPs and MLAs, protesters chanted slogans: ‘He is dead, brother, he is dead, our leader is dead.’ Police from 5 police stations were deployed during the protest. Protesters were detained near Baikunth Dham and sent to Eco Garden. These people had arrived to protest at the invitation of Sandeep Singh, president of Savarna Morcha. See 5 pictures- After walking some distance, people took out a symbolic funeral procession for the upper-caste MPs and MLAs.

stories.title: 60 extra buses to run in Gorakhpur for Raksha Bandhan:Services to increase from 26 August, women and one companion to travel free from 27 Aug night
stories.summary: 60 additional buses will be run in Gorakhpur Local. In view of the possibility of an increase in the number of passengers on Rakshabandhan in Gorakhpur, the roadways have intensified preparations. Bus frequencies will also be increased from 26 August. The focus will be mainly on the Gorakhpur to Lucknow, Varanasi, Deoria, Basti, and Kushinagar routes. On the day of Rakshabandhan, women will get the facility of free travel in buses. From the night of 27 August to the night of 28 August, women will be able to travel in UP Roadways buses without fare. One co-passenger will also be given the facility of free travel with them. 60 additional buses, number will increase if needed On Raksha Bandhan, there is a possibility of an increase in passenger crowds at Gorakhpur bus stands. In view of this, the transport corporation has arranged additional buses. 60 additional buses will be run on different routes of Gorakhpur Local. From 26 August, the frequency of buses will also increase. If the number of passengers suddenly increases on any route, an additional bus will be sent there immediately. More pressure on Lucknow-Varanasi route The number of passengers is high on routes from Gorakhpur to Lucknow, Varanasi, Deoria, Basti, and Kushinagar. On Raksha Bandhan, the pressure on these routes is expected to increase further. Therefore, along with increasing the availability of buses on these routes, their frequency will also be increased. Free travel for women from the night of 27th On Rakshabandhan, women will get the facility of free bus travel for 24 hours. From the night of 27 August to the night of 28 August, women passengers will be able to travel without fare. One co-passenger will also be able to travel for free with them. Before and after this period, normal fare will apply. All depots alert, focus on security too RM Love Kumar Singh informed that all depots have been alerted regarding Rakshabandhan. Additional buses will be deployed on the spot according to the number of passengers. Special attention will also be given to the safety and convenience of women, so that passengers do not face any kind of problem during the festival.

stories.title: Gorakhpur man attempts suicide by jumping into Rapti:PAC team rescues him within minutes, hands him to police
stories.summary: On Sunday morning, a young man allegedly jumped into the Rapti river in Gorakhpur in an apparent suicide attempt. Within seconds, he began drowning in the deep water, triggering panic at the spot. However, a flood relief team from the 26th Battalion PAC, stationed nearby, immediately launched a rescue operation and pulled him to safety. The incident took place at Ramghat in the Nausad area. A major tragedy was averted because of the team’s quick response and presence of mind. Twenty-five-year-old Laddu Manjhi, a resident of the Majhaulia police station area, reached Ramghat at around 9 am and jumped into the river without telling anyone. The strong current and depth of the river quickly left him struggling in the water. The situation turned critical before people nearby could react. Rescue operation launched by motorboat Seeing the young man drowning, people at the ghat raised an alarm and immediately alerted the PAC team stationed nearby. All eyes turned towards the river as people feared for his life. The B Team of the 26th Battalion PAC, deployed at Ramghat for flood relief operations, immediately sprang into action. Under the leadership of team leader Rana Pratap Chauhan, the jawans boarded a motorboat and entered the river. Despite the strong current and depth, the team reached the young man within minutes and pulled him out of the water. Young man handed over to police After the rescue, the young man was brought safely to the riverbank and given first aid. He was later handed over to the local police. According to police, Manjhi is a resident of West Champaran in Bihar and had been under stress for some time. Police said he jumped into the river after becoming distressed. He is currently safe, and his condition is reported to be normal. The PAC personnel were praised for their courage and quick response. Team leader Rana Pratap Chauhan said the jawans took the right decision at the right time, helping save a life. Head Constable Baldev Prasad and Constables Jitendra Kumar, Ravi Gautam, Vikas Jaiswal and Ravindra Paswan were part of the rescue operation. The operation was successfully completed through the combined efforts of the team.

stories.title: Medical Representative burnt alive inside Wagon-R:Driving seat turned into pyre, short circuit locked doors; man was on his way to meet his mother
stories.summary: A 50-year-old man was burnt alive after his Wagon-R caught fire in Barabanki on Sunday morning. The incident occurred around 10.30 am when the car suddenly caught fire and quickly turned into a ball of flames. All four doors became locked. Rajanarayan Verma, who was sitting in the driver’s seat, became trapped inside. He tried to open the door but could not escape. Villagers rushed to the spot after seeing the flames but were unable to approach the burning car. They alerted police and the fire brigade and tried to douse the flames with water. By the time the teams arrived, the fire had been brought under control. The car door was broken open, and Rajanarayan’s badly burnt body was found stuck to the seat. The body was recovered and sent for post-mortem. Police said the car was a petrol variant and the initial investigation suggests a short circuit caused the fire. The vehicle has been seized. The incident took place in the Safdarganj police station area, around 15km from the district headquarters on the Barabanki-Ayodhya road. See the horrific pictures On his way to meet mother, man died just 2km from home Rajanarayan Verma worked as a stamp vendor at the Barabanki registry office. He was originally from Bariyarpur village and lived with his wife in a house in the Vijaynagar area of the city. His daughter is married, while his son lives in Andhra Pradesh and is doing B.Tech. Rajanarayan’s parents, Mewa Lal Verma and Babita Verma, lived in the village. His brother, Jung Bahadur Verma, worked in property dealing in the city, and Rajanarayan also worked with him. Earlier, he had worked as a medical representative (MR) for 10 years. According to the family, Rajanarayan attended a relative’s event on Saturday night. On Sunday morning, he left for Bariyarpur village in his Wagon-R (UP 41 R 8292). He turned towards the Bhaudra road in the Safdarganj area from the Barabanki-Ayodhya road. When he reached a canal just 2km from home, smoke suddenly started coming from inside the car. Within moments, the vehicle caught fire. Safdarganj police station in-charge Amar Chaurasia said- Information was received about a car catching fire. The police team reached the spot and took possession of the body and sent it for post-mortem. Initial investigation revealed that the fire was caused by a short circuit in the wiring. Police are investigating the circumstances of the accident and the actual causes of the fire.
