stories.title: Lucknow murder case:Manager wife demanded ₹1.5 crore, wanted to live separately from sister-in-law; SBI officer killed entire family in 30 minutes
stories.summary: Lucknow police say an SBI officer carried out two murders and killed himself within 30 minutes, after allegedly surveilling his estranged wife for two days. Initial investigation has pointed to two possible motives: bank manager Divya Mishra had sought ₹1.5 crore in alimony from her husband, SBI officer Manas Bajpai, during divorce proceedings, and she did not want to live with his mentally ill sister, Sheeba. According to police sources, a hearing in the couple's divorce case was held in family court on 18 August, during which a dispute reportedly broke out between Manas and Divya over the alimony demand. Police say Manas grew increasingly disturbed after this and began planning to kill his wife and sister before taking his own life. He allegedly bought three firearms and surveilled Divya for two days. On Thursday afternoon, around 12 pm, Manas reportedly arrived by auto-rickshaw at the ICICI Bank branch where Divya worked and called her outside. Police say the two argued and there was a physical altercation, after which Manas shot her twice in the face. The incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed outside the bank. He then reportedly fled the scene in the same auto-rickshaw and reached his home, about 2 km away. Police say he shut himself in a room, played the Hanuman Chalisa loudly on television, then shot his sister Sheeba in the head before shooting himself. Divya was the sister of YouTuber Pragya Mishra, who has alleged that her brother-in-law was "psycho" and that her sister kept her distance from him for this reason. Manas and Divya had married for love nine years ago. Read the full story See 2 pictures related to the murder Love marriage nine years ago, wife left home a year ago According to family members, Manas and Divya married in 2017 and their relationship was reportedly fine in the initial years, but disputes over minor issues began later, leading to growing distance between them. In 2018, when Manas's mother was diagnosed with cancer, Divya reportedly moved back in with him. Around this time, disputes are said to have started between the couple over living with Manas's sister. After his mother's death in 2019, Divya reportedly separated again, before the two later reconciled. In 2025, the dispute over the sister reportedly resurfaced, with Divya saying she did not want to live with her, while Manas was said to be unwilling to agree. Divya reportedly moved out completely in November 2025. Manas is said to have tried to save the marriage and spoke to Divya several times, but the matter eventually reached Lucknow family court. Divya filed a case in the family court in January 2026, beginning the legal divorce process. Bought three weapons, began surveilling wife A friend of Manas told police he had been out of the city for around three months for bank audit work. After returning, he reportedly learnt of the 18 August family court hearing and attended it, where police say he learnt of the ₹1.5 crore alimony demand, which allegedly left him stressed. According to the police investigation, after the 18 August hearing, Manas planned to kill his wife and sister and then take his own life. He is said to have arranged three weapons — reportedly two 9mm pistols and a country-made pistol — over two days. Police have recovered all three weapons, all of which were loaded. Where and from whom he obtained them is still under investigation, after which he allegedly began surveilling Divya. Called wife over, allegedly beat then shot her Divya's cousin, Mayank Dixit, said that on 20 August, Divya had gone out for bank work and, upon returning to office by car in the afternoon, found Manas already present. He reportedly signalled to her and said he wanted to talk. When Divya approached him, Manas allegedly began assaulting her. Bank guards and staff reportedly rushed to help her, during which Manas allegedly shot her in the forehead. Divya collapsed on the road, after which Manas fled the scene. He is then said to have gone straight to his home, about 2 km away, where he allegedly shot his sister Sheeba dead before shooting himself. CCTV footage of the entire sequence has also emerged. WhatsApp status before suicide alleged wife "betrayed" him Police say Manas put up a WhatsApp status after killing his wife, in which he accused her of betrayal and wrote about killing himself and his sister. The status reportedly also mentioned Divya's sister Pragya and her husband, Bharat Yadav. Mayank Dixit said Pragya and Bharat had no knowledge of any such plan, and that Manas's behaviour had not seemed normal for some time. Police are also investigating the claims made in the status. Divya was living with parents, Manas lived with sister in rented house After separating from Manas, Divya had been living at her parental home in Shringar Nagar, Alambagh. She had recently built a house in Buddheshwar, Para, where she was living with her parents at the time. Her father is a retired government employee, while her mother is a homemaker. Manas lived in a rented house near Husadiya Chauraha with his sister, Sheeba Bajpai (28). He worked as a field officer at SBI's engineering college branch. His father, also a bank employee, died around six years ago; his mother has since died as well. Pragya alleges Manas was also involved in mother's death YouTuber Pragya Mishra wrote on X, alleging that her sister had told her Manas and his sister had beaten their ailing mother so severely that she died. She alleged her brother-in-law was "psycho" and had stalked Divya before. She said Divya had been in an accident some time earlier due to stress, breaking her arm and leg, and had only returned to work after a month and a half, still limping. Pragya wrote that everyone who knew Divya was aware of what she had endured, and that she felt this was an important time to speak out despite her grief. "He was cruel to my sister," Pragya alleges Pragya alleged that on their wedding night, Manas had drawn up a list of household expenses and insisted Divya pay half, which she had agreed to. She alleged he was cruel to her sister, including berating her over spoiled tomatoes ordered through a delivery app. She said Divya had stopped paying her share of expenses over the past year, which she believed Manas may have viewed as a betrayal, while Divya had simply wanted to separate from him. Pragya said her sister had told her there had been a confrontation between Manas and a counsellor during family court proceedings. "She wanted things to be fine, hoped he would change" Pragya said she had known her brother-in-law was cruel to her sister and that this was why Divya wanted to separate, but she had not anticipated he would take such a drastic step. She said that despite everything, Divya had still planned to observe the Teej fast and had not removed a tattoo of Manas's name, saying she had hoped, deep down, that things would work out. Pragya said she had not been able to bring herself to tell their mother that Divya had been killed, telling her instead that her condition was critical, and that this was the first time she had realised how difficult it was to speak the truth.

stories.title: Yogi govt gives bulletproof jackets to Akhilesh, Mayawati:44 leaders receive ₹10 lakh jackets; minister says, ‘We don’t know how to wear them’
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government has provided bulletproof jackets to 44 leaders, including Akhilesh Yadav and Mayawati, ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. The list includes 11 Cabinet ministers. Ministers Sanjay Nishad, Nand Gopal Gupta ‘Nandi’ and OP Rajbhar have received the jackets. The bulletproof jackets have been purchased by the UP government’s Security Headquarters. Each jacket reportedly costs around ₹10 lakh. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Minister Sanjay Nishad confirmed that he had received one. However, he said he did not know how to wear it and had not yet been trained to use it. According to sources, the government has taken the precautionary step keeping the 2027 Assembly elections in mind. This is reportedly the first time that bulletproof jackets have been provided to political leaders. The government has not officially disclosed why the jackets are being distributed. However, sources said 98 leaders in Uttar Pradesh currently have security cover under different categories, of whom 44 have been provided with bulletproof jackets. The list is not limited to ministers and prominent opposition leaders. BJP’s firebrand western UP leaders Sangeet Som and Suresh Rana are also among those receiving the jackets. Rana is an MLA, while Som currently holds no political post. This has led to speculation that the jackets may have been issued based on intelligence inputs. 98 people have security cover in UP, 12 have Z-plus security These ministers have Y-plus security Sanjay Nishad gets Y-category security State Fisheries Minister Sanjay Nishad has been provided Y-category security with an escort. The same security cover has been given to Pankaj Singh, son of Rajnath Singh; former Governor Kalraj Mishra; former Governor Phagu Chauhan; State Women’s Commission vice-chairperson Aparna Bisht Yadav; former DGP and BJP Rajya Sabha MP Brij Lal; Rajveer Singh, son of former Chief Minister Kalyan Singh; Pooja Pal, MLA from Chail in Kaushambi; and Santosh Das, popularly known as Satua Baba, the mahant of Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi. Overall, 10 people have Y-plus security, 26 have Y-category security, and 17 have X-category security.

stories.title: ₹1.40 crore worth of hydroponic cannabis seized in Gorakhpur:5 smugglers arrested; consignment was to be supplied to clubs and discos in Gujarat
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Ramgarhtal police, in a joint operation with the Anti Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) and Uttar Pradesh Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), have arrested five alleged smugglers and uncovered an interstate network involved in supplying hydroponic ‘OG’ cannabis from Thailand to Delhi and then Gujarat. Cannabis allegedly supplied to Gujarat clubs and discos According to sources, the high-value cannabis was allegedly being smuggled into Gujarat and supplied to clubs and discos, where it was sold to young people at premium prices. 3.085kg cannabis worth Rs 1.40 crore seized The five suspects were arrested late on Wednesday (19 Aug) night in the Ramgarhtal area. Police recovered 3.085 kg of hydroponic cannabis, estimated by ANTF to be worth around ₹1.40 crore. An Ertiga car, five mobile phones and ₹30,390 in cash were also seized. The accused are residents of Pratapgarh and Gujarat. 3kg hydroponic cannabis recovered from Ertiga during search SP City Nimish Patil said, “The joint ANTF and UP ATS team intercepted an Ertiga bearing registration number GJ-15 AA-8841 near the LIC office on Deoria Bypass late on Wednesday, August 19. During a search of the vehicle, officers recovered hydroponic ‘OG’ cannabis from the accused.” Thailand consignment allegedly routed through Delhi to Gujarat During interrogation, the accused allegedly revealed that the hydroponic cannabis sourced from Thailand was being transported to Gujarat via Delhi. In Surat and Bhavnagar, the cannabis was allegedly divided into smaller packets and sold to users at high prices. Investigators also suspect that supplies were delivered to clubs and discos based on demand. Cannabis allegedly collected from vehicle in Deoria The arrested suspects have been identified as Suraj Singh and Satyam Singh of Karmahi village in Kandhai, Pratapgarh; Prince Patel of Grid Road, Navsari; Ratnam Trivedi of Katargam, Surat; and Bhavin of Daman Chowk, Bhavnagar. During questioning, the accused allegedly told investigators that a youth had supplied the OG cannabis in a vehicle bearing a Deoria registration number. His identity and address have not yet been established. ATS and ANTF teams have also found indications pointing to foreign links in the suspected smuggling network. Investigation underway to trace Thailand-India route Investigators are now trying to establish how the cannabis allegedly travelled from Thailand to India and identify the channels used to transport it further. The accused's mobile phones are being examined to trace their contacts and the wider network. The ANTF Gorakhpur unit in-charge has lodged an FIR for alleged drug trafficking at Ramgarhtal police station.

stories.title: Digital arrest, nude video calls… 4 weapons of cyber fraud:Over ₹100 crore scammed every month in UP; 2.5 lakh complaints, less than 1% FIRs
stories.summary: More than ₹100 crore is being lost to cyber fraud in Uttar Pradesh every month. Shocking figures from the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) show that over 2.5 lakh complaints were received in the state in the past seven months, but FIRs were registered in only 1,040 cases. Police managed to arrest just 1,957 accused. Instead of hacking mobile phones or computers, cyber fraudsters are now hacking people’s minds. They exploit fear, greed, romance and sympathy to trap victims. From educated young people to senior citizens, victims have lost more than ₹720 crore to such frauds. Timely intervention helped freeze ₹242 crore, but ₹478 crore reached the fraudsters. Here is how the four major cyber fraud models work: 1. Digital arrest: Fraudsters exploit fear of police action In this model, fraudsters pose as police officers or officials from investigative agencies and threaten victims with legal action. According to the NCRP, such cases may be fewer in UP, but they accounted for around 23% of the money lost to cyber fraud in the seven months. In July, a senior citizen couple in Lucknow was kept under ‘digital arrest’ for nearly seven days. The fraudsters posed as senior officials of an investigative agency and claimed that a SIM card issued in the couple’s name had been used for terrorist activities in Kashmir and money laundering. The couple became so frightened that they locked themselves in a room at home. The fraudsters remained connected with them through video calls and continuously issued instructions. They even controlled when the couple slept, woke up and ate. Under pressure, the couple broke fixed deposits and transferred their life savings. They ended up transferring ₹70 lakh to the fraudsters’ bank accounts. 2. Greed: Fake investment schemes promise quick profits This model generally begins with a phone call or social media message. Victims are persuaded to transfer money through UPI. It is the most common model in UP, accounting for 32% of cases. A recent case was reported from Kanpur on 16 August. Rajaram Shakyawar was added to a social media group and promised high returns from the stock market. The fraudsters claimed to be associated with a registered security company. They first shared stock market information to gain his trust and then persuaded him to invest in IPOs and FPOs. He transferred ₹6.5 lakh. When Rajaram tried to withdraw the money, the fraudsters demanded more deposits. Realising he had been duped, he filed a complaint on the cybercrime portal. Kalyanpur Police are investigating the bank accounts, mobile numbers, website and financial transactions linked to the case. 3. Nude video calls: Threat of public shame used to extort money Around 9–10% of cyber fraud cases follow this model. Many victims hesitate to report such crimes because they fear social embarrassment. On 6 April, a retired sub-inspector from Bhogaon in Mainpuri was targeted through a romance scam. A woman first called him on WhatsApp and claimed to be a relative. She then made a video call and suddenly appeared nude when he answered. He immediately ended the call. Around 40 minutes later, she called again, claiming that her mother was ill and she needed ₹1 lakh. She threatened to make the video call recording public if he did not pay. The retired officer refused. The next day, he received an edited video on WhatsApp showing him apparently speaking to the woman while she was nude. Fearing public humiliation, he transferred around ₹3.47 lakh to the bank account provided by the fraudster. 4. Impersonation: Fraudsters hack accounts and ask contacts for money In June, Dr Himani Agrawal, a member of the Uttar Pradesh State Commission for Women, had her WhatsApp account hacked. The fraudsters began messaging people in her contact list, including police officers, doctors and others. Posing as Dr Agrawal, they asked for ₹45,000, ₹50,000 and ₹52,000. Some people even transferred money. The fraud was exposed when people who knew Dr Agrawal called her to confirm the requests. Such cases account for around 5% of cyber fraud in UP. One reason the success rate is lower is that people often call the person directly to verify the request, preventing the fraud. Cyber expert: Fraudsters create pressure to make victims act quickly Cybersecurity expert Rakshit Tandon, who trains Uttar Pradesh Police personnel in cyber technology, says fraudsters use one tactic regardless of the method: they pressure victims into making an immediate decision. They repeatedly tell victims that they have only five minutes to act — otherwise a case will be registered, a parcel will be seized or their bank account will be permanently blocked. This leaves victims with little time to think, speak to their family or contact the relevant department. They make decisions under fear and pressure, which is exactly what fraudsters exploit. Tandon advises victims not to panic if they lose money to cyber fraud. The first hour should be treated as the ‘golden hour’. Victims should immediately call the national cybercrime helpline 1930. The sooner a complaint is filed, the greater the chance of putting the money on hold or recovering it. Children and young people are also being targeted Cyber fraudsters are increasingly targeting children and young people through gaming, fake APK files and investment scams. Gaming apps: Free coins can empty bank accounts Children are offered free coins, rewards or new characters in online games. They may then be asked to download an app or click on a link. In some cases, children also share passwords or OTPs received on their parents’ phones. Fraudsters can then withdraw money from the linked bank account within minutes. Fake APK files: Wedding invitations and challans used to hack phones Fraudsters send APK files through WhatsApp or SMS, disguising them as wedding invitations, traffic challan updates or documents containing confidential information. Once a person downloads and installs the file, malware can enter the phone. This allows fraudsters to gain control of the device and steal OTPs and other sensitive information. Fake trading and crypto schemes: Promises of 500% returns Fraudsters create fake trading and cryptocurrency groups on Telegram and Instagram, promising returns of up to 500%. They initially show fake profits on an app or account to gain the victim’s trust. Once the victim is convinced, they are encouraged to invest larger amounts. Young people who have recently started working are particularly vulnerable as they can be drawn in by promises of quick money and end up losing their savings.

stories.title: How responsive are UP DMs, SPs to common people?:Bhaskar called officials in all 75 districts, only 3 answered; know the reality
stories.summary: Most government officials in Uttar Pradesh appear to be unavailable to members of the public — either attending meetings or participating in video conferences. Many district magistrates (DMs) and senior police officers do not answer calls made to their official numbers themselves. Instead, their official phones are often with public relations officers (PROs) or stenographers, who decide whether a caller can speak to the officer. This is despite government rules requiring DMs, SPs and SSPs to keep their official mobile phones with them and answer public calls themselves. The government spends crores of rupees every year to keep these official numbers operational so that people can seek quick solutions to their problems. The police department alone spends around ₹9 crore a year on recharges for its official CUG numbers. Yet, officers often appear reluctant to speak to people over the phone. MPs and MLAs have repeatedly raised complaints about this with Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. But do officers really fail to answer their official numbers? To find out, Dainik Bhaskar called the official numbers of DMs and police chiefs in all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh. Since officers could be busy at different times, calls were made three times a day — at 11 am, 3 pm and 6 pm. Now, let's tell you sequentially what responses were received where 72 of 75 DMs did not answer calls Of the 75 DMs contacted, 72 did not answer the calls themselves. In several districts, the PRO answered the phone, while in some cases the number could not be reached. Only three DMs directly answered the call and explained how the problem could be addressed. The situation was worse with the police chiefs. Not a single SP or SSP spoke directly over the phone. In Moradabad, the SSP’s PRO even asked whether the caller had used any “source” or contact to get through to the officer. Here is what Bhaskar found across the districts: In 25 districts, the answer was: ‘DM is in a meeting’ In Firozabad, Mainpuri, Mathura, Kanpur Nagar, Kanpur Dehat, Ayodhya, Sultanpur, Gorakhpur, Maharajganj, Lalitpur, Banda, Bahraich, Balrampur, Shravasti, Saharanpur, Rae Bareli, Meerut, Gautam Buddh Nagar, Baghpat, Bulandshahr, Hapur, Shahjahanpur, Basti, Hathras and Pratapgarh, the person answering the phone gave the same response: The officer is in a meeting or video conference. In 14 districts, assistants offered alternatives In Agra, Jhansi, Jalaun, Kannauj, Kaushambi, Mirzapur, Gonda, Bareilly, Lucknow, Chandauli, Azamgarh, Varanasi and Sonbhadra, the PRO or stenographer did not connect the caller to the DM. Instead, they suggested visiting the tehsil or sub-divisional magistrate (SDM), or coming to the office the next day with a written complaint. Some were ‘busy with guests’, others had switched-off phones In Kushinagar, the DM’s PRO said guests had arrived and the officer was busy. In Farrukhabad, Chitrakoot and Pilibhit, callers were told: “The DM is busy. Come to the office tomorrow.” In Shamli, the PRO suggested sending the complaint on WhatsApp instead of connecting the caller to the DM. In Prayagraj, the DM’s PRO said the CUG number was meant only for emergencies and that the officer was at the High Court. However, the government rules allow members of the public to contact officials on their official numbers. The CUG numbers of the DMs in Ambedkar Nagar, Ghaziabad and Kasganj were switched off. In Deoria, Etah, Amethi and Siddharthnagar, the numbers repeatedly showed messages such as “out of network coverage area” or “not reachable”. In 21 districts, the phone kept ringing In Unnao, Amroha, Mahoba, Hardoi, Sitapur, Barabanki, Moradabad, Ghazipur, Ballia, Mau, Bhadohi, Jaunpur, Fatehpur, Badaun, Bijnor, Muzaffarnagar, Rampur, Sant Kabir Nagar, Sambhal, Hamirpur and Aligarh, the phone kept ringing, but no responsible officer or staff member answered. Only three districts offered a solution In Etawah, DM Shubhrant Kumar Shukla answered the official number himself. He listened to the problem and advised the caller to first approach the tehsil. He said he would personally look into the matter if it was not resolved there. In Auraiya, the DM was on leave for official reasons, but Additional District Magistrate (ADM) Brijesh Kumar answered the CUG number. He listened to the problem and offered help. In Lakhimpur Kheri, DM Anjani Kumar Singh answered the call himself and asked the caller to send the complaint directly on WhatsApp, providing a simple way to register the grievance. What happened when Bhaskar called the police chiefs? Bhaskar called the official numbers of 68 SPs/SSPs and seven police commissioners across Uttar Pradesh. Not a single police chief spoke directly. Three police chiefs had switched-off phones The official numbers of the SPs in Hapur, Mirzapur and Sant Kabir Nagar were switched off. Calls went unanswered in 16 districts Calls to the official numbers of the police chiefs in Lucknow, Ghaziabad, Baghpat, Ballia, Barabanki, Bijnor, Ghazipur, Gonda, Gorakhpur, Jhansi, Kannauj, Kanpur Dehat, Mahoba, Mau, Saharanpur and Shravasti went unanswered. Only two offices called back The SP offices in Maharajganj and Sonbhadra called back later. However, even there, the PRO spoke to the caller instead of the SP. The response was the same: “The officer is busy. We will get you connected later.” Assistants answered in 54 districts In 54 districts, assistants answered the calls and said the police chief was busy in a meeting and might be available later. When Bhaskar called again, however, the officer was still not connected. Strange responses from Kushinagar and Moradabad In Kushinagar, PRO Mahendra Prajapati, speaking on behalf of SP Keshav Kumar, said the officer did not speak to people over the phone. He asked callers to visit the public grievance hearing between 10 am and 2 pm or tell him their problem. In Moradabad, the SSP’s PRO asked: “Are you an officer? Have you got someone to call on your behalf to speak to the sahib?” He added that the SSP did not speak to people directly over the phone. What do the rules say about official numbers? In November 2020, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath ordered all DMs, SPs and SSPs to keep their official mobile phones with them and answer calls from the public themselves. The order also prohibited officers from handing over their official phones to PAs, PROs, gunmen or subordinate staff. The Chief Minister’s Office can randomly call officers on their official numbers to check whether they are answering calls themselves. Failure to answer or return missed calls can be treated as indiscipline and neglect of public grievances, with departmental action possible. On 15 March 2021, then Director General of Police Hitesh Chandra Awasthi also issued a strict circular directing all police chiefs, commissioners, DIGs and IGs to keep their official numbers with them. Police spends ₹9 crore a year on CUG numbers The Uttar Pradesh Police has around 25,000 CUG SIM cards, most of them operated through BSNL. The state’s 2026-27 Budget provides around ₹9 crore for keeping these numbers active and paying for data and other recharges. The department declined to disclose the expenditure on CUG connections issued to district magistrates. The Bhaskar investigation raises a basic question: if official numbers are meant to give citizens direct access to senior officers, why are so few officers answering those calls themselves?

stories.summary: In an inspiring turn of events, Sandwich Terns have returned to Pagham Harbour in unprecedented numbers following a devastating bird flu outbreak. Thanks to dedicated habitat restoration and predator management efforts, conservationists have helped establish one of England's largest breeding colonies. The sight of flourishing chicks this breeding season, nourished by ample food resources, signals a promising recovery for seabird populations grappling with the aftermath of disease.

stories.title: Lok Sabha Secretariat issues notices to 20 rebel TMC MPs
stories.summary: Dated Aug 25, the notices to the 20 rebel MPs forward a copy of Banerjee’s petition dated June 18 filed against the MPs under Rule 6 of the Members of Lok Sabha (Disqualification on Ground of Defection) Rules, 1985. In the recently concluded Monsoon session, Banerjee had met the Speaker on Aug 12 to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted to him in June.

stories.title: For nearly a decade, a California town fought to seize its privately owned water utility
stories.summary: In a landmark decision, California's Supreme Court dismissed a town's claim regarding the use of eminent domain for utility purposes. The judges emphasized the need for a thorough, independent evaluation of necessity declarations before any utility can be seized. This shift significantly impacts how courts will weigh municipal efforts to take over private utility companies, allowing private water, gas, and electricity firms to challenge such actions more effectively.

stories.title: How 23,000 edible dormice became a problem for Britain
5.2 kg heroin seized in Jammu, NCB busts Pakistan network; 3 held
stories.summary: “Preliminary investigation led NCB to another resident of Baramulla, the suspected mastermind. He was traced and arrested in Leh on Aug 24. The seized drug, suspected to have been smuggled from Pakistan, entered India through the Uri border sector,” the NCB official said. “The probe will identify cross-border suppliers, financial links, transporters, local associates, and the intended distribution network,” the spokesperson added.

stories.title: ICE arrests nearly 50,000 immigrants in July, highest monthly tally under Trump’s second term
Chantelle Van Vliet wins £32,237 after being fired over menopause symptoms, tribunal rules
stories.summary: A 48-year-old beauty therapist was fired after requesting flexible working hours to manage severe menopause symptoms, including fatigue, confusion and brain fog. An employment tribunal found that she had been subjected to disability discrimination and denied reasonable workplace support. Chantelle Van Vliet was awarded £32,237 in compensation, although receiving the money remains uncertain because the company is in voluntary liquidation.

stories.title: This 240-mile stretch on Dalton highway in Alaska is one of America’s remotest roadways
'Open dialogue, inclusive to all': RSS reacts to row over Mohan Bhagwat's New York event
Govt pushes to make SCADA systems in power sector Indian by 2030
'Let sugar become expensive': BJP minister Vijayvargiya's odd take on price spike
Meet Alyssa Yu, the 17-year-old Maryland student who built a mathematical model for what...
stories.summary: A student from Maryland has developed an innovative model aimed at predicting the interactions of infectious diseases, effectively filling a critical gap in public health forecasting amid multiple outbreaks. Her groundbreaking research has garnered her recognition as a finalist in a national science competition. This mathematical framework could revolutionize the planning of focused vaccination campaigns during epidemics, providing essential strategies for managing disease transmission.

stories.title: California man arrested with guillotine in pickup truck near US Capitol building
Meet Ashka Shah, the 17-year-old New York student who studied how a cancer-driving protein
stories.summary: A student from New York has pioneered a groundbreaking technique aimed at halting the growth of cancer cells. This research focuses on a crucial protein linked to the rapid development of tumors. By inhibiting the harmful activity of this protein, her method preserves the viability of healthy cells. She gained national acclaim as a finalist in a prestigious science competition, illuminating a promising new pathway for precision cancer therapies.

stories.title: US colleges are rolling out three-year bachelor's degrees in 120 programmes across 26 states
stories.summary: US colleges are increasingly offering three-year bachelor's degree programmes that require 90 credits instead of the traditional 120. The programmes are now available or announced in 26 states, with 119 reduced-credit programmes identified by RAND. Supporters say they can save students time and money, while critics question their impact on learning, professional licensing, graduate admissions and employer acceptance.

stories.title: Holly Madison won’t sell her ‘haunted’ LA home; lists it for rent at $9,500 a month
stories.summary: Holly Madison has listed her historic Tudor-style Los Angeles home for $9,500 a month after deciding not to sell it. She bought the property for just under $1.5 million in 2012 and has described it as a fairytale-like home. The house was also investigated for paranormal activity in 2021. Madison says she may eventually keep the property for retirement and pass it on to her children.

stories.title: Brooklyn newlyweds got bedridden with norovirus just after a day of their wedding reception
3 teenagers killed, 4 injured in Brooklyn highway crash
Quote of the day by Confucius: "The good man does not grieve that other people do not..."
Uttarakhand CM Dhami joins Tapkeshwar Mahadev Shobha Yatra
stories.summary: Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Wednesday participated in the Shobha Yatra of Tapkeshwar Mahadev Ji, which commenced from Shivaji Dharamshala in Arhat Bazaar and will pass through major routes of Dehradun before reaching the historic Tapkeshwar Mahadev Temple.

stories.title: Meet Kinley Rasmus, the 12-year-old Alabama girl who became only the 25th girl to play in the...
stories.summary: Kinley Rasmus made history as the 25th girl to participate in the Little League World Series. With a remarkable debut, she pitched six scoreless innings, striking out eight batters, equaling Mo'ne Davis's record for female pitchers. Additionally, Rasmus made her mark by setting a record for the highest number of hits by a female player, earning admiration from fans across the nation.

stories.title: UP: CM Yogi launches 'Lokmata Ahilyabai Matrushakti Yatra', women aged 60+ to get free bus travel
stories.summary: Speaking at the launch event in Lucknow, CM Yogi said the scheme was aimed at making the journey of women more convenient and dignified and strengthening their self-reliance.

stories.title: 3 Telangana students killed in Florida road accident, one identified as Nizamabad native
14 fossilised teeth from Egypt reveal five extinct ancient shark species
stories.summary: Fossilised shark teeth from Egypt's Western Desert reveal prehistoric ocean life. Scientists discovered teeth from five extinct shark species in the Abu-Tartur Plateau region. These ancient predators inhabited warm tropical seas during the Late Cretaceous period. The findings expand the known record of shark diversity in North Africa. This discovery highlights Egypt's ancient marine environments hidden beneath its deserts.

stories.title: Beyond Ayodhya and the fish row: Why Nishad vote matters in Uttar Pradesh 2027 battle
stories.summary: A fish controversy in Uttar Pradesh has highlighted the Nishad community's political significance. This community's vote has shifted loyalties and remains a key factor for parties. The BJP seeks to retain its OBC coalition while opposition parties try to gain support. Nishad leaders have historical ties to epic narratives and social justice movements. The 2027 elections will test alliances and demands for representation and livelihoods.

stories.title: Evening news wrap: Over 30 killed in Nepal floods, PM Modi speaks to Balen Shah, and more
Dasgaja from the sky: Why India and Nepal are deploying drones over no-man’s land
Michigan puts $6.5 million toward 22,650 Keweenaw acres as conservation fund tops $1.4 billion
stories.summary: Michigan’s Natural Resources Trust Fund is marking 50 years of supporting land conservation and outdoor recreation. Created in 1976 using earnings from state-owned oil, gas and mineral revenues, the fund has awarded nearly $1.4 billion so far. Its latest grants include $6.5 million to acquire nearly 22,650 acres in the Keweenaw Peninsula, along with funding for parks, trails, waterfront areas and recreation projects across Michigan.

stories.title: Prince Harry, Meghan and children arrive in UK after 6 years
Nepal flash flood unlikely to pose major threat to UP; 105 Indians among missing tourists
A New Zealand sailor spent years living alone on a remote Cook Islands atoll across 3 separate stays
stories.summary: Suwarrow atoll, once the secluded refuge of hermit Tom Neale, has transformed into the Cook Islands' inaugural conservation sanctuary. After Neale spent sixteen years in seclusion on Anchorage Island, the atoll was designated as a national park and bird haven. This vital area now protects critical seabird nesting grounds and marine ecosystems, allowing Neale's legacy to be honored through his preserved hut and a tribute on the island.

stories.title: This prehistoric Czech sanctuary is 1,000 years older than Stonehenge
New York City restaurants save 800 pounds of oyster shells daily to rebuild reefs
Nepal floods: PM Modi speaks to Balen Shah, offers support
'Highly malicious': India rejects with 'contempt' UN report on racial discrimination
Florida's underwater sculpture garden is now a living reef with 100+ species
In 1967, Emily Frew Oliver sold her Wyoming dude ranch to the US government but kept a life estate
stories.summary: The 4 Lazy F Ranch in Wyoming remained with the Frew family for decades after they bought it in 1927. Emily Frew Oliver turned the family summer retreat into a dude ranch in 1950. In 1967, she sold the property to the federal government but kept a life estate. She voluntarily gave it up in 2006, ending her family’s long connection with the historic ranch.

stories.title: Singapore is paying parents $55,000 to have babies; here's why
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking move, Singapore is launching a substantial financial support package designed for families with children. Targeted at reversing the alarming trend of declining birth rates, the government will provide up to S$70,000 per child until they reach seventeen. This initiative replaces previous schemes, providing consistent financial relief to parents, thereby encouraging family growth in the nation.

stories.title: North American crayfish introduced to Britain now threaten native species
Illinois cooling film kept Houston roofs 40°F cooler without electricity
Indian-origin former Optum director sentenced to 3 years in prison over $950,000 fraud scheme
Woman bought family farm in 1908, spent decades painting and birdwatching, then left it as sanctuary
stories.summary: Mabel Norman Cerio turned her 1908 purchase of Paradise Farm in Middletown, Rhode Island, into a lifelong connection with art, wildlife and conservation. An artist and birdwatcher, she planned a bird sanctuary during her lifetime and later left the property to the community through her trust. After her death in 1949, the land became the Norman Bird Sanctuary, which today protects 300 acres of coastal habitat, six miles of trails and diverse wildlife. Her legacy also includes her paintings, sculpture interests and historic links to artists in Europe.

stories.title: India, China could help Trump resolve Iran crisis through diplomacy: Hillary Clinton
Cloud seeding drones produce 19 million gallons of water in Alaska in 3 hours
stories.summary: A pioneering climate-tech startup claims its drones have successfully induced millions of gallons of extra rainfall in Alaska. By targeting existing clouds and promoting ice crystal growth, this technology could provide vital support for drought-affected regions in the American West. The Alaska trials sought to measure the precipitation output, a crucial step forward. Future assessments will be essential in confirming the method's reliability and broader application.

stories.title: MIT class project becomes $850M plan for 8-motor hybrid aircraft factory
Les Paul’s New Jersey home sold for $990K, then demolished; son says family got no warning
stories.summary: The New Jersey home of guitarist Les Paul was demolished shortly after its sale. This property served as his workshop and laboratory for recording innovations. His son expressed deep pain and questioned the lack of family notification. Efforts were made to save historically significant materials from the damaged house. The demolition raises broader questions about preserving creative history and private property.

stories.title: 'Questions don't stop with batons': Rahul Gandhi attacks Bihar govt over BPSC protests
Indian-origin Toronto man found dead at home; homicide angle being probed
‘Shouldn't it begin with Congress?' BJP targets Rahul Gandhi over 'smash the patriarchy’ remark
stories.summary: The BJP criticized Rahul Gandhi's "smash the patriarchy" remark, questioning its application within his party. BJP leader Bansuri Swaraj accused Gandhi of hypocrisy and lacking a positive agenda. She cited past Congress remarks against Kangana Ranaut and Hema Malini as examples. Gandhi's campaign focused on challenging patriarchal systems and empowering women's choices. He advocated for ending restrictions placed on women in Indian society.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Albert Einstein: "If a cluttered desk is a sign of a…"
stories.summary: Albert Einstein questioned the assumption that a cluttered desk signifies a disorganised mind. He suggested that an empty desk does not automatically indicate clarity or productivity. People possess diverse thinking and working styles which influence their environments. Creative processes can appear chaotic, reflecting experimentation rather than a lack of discipline. Ultimately, a person's ability to think and create matters more than their workspace appearance.

stories.title: Next Atlantic storm to be named 'Dolly' in an uncanny 'coincidence'
A Scottish scholar and his American wife bought an island, spent decades preserving Gaelic culture
stories.summary: Scottish Gaelic scholar John Lorne Campbell and American musician Margaret Fay Shaw bought the remote islands of Canna and Sanday in 1938 and made Canna House their home. For decades, they collected Gaelic songs, stories, photographs and historical records. In 1981, Campbell gifted Canna, their home and their extensive collections to the National Trust for Scotland, preserving their life’s work for future generations.

stories.title: Australia to hand-vaccinate 5,000 wild penguins against bird flu
Ohio workers rescue kitten from excavator; now she has a hard hat and a job
Columbia engineers develop pigment-free coating that kept surfaces 6°C cooler under Arizona sun
stories.summary: Columbia Engineering researchers developed a porous polymer coating that can cool surfaces below the surrounding air temperature without using electricity. The coating replaces conventional white pigments with nano-to-microscale air voids that reflect sunlight and release heat towards the sky. Tests showed the surface stayed about 6°C below ambient temperature in Arizona and 3°C below it in Bangladesh.

stories.title: Savannah audited 39,000 Flock searches and found 34 unjustified; 4 employees arrested
stories.summary: Four former Savannah Police Department employees have been arrested over alleged misuse of the Flock Safety license plate reader system. The arrests followed an internal audit of 39,000 searches, which flagged 127 for review and found 34 were unjustified. Six employees were fired, while the Georgia Bureau of Investigation continues to investigate the case.

stories.title: Thousands of ancient brains survived for 12,000 years; scientists uncover why
stories.summary: Recent studies shed light on how some ancient brains manage to endure over time. The availability of oxygen is pivotal in influencing the survival of brain proteins post-mortem. In moist, low-oxygen environments, decomposition favors protein cross-linking, which fortifies these proteins against degradation. This explains the remarkable preservation of certain ancient brains while other bodily tissues succumb to decay.

stories.title: Japanese engineer’s anime-inspired hair helped test a driver safety camera
Ancient DNA reveals two unknown human lineages hidden in modern genomes
How a family reunion in China ended in a 3-year prison term for artist Gao Zhen
stories.summary: Chinese artist Gao Zhen received a three-year prison sentence for his satirical artwork. Authorities charged him with "infringing upon the reputation of heroes" for his art. Gao's wife expressed deep disappointment and sadness over the unexpected conviction. His supporters argue the artworks predate the law under which he was prosecuted. The sentence highlights China's narrowing space for artistic and political expression.

stories.title: 47-year-old California pastor makes college football roster 30 years after an injury ended his career
'Become capitalists, raise money': Singer's 'advice' to Zohran Mamdani amid Bhagwat US event row
Nimaya Williams earns $40,000 BigFuture scholarship as one of only two students nationwide
stories.summary: Nimaya Williams has achieved a remarkable milestone by securing a $40,000 scholarship from College Board's BigFuture. This accolade was awarded to her for completing various college and career planning tasks available on their platform. The financial support alleviates a significant burden for her family regarding higher education costs, showcasing how strategic planning can create unforeseen pathways to success.

stories.title: Stranded for 11 months, no wages for 5: 7 Indian seafarers repatriated from Abu Dhabi tanker
‘Situation under control’: Delhi minister as city logs 2,308 H1N1 cases amid flu surge
stories.summary: In response to a surge in H1N1 and flu cases, Delhi schools are considering new safety protocols. Health Minister Pankaj Singh reassured the public, stating that the situation remains stable and should not instill panic. So far, Delhi has seen around three thousand influenza cases, with over two thousand attributed to H1N1. Hospitals are ready with adequate medical staff, medications, and isolation facilities to treat patients.

stories.title: 'Be ready for Cockroaches!' CJP doubles down on September 5 protest as 3 demands still 'pending'
stories.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party plans a September 5 march in Delhi over unmet demands. Three of four demands remain pending since the July 25 protest withdrawal. The party seeks compensation and withdrawal of FIRs against student protesters. Assurances were given by ministers after talks on July 25. The march will proceed from India Gate to the Police Headquarters.

stories.title: 6,500-year-old human tooth found in Serbian museum collection
Texas wildfire jumps creeks and rivers as powerful winds drive rapid spread
'We support protest for accountability': AISA backs CJP's proposed September 5 march
'Hijab on their heads, not minds': Owaisi calls Allahabad HC ruling 'attack on Islam'
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi criticized the recent Allahabad High Court ruling that denied a student the right to wear a hijab, labeling it an attack on Islam and individual religious liberties. The court dismissed the petition on the grounds of insufficient religious documentation, emphasizing students had followed uniform rules while reiterating that no enforceable right is granted to change school dress policies.

stories.title: San Francisco woman hires a $30-an-hour humanoid robot to clean her apartment
1,500-year-old child burial unearthed in Peru with whistles, rattle and vessel
stories.summary: Archaeologists found a 1,500-year-old infant burial in northern Peru. The child was buried with whistles, a rattle, and a sculptural vessel. This burial displays patterns characteristic of the ancient Moche culture. The discovery occurred in a residential area, offering insights into daily life. Excavations continue to expand understanding of the Moche community.

stories.title: Seven dead, nine Chinese workers missing after fire at gas chemical complex in Russia
stories.summary: A fire at a gas chemical complex in Russia's Amur region has claimed seven lives. Six Chinese nationals were among the deceased in the Tuesday incident. Nine more Chinese workers are currently missing after the blaze. The fire broke out at the facility and was later extinguished. The plant's press service confirmed the tragic events occurred.

stories.title: 11-year-old finds 48-million-year-old turtle fossil in Wyoming
SpaceX’s $100 billion bet on Louisiana Starbase: 3,000 jobs, rocket hub - why it matters
Oregon teen builds free platform to help students find research mentors and publish their work
stories.summary: Inspired by her own struggles during a research internship, Riya Velhal, a driven high school junior, established StratScholar. This innovative initiative is dedicated to providing mentorship and resources that empower young researchers, particularly those in middle and high schools. By fostering accessible research experiences and honing critical research and communication skills, StratScholar ensures that students are supported throughout their research journeys.

stories.title: Scottish town raises £6 million to create a vast 10,500-acre nature reserve
Trump sends Saudi nuclear deal to Congress, keeps Israel normalisation as condition
stories.summary: The United States has submitted a civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress. This pact will only proceed if Riyadh agrees to normalize relations with Israel. Congress has ninety days to review the proposed thirty-year agreement for potential nuclear proliferation concerns. The deal facilitates US companies' involvement in Saudi Arabia's nuclear program development. Saudi Arabia's stance on Palestinian statehood remains a significant hurdle for normalization.

stories.title: Lok Sabha Speaker seeks response from 20 rebel TMC MPs on disqualification petitions
Was PoK's Skardu airbase next after Sargodha? Ex-CDS Chauhan reveals why India switched targets
'They had gone towards Sargodha': Ex-Navy officer backs former CDS Anil Chauhan on Kirana Hills remarks
stories.summary: Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan discussed Operation Sindoor's success. He indicated loitering munitions were deployed near Sargodha during the operation. These munitions searched for radars and may have struck Kirana Hills. This occurred after failing to locate their intended targets in the region. Chauhan's comments clarified the operation's impact on the Pakistani hills.

stories.title: Singapore sends 70 tonnes of unwanted clothes to Malaysia to recycle
stories.summary: Singapore sends up to seventy tonnes of clothing weekly to Malaysia for recycling. This cross-border initiative gives discarded garments a second life through reuse and repurposing. The volume has doubled in two years, highlighting the growing scale of textile waste management. At the Malaysian facility, clothes are sorted for resale or material recovery. This partnership aims to keep textiles in circulation and reduce landfill disposal.

stories.title: ‘Secure, predictable sea lanes indispensable’: India urges UN to safeguard key maritime routes
stories.summary: India called for collective international action to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure. Secure shipping routes are essential for uninterrupted movement of vital commodities globally. Conflicts and attacks on maritime routes threaten food and energy supplies worldwide. India stressed the need for unimpeded humanitarian access and objective supply chain assessments. Strengthening domestic agriculture and diversifying supply chains are crucial for food security.

stories.title: 15 newborns killed in fire at Islamabad hospital's gynaecology ward in Pakistan
'Bro wait... Bharat Mata ki Jai': Kangana Ranaut hits back at Rahul Gandhi amid 'smash patriarchy' row
NMC orders monthly reporting of student suicides by medical colleges
US halts visa appointments globally amid Trump's immigration crackdown
stories.summary: United States visa appointments are paused worldwide for consular officer training. This initiative supports the administration's broader immigration enforcement efforts. Immigrant visa applicants are being notified of rescheduled interviews due to this program. The government is also tightening restrictions on legal immigration and visa issuances. These actions reflect ongoing reviews and adjustments to the US visa system.

stories.title: ‘They opposed Ambedkar’s Constitution, wanted Manusmriti’: Owaisi targets RSS, BJP
stories.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi has openly criticized the RSS and BJP for their connections to the Manusmriti, questioning their true allegiance to the Indian Constitution adopted in 1949. He emphasized the valiant efforts of Muslim freedom fighters during the resistance against British colonialism and pointed out VD Savarkar's letters to the British while imprisoned. The ongoing discourse regarding Manusmriti's relevance and constitutional principles is growing more fervent by the day.

stories.title: 'Warned by FBI, Canadian police of credible plot': Pannun claims fresh threat to life
A ketchup cap inspired engineers to build a motor-free shape-shifting robot
Port Houston donates $500,000 to 32 nonprofits for community programmes
stories.summary: In a significant move to bolster local communities, Port Houston has allocated $500,000 among 32 organizations focused on enhancing workforce training, educational resources, and health initiatives. A noteworthy portion of this funding is devoted to developing maritime career opportunities. Starting in 2027, upcoming grants will be aligned with the strategic Anchored in Action plan, reinforcing community development along the Houston Ship Channel region.

stories.title: California releases more than 3,000 endangered mountain frogs into the wild
Wiltshire couple face demolition of home they built for disabled daughter in 2022 after planning row
stories.summary: A Wiltshire couple who built a four-bedroom home for their disabled daughter in 2022 now face a council demolition order following a planning dispute. The property, built on Green Belt land, includes a basement and decking that were not part of the approved plans. The couple have appealed to the Planning Inspectorate, with a decision expected in autumn.

stories.title: 'I don't support the rally': Zohran Mamdani opposes RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat's Madison Square event
stories.summary: Bhagwat is scheduled to address around 5,000 members of the Indian diaspora at the iconic New York venue on August 29. His visit to the United States is part of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's centenary-year global outreach programme. "I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event,” Mamdani said at a news conference on Tuesday.

stories.title: ‘Separatist’ OCI card holder in SC, seeks nod to visit Kashmir
stories.summary: Appearing for Qazi, whose OCI card cancellation was annulled by a single judge bench of Delhi high court and appeals against which is pending before a division bench, senior advocate Parag Tripathi told the Supreme Court that the 82-year-old medical practitioner had visited India in the past and given his age and that of his relatives, this may be the last time he would be able to visit Kashmir.

stories.title: Congress’s pellet gun fire draws BJP 1984 counter
stories.summary: A BJP member brought up the “glorification” of anti-Sikh riots convict Sajjan Kumar to counter the Congress’s move to raise a matter that was not part of the agenda of “crimes against children”. Chugh’s remarks drew a sharp reaction from Congress MP Jai Prakash, who said the issue was not relevant at all. BJP has accused Congress MP Deepender Hooda of being laudatory in his tribute to Kumar.

stories.title: Ram Temple donation ‘scam’ whistleblower gets protection from arrest
stories.summary: Appearing for the petitioner, senior advocate Pradeep Rai told a bench of CJI Surya Kant that Upadhyay was the whistleblower and the first to report the alleged misappropriation of monies donated by devotees at the Ayodhya temple. He said since UP Police is vindictive, investigations into the alleged road accident case lodged against him coupled with charges under SC/ST Act should be transferred to an independent agency.

stories.title: A vanished giant cliff may explain Earth’s mysterious missing billion years
All Banke Bihari donations must go to deity: Supreme Court
stories.summary: Senior advocate Maninder Singh said the sevayats cover the donation box put up by the temple management committee with flowers to prevent devotees from putting their donations into it. These donations are then taken away by the sevayats, he said. Senior advocate Maninder Singh said the sevayats cover the donation box put up by the temple management committee with flowers to prevent devotees from putting their donations into it.

stories.title: Revised bullet train cost Rs 2 lakh crore, 2x of original estimate
stories.summary: Sources said most of the additional funding would come from budgetary support. So far, the funding of Rs 1.1 lakh crore has been from Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and budgetary allocation. They added that Railways has said high-speed trains will be manufactured in India and each of these would cost around Rs 390 crore to Rs 400 crore.

stories.title: Surrender within 3 weeks, SC tells ex-Tehelka editor Tarun Tejpal
stories.summary: Goa govt opposed his plea for exemption from surrendering and said his appeal was not admissible since he had not filed a separate application seeking exemption from surrender or shown a certificate that he has already surrendered as per Order XXII Rule 5 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2013. The Goa Police subsequently registered an FIR against Tarun Tejpal.

stories.title: NMC pushes old doctors to re-register, but can’t net new ones
stories.summary: With over 91,000 MBBS seats available in 2020-21, even with an estimated 75-90% pass percentage, at least 68,000 MBBS graduates should have registered to practice in 2025. Yet the Indian Medical Register shows just over 44,400 entries. That means at least 24,000 of those who graduated just last year are missing from the registry.

stories.title: Govt seeks 2 years to frame creamy layer criteria for PSU, private staff kids
stories.summary: In its application, Centre said, “On account of the serious challenges and implications with the implementation of the directions of SC, govt is committed to bring out a policy which will effectively address the observations made by SC, while also ensuring that the direct and indirect impact of the policy is fair and just.”

stories.title: Quote of the day by Aristotle: "The man of practical wisdom aims at..."
Texas Roadhouse says claims of employees discussing spitting in Black customers' food in a Facebook group are 'completely unfounded'
No intention to quit politics, Nitin Gadkari clarifies
stories.summary: Nitin Gadkari’s office said, “In that context, Gadkari said that he could no longer take on as much work as before and that the younger generation should be given an opportunity to take greater responsibility. His remarks were clearly related to the functioning and future leadership of the Trust. However, some television channels are presenting the statement as a political remark, taking it out of its actual context.”

stories.title: Of 27 lakh ‘logical discrepancy’ deletions in West Bengal, only 7 lakh appealed
stories.summary: A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana was informed by senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan that of total 38.1 lakh appeals filed before the SIR appellate tribunals, an overwhelming 31 lakh were filed by those who challenged inclusion of names in the rolls claiming they were ineligible to be voters in Bengal.

stories.title: ‘Do we need a 4th-party audit?’ PM raps secretaries over quality of public projects
stories.summary: Chairing the monthly Pragati meeting on Tuesday, Modi is learned to have told the top bureaucrats that such things are “unacceptable” and the system won’t work like this. Modi reviewed six infrastructure projects across railway, road and power sectors, spanning nine states with a cumulative cost of over Rs 30,000 crore. He said infrastructure projects should be viewed and monitored as an integrated whole, rather than as isolated sections, stretches or packages.

stories.title: 'We got this wrong': Target says sorry for Halloween costume that looked like racist caricature, pulls it down from collection
Kentucky golf course shut after low turnout is becoming a 225-acre park, 70% greenspace
stories.summary: A Kentucky county closed its 225-acre Fox Run Golf Course after it averaged just 9,000 to 10,000 rounds annually. Now, the former golf property is being transformed into a major public park featuring trails, climbing areas, biking facilities, water features and family spaces. Around 70% of the site will remain preserved as natural greenspace for future generations.

stories.title: In 1957, Georgia artist Eddie Owens Martin began transforming his inherited farmhouse and seven acres
stories.summary: Eddie Owens Martin, an innovative and unconventional artist, dedicated nearly three decades to transforming his land in Georgia into the vibrant, visionary art space known as Pasaquan. He intricately combined various cultural elements through his painted totems and impressive masonry. After years of exposure and deterioration, the Kohler Foundation intervened with a major restoration, breathing new life into this unique site.

stories.title: Foreign students must make an official request for authorization: ICE issues new memo as colleges pause CPT program; American students will also have to complete training
In 1903, rabbits were released on Hawaii’s Laysan Island as a food source; within a decade...
stories.summary: German immigrant Max Schlemmer introduced rabbits to Laysan Island in 1903 for business and entertainment. These rabbits rapidly consumed vegetation, leading to the extinction of three unique landbird species. President Theodore Roosevelt established the Hawaiian Islands Bird Reservation to protect the remaining wildlife. Federal authorities later removed Schlemmer and eradicated the invasive rabbit population by 1923. Conservationists have since worked to restore the habitat and reintroduce species to the island.

stories.title: Small island states can serve as labs for innovation and tech: Maldives prez
stories.summary: Delivering a keynote statement at the opening ceremony of the Small Island Developing States Global Business Network (SIDS GBN) Forum 2026, Muizzu outlined an economic modernization plan aimed at turning geographic constraints into digital and strategic advantages. With the global dialogue surrounding small island nations focused on their acute climate risk, geographical isolation, and structural economic constraints, Muizzu stressed that vulnerability represents only half the story.

stories.title: India, China to work towards political settlement of boundary question in long-term interests; Beijing stresses package solution
2 killed at NHAI construction sites in J&K
Hydel project shutdown triggers power crisis in J&K
stories.summary: The prolonged shutdown has widened the region’s power deficit. Jammu & Kashmir’s peak electricity demand stands at about 2,500MW in summer and 3,000MW in winter. With both Baglihar units largely unavailable for most of the past week, Jammu & Kashmir faced a shortfall of nearly 900MW. Built on the Chenab river, Baglihar stages I and II are among Jammu & Kashmir’s key power sources.

stories.title: 8 terror suspects held in Kashmir; arms-ammo, posters seized
stories.summary: Six arrests were made in south Kashmir’s Shopian district and two in Pulwama, also in south Kashmir. A cache of arms and ammunition was recovered in north Kashmir’s Sopore district, J&K Police said Tuesday, claiming the action had dealt a major blow to terror networks operating in the Union Territory.

stories.title: New Mexico has protected nearly 11,000 acres along the Mimbres River as a new wildlife area
stories.summary: In a significant conservation achievement, officials in New Mexico have successfully acquired nearly eleven thousand acres of lush land along the Mimbres River, now designated as a public preserve. This initiative not only safeguards essential water rights and desert habitats for indigenous wildlife but also enhances public access while fostering tourism and outdoor activities. The long-term impact of this effort will greatly benefit the environment and local communities.

stories.title: 'Country is not a dharamshala': Amit Shah sets target for illegal immigration-free India
stories.summary: Home Minister Amit Shah has announced a strategic vision to rid India of illegal immigration in the near future. This initiative involves collaborating with border states through a four-pronged strategy aimed at bolstering security. The plan includes the participation of border forces, state administrations, central agencies, and local communities. Shah further highlighted the commitment to tackle terrorism and drug issues with proactive interventions, aiming for a developed nation by 2047.

stories.title: "E20 fuel hazardous for pre-2023 vehicles, auto firms silenced by fear of raids": Arvind Kejriwal
stories.summary: Addressing a press conference in Goa ahead of a town hall on the issue, Kejriwal claimed top officials of leading car and bike companies have privately admitted that E20 fuel can cause severe damage to vehicles manufactured before 2023, but are refusing to speak publicly due to government pressure.

H-1B contracting firms under stricter scrutiny in new regulation: 'Why no new regulation for H-2B who work at Mar-a-Lago'
9,000-year-old arrowheads covered in strange markings leave archaeologists puzzled
stories.summary: Unearthed from the depths of Turkey, ancient arrowheads reveal enigmatic hand-carved symbols. These Neolithic treasures showcase intentional incisions rather than random scratches, prompting researchers to ponder their origins. Despite thorough investigations, the specific purpose behind these markings remains unknown. Observations indicate that this intriguing practice was limited to select communities, leaving archaeologists grappling with unanswered questions about their significance.

stories.title: Jimmy Donaldson started YouTube at 13; years later the channel turned into a $5 billion business
stories.summary: Jimmy Donaldson started uploading YouTube videos as a 13-year-old in Eastern North Carolina. Years of low-view uploads, intense YouTube analysis and aggressive reinvestment helped turn MrBeast into a massive media and business operation. From viral challenges and Feastables to Beast Mobile, Step and Beast Games, Donaldson’s channel became the foundation of Beast Industries, now valued at roughly $5.2 billion.

stories.title: Georgia sheriff’s office arrested a second deputy in one month over alleged Flock misuse
stories.summary: In a troubling turn of events, a second deputy from Habersham County, Jonathan Thomas, has been dismissed and arrested for misusing surveillance technology. He reportedly accessed the license plate reader system for personal use, following a similar incident involving former deputy Christian Brewer. As a response, the sheriff's office is enhancing regulations around sensitive data access, part of a broader state investigation into data misuse incidents.

Ohio student pitched nonprofit helping seniors use technology, wins AI leadership award
stories.summary: Hannah Joseph, a sophomore at Indian Hill High School in Ohio, attended Cincy AI Week through the school’s Experienceships programme and its partnership with Cincinnati AI Catalyst. Instead of staying quiet among hundreds of professionals, she introduced herself, asked questions, met speakers and pitched her nonprofit, Seniors Go Digital. Her initiative earned her the 2026 AI Next Generation Award, part of the Cincinnati AI Leadership Awards.

In 2022, CaseOh was mowing lawns for work; two years later, he won Content Creator of the Year
stories.summary: CaseOh’s creator journey moved at a ridiculous speed. In 2022, Case Dylan Baker was doing maintenance work with his father in rural Arkansas while making NBA 2K TikToks after work. His clips soon brought thousands of followers and pushed him onto Twitch. By December 2024, he had beaten several major creators to win Content Creator of the Year at The Game Awards.

stories.title: Florida voters have approved $35 million to buy and transform 5.8 miles of underused railroad...
stories.summary: Bonita Springs voters have greenlit a $35 million bond aimed at improving the essential rail corridor. This significant investment secures the central portion of the Bonita Estero Rail Trail, effectively bridging a gap within the Florida Gulf Coast Trail. Importantly, this development will enhance connectivity between the Estero and Collier County sections of the trail, with construction anticipated to commence in October following the finalization of the purchase.

Mentmore Towers, Batman Begins’ Wayne Manor in Buckinghamshire, could be seized over repairs
stories.summary: The real-life Wayne Manor from Batman Begins, Mentmore Towers in Buckinghamshire, could face compulsory purchase if its owners fail to repair the deteriorating Grade I-listed mansion. According to SWNS, authorities have ordered urgent restoration work and three bat surveys by August 2027. The historic property has suffered damaged roofs, cracks, broken windows and neglect.

Artist turns 600-square-foot cabin into 5,000-square-foot home and living artwork over 37 years
stories.summary: Luna Parc in New Jersey began as a 600-square-foot cabin that artist Ricky Boscarino started transforming in 1989. Over the years, he turned it into a 5,000-square-foot, 11-level home and studio filled with artwork, collections and unusual spaces. The property also serves as a teaching space where young local artists learn craft and business skills.

stories.title: 7,000-year-old beaver bone pit reveals how Europe’s first farmers used animal fur
stories.summary: Near Alsleben, Germany, archaeologists have unearthed a beaver bone pit that dates back 7,000 years. This remarkable find sheds light on the early farming communities and their sophisticated practices in fur exploitation. The arrangement of the bones points to organized hunting activities. Researchers suggest that such evidence indicates that these ancient peoples crafted intricate fur clothing to adapt to their environment.

stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi has publicly supported Kriti Sanon over her outfit in a Raksha Bandhan ad, asserting that women's clothing choices should be respected as personal. Sanon further pondered the absurdity of judging cultural values based on attire, affirming that genuine traditions stem from the heart rather than the neck. In 1867, New Zealand introduced brown trout for sport fishing; more than 60 million were released
stories.summary: In 1867, British settlers introduced brown trout to New Zealand, intending to enhance sport fishing. This decision led to the release of over sixty million trout, which had devastating effects on local fish populations, resulting in declines and even extinction of some native species. The presence of these invasive fish fundamentally changed stream ecosystems and insect behaviors, making their management a significant conservation challenge even today.

stories.summary: San Francisco is on the lookout for private partners to rejuvenate a 9.5-acre lakeside site, previously a shooting range that has been extensively cleaned up. The city envisions this area transforming into a vibrant public park and recreation hub, inviting proposals for water access, community spaces, and outdoor activities. This project aims to restore nearly a century of waterfront land for public enjoyment.

stories.summary: In a significant diplomatic encounter, National Security Adviser Ajit Doval engaged with Chinese Vice President Han Zheng in Beijing. Their discussions centered on boundary issues to ensure peace, while also enhancing economic and political ties. The leaders are committed to managing differences and promoting long-term bilateral cooperation, following a series of recent high-level discussions between Modi and Xi.

stories.summary: Upon losing his job at the factory, Harry Hartman transformed his passion into a breathtaking folk art garden made from more than 250,000 stones and repurposed materials. For 53 years, his devoted wife Mary cared for this enchanting space until the Kohler Foundation restored it and handed it over to a community non-profit. The garden is now a beautiful destination for public tours, showcasing Harry's visionary artistry.

stories.title: In 2014, Texas bought 17,351-acre Powderhorn Ranch; 15,000 acres later became a wildlife area
stories.summary: In 2014, a coalition of conservation groups bought 17,351-acre Powderhorn Ranch on the Texas coast for $37.7 million. A major share of the funding came from BP and Transocean penalties linked to the Deepwater Horizon oil spill. Four years later, more than 15,000 acres were transferred to Texas Parks and Wildlife Department as a wildlife management area.

In 1993, Minnesota turned 5,000 acres of abandoned iron mines and 15 flooded pits up to...
stories.summary: A former Minnesota iron mining area has undergone a remarkable ecological transformation over thirty-three years. Abandoned pits and damaged land now host extensive mountain bike trails and natural shorelines. This restoration effort has revitalized nearby communities and created new outdoor tourism opportunities. The clear, deep mine pit lakes also attract scuba divers and anglers from across the region.

American woman loses 100-year-old ring; husband finds it from 20,000 pounds of garbage
stories.summary: A remarkable story has emerged from Brooklyn, where Victor, a determined husband, embarked on an extraordinary quest through tons of refuse to recover lost rings. His wife inadvertently tossed a platinum family heirloom and a gold ring into the trash. With the help of a thoughtful sanitation worker, Victor unearthed the trash bag that held the cherished jewelry, including a historic platinum ring linked to a proposal.

In 1972, Lyndon Johnson gave away Texas White House, but his wife continued living there until 2007
stories.summary: Lyndon B. Johnson and Lady Bird Johnson donated their Texas ranch house and about 600 acres to the National Park Service in 1972, but retained lifetime rights to use the property. After Lyndon Johnson died in 1973, Lady Bird continued living at the ranch until her death in 2007. The property, known as the “Texas White House”, was then prepared for public tours.

Vande Mataram row: Is Congress taking a calculated gamble or walking into BJP's trap?
stories.summary: The Congress party's choice to sing two stanzas of Vande Mataram sparked intense backlash from the BJP, with Union ministers accusing them of engaging in appeasement politics and being responsible for the partition. Congress leaders defended their actions by invoking historical importance, while they criticized the BJP for politicizing the issue. This controversy underscores Congress's struggle to navigate its revival strategy amidst opposing pressures.

In 2022, Hunga Tonga sent water vapour into the stratosphere, altering ozone and radiation
stories.summary: An eruption from an underwater volcano released a massive cloud of water vapor into the stratosphere, impacting global weather patterns for two years. This additional moisture led to an initial cooling effect on the stratosphere while also modifying circulation patterns. The presence of sulfate aerosols played a significant role in blocking sunlight, creating a stronger cooling influence.

FSSAI crackdown: Food companies withdraw ‘100%’ and health claims after notices
stories.summary: India's food regulator FSSAI has taken action against several major food business operators. Companies like Amway India and Juza Foods have removed misleading claims from their products. These corrective actions follow notices issued over regulatory violations and consumer safety concerns. FSSAI's enforcement drive targets false s and labelling discrepancies across the industry. Many businesses are now revising packaging and withdrawing problematic s.

stories.title: In 2006, a gold mine became America’s deepest lab; scientists search for dark matter 4,850ft down
stories.summary: A former gold mine in South Dakota has been transformed into a major underground science facility. The Homestake Mine once produced about 41 million ounces of gold and 9 million ounces of silver, but today its tunnels are used to study some of the Universe’s biggest mysteries. Scientists conduct experiments searching for dark matter, neutrinos and rare radioactive decay, while also researching microbes, geology and geothermal energy. Located 4,850 feet underground, the Sanford Underground Research Facility shows how a site once built for mining has found a new purpose in scientific discovery.

stories.title: China's Xi Jinping to visit India with 400-member delegation for Brics: Report
stories.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to arrive in New Delhi for the upcoming BRICS summit next month. Accompanied by a robust delegation of around 400 officials, this visit marks a significant increase from his last attendance. This diplomatic mission comes at a crucial time as India and China aim to mend their relationship following past border conflicts.

stories.title: India mulls annual dope tests on all commercial pilots on a random basis
stories.summary: Indian pilots may soon undergo annual random drug tests for safety. The Directorate General of Civil Aviation is reviewing current regulations and policies. This move follows an incident involving an Air India pilot testing positive. Airlines are voluntarily conducting one-time dope tests on all their pilots. Investigations into a recent Air India flight incident are also ongoing.

In 2014, scientists set off 23 blasts to uncover magma hidden beneath Mount St Helens
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, researchers utilized controlled explosions paired with seismic technology to investigate Mount St. Helens' subterranean magma systems. They discovered a magma-reservoir located between four to fifteen kilometers deep. This extensive analysis employed numerous instruments to track seismic waves within the volcano, yielding vital knowledge about magma movements. Such understanding is instrumental in forecasting volcanic activity and potential eruptions.

Scientists reidentify Ireland’s “Kerry Cow” bones as bear and wild boar, challenging farming theory
stories.summary: Ancient animal bones from Ferriters Cove are now identified as bear and wild boar. This reclassification challenges decades of evidence for early farming in Ireland. Previously thought to be cattle, these remains are now understood differently. Modern scientific techniques revealed the true identity of these ancient specimens. This discovery prompts a reconsideration of Ireland's prehistoric transition to agriculture.
