Wallabies came to New Zealand in 1912; they now threaten to spread across a third of the country
stories.summary: Wallabies introduced to New Zealand more than a century ago have now spread across more than 200,000 hectares in the Bay of Plenty region. The animals feed on native tree seedlings, ferns and grasses, damage plantation trees and compete with livestock for pasture. Authorities warn that unchecked wallabies could eventually occupy one-third of New Zealand by 2065 and cause $84 million in annual damage.

stories.title: Sadhguru, Graphic India team up for animated film 'Shiva -The Adiyogi'
stories.summary: In an exciting collaboration, Sadhguru and Graphic India are creating an animated feature film that focuses on Shiva's portrayal as Adiyogi and the foundational concepts of Yoga. Rich in yogic narratives, this film will be narrated by Sadhguru and is slated for a global theatrical release in 2027, as the production progresses toward delivering a unique cinematic experience.

stories.summary: Dr DisRespect has seemingly threatened Nickmercs during aCall of Duty Modern Warfare 4Beta livestream. After a viewer asked about streamer skins, the Doc questioned whether Nickmercs was in the game before calling him a “phony” and “wannabe tough guy.” He also made a gesture suggesting a strike to the face. In another clip, Dr DisRespect claimed Nickmercs walked away after being confronted by him previously.

stories.title: Meet Jeremiah Bents, the Minnesota student who recreated Mars soil to test water cleanup
stories.summary: Jeremiah Bents, a Minnesota student, explored water filtration using Mars soil simulant. His project examined ammonia removal from contaminated water in a laboratory setting. This innovative work earned him the Earth Systems Science Award at a state science fair. He received guidance from university researchers and a NASA scientist. Bents' experiment demonstrated a practical application for future space missions.

BJP leaders had gathered there to flag off "Pavan Mati Kalash" processions for Sant Ravidas' birth anniversary. AAP MLA Kuldeep Kumar shared a video showing the event amidst flooded stadium grounds. He sarcastically congratulated Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta for the arrangements. The BJP stated the campaign aims to spread Sant Ravidas' teachings across society.

Scientists turn plastic waste into protein cookies; food can tackle hunger and feed space crews
stories.summary: Researchers at Southern Illinois University Carbondale are developing protein-rich cookies made using plastic waste and agricultural waste. Called µBites, the cookies use PET plastic from bottles and discarded corn stalks and leaves. Programmed yeasts convert processed waste into proteins, fats, acids and flavouring molecules. The NASA-linked project is aimed at developing food for resource-limited environments, including future deep-space missions.

“I deceived people, I lied”: Woman pretended to be a child for years, convicted of fraud
stories.summary: In a shocking case from Brazil, Amanda Maria Souza de Oliveira was found guilty of fraud and assuming a false identity, having lived undetected as a child for years. Although she confessed to her masquerade, she maintained that her motivations were rooted in personal vulnerability rather than dishonesty. The court, however, sentenced her to prison for her deceptive actions, highlighting the seriousness of her offenses.

Assam: CM Himanta meets Nitin Gadkari, seeks flood-resilient highways, restoration of damaged roads
stories.summary: In a crucial meeting in New Delhi, Assam's Chief Minister and Union Minister Nitin Gadkari focused on the urgent need to rehabilitate National Highways affected by recent floods. They prioritized an evidence-driven strategy for enhancing drainage systems, which included critical improvements to bridges and culverts.

stories.title: ‘Grain’ revolution: How lost varieties of rice are coming back
stories.summary: Decades after disappearing from Indian fields and kitchens, heirloom paddy is making a comeback, powered by seed savers, small farmers, and an appetite for what was once lost, write Sneha Bhura & Deepthi Sanjiv.

He stated the proposed legislation violates constitutional basics and federal democracy principles. Chidambaram believes the bill's text prevents elections in 2029, which he sees as fortunate. The parliamentary committee received suggestions to define grounds for deferring state polls. Opposition parties plan a nationwide campaign against the "constitutional monstrosity" legislation.

stories.summary: A young student's research explored existing medicines for Alzheimer's disease protection. He identified two drugs, nintedanib and pirfenidone, showing protective effects in cell models. This drug repurposing approach offers a faster, less expensive research starting point. Wang's work highlights targeting APOE4 and brain blood vessel cell changes. His findings suggest further investigation into TGFβ pathway drugs is warranted.

These hidden lakes were found to fill and drain over short periods. This dynamic water system influences ice stream speeds and mass balance. The findings showed a hidden, active world beneath the frozen continent.

10 years of UPI: PM Modi hails India’s digital payments milestone and massive reach
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked ten years of the Unified Payments Interface, a transformative digital payment system that has reshaped financial transactions in India. UPI facilitates seamless bank-to-bank transfers via mobile, showcasing the country's commitment to digital finance. Citizens are urged to recount their journeys with the platform, celebrating its remarkable impact on everyday transactions.

Owens criticized Turning Point USA’s handling of events following Charlie Kirk’s death, arguing that people can oppose fundraisers for Clancy while also believing TPUSA should stay out of the case. Her latest comments add another chapter to her ongoing public feud with Erika and TPUSA.

stories.title: TikTok Mom Dies In Crash: creator ‘Mama A’ killed in 2-car wreck; GoFundMe aids 4 kids
stories.summary: Alyshia Rushing, known as TikTok’s “Mama A,” died at 26 after a two-vehicle crash in Montgomery, Alabama, on August 22. Police are investigating the crash, which also killed Landon Dunn. Rushing leaves four children, and a GoFundMe has been launched to support them and their father with daily needs, schooling, housing, childcare and counseling.

As Gary expanded and the lakeshore became valuable, she fought repeated legal battles against attempts to acquire the land. Decades after her death, part of her former property was included in a 212-acre donation that became protected land within Indiana Dunes National Lakeshore.

stories.summary: A Michigan couple bought an abandoned 160-year-old farmhouse for $26,000 and spent nearly $320,000 bringing it back to life. Samantha and Sean Kilgore tackled the massive restoration without professional renovation experience, transforming everything from the foundation to the kitchen. stories.summary: Dead fish have been removed from Poland's Gliwice Canal after a toxic algae bloom. This event mirrors the devastating 2022 ecological disaster in the Oder River system. Authorities are monitoring the affected waters to prevent further spread of the harmful organism. Elevated salinity and warm temperatures create conditions for golden algae to flourish. Scientists warn climate change may increase the likelihood of such ecological crises.

Researchers develop 3D-printed replacements for missing pottery parts, embed sensors in them
stories.summary: Researchers at Koc University have developed a method that uses photogrammetry, 3D printing and embedded sensors to repair damaged ancient pottery. The customised 3D-printed sections can replace missing parts while monitoring temperature, humidity, pH and physical stress. Tested on maritime amphorae from Türkiye and Italy, the approach could help conservators track changes and support long-term preservation.

stories.title: A black hole keeps tearing pieces off the same star, yet the star survives and comes back again
stories.summary: Astronomers have made fascinating observations of stars that are caught in a gravitational dance with supermassive black holes. As these stars approach, they lose material in a series of light bursts that fade over time. New research indicates that the stars' rapid initial spin is key to this phenomenon, as it limits excessive rotation during subsequent encounters with the black holes.

stories.summary: Scottish judoka Summer Shaw made headlines by winning a bronze medal at the Commonwealth Games, only to head back to her part-time McDonald's job to make ends meet for her sporting endeavors. Her engaging TikTok video on the matter caught widespread interest, highlighting her need for further financial support. Eager for sponsorship, she dreams of fully committing to her judo career.

stories.summary: CM Dhami also purchased rakhis made by the women of local self-help groups and appreciated their skills and hard work. The Chief Minister encouraged their efforts and said that the Sashakt Behna Utsav Yojana has provided livelihood opportunities to a large number of women, with many also benefiting from the initiative last year.

stories.title: GTA 6 Release: Kai Cenat dodges every alleged leak; vows to 100% game first
stories.summary: Kai Cenat says he has not watched any GTA 6 leaks because he is “committed to the actual game.” During his August 22 livestream, he also promised to become the first person ever to 100% GTA 6. The streamer previously said he could spend unlimited time playing after launch. With GTA 6 arriving in November 2026, Cenat already has his challenge planned.

stories.title: In 1900, JP Morgan bought 117 acres for daughter's wedding; land later went to Acadia National Park
stories.summary: A stretch of Maine coastline that was once part of a wealthy family’s private summer estate is now open to visitors as part of Acadia National Park. The land was donated in 1949 by Eleanor Morgan Satterlee in memory of her mother, Louisa, after the family property was badly damaged in the 1947 fire.

stories.title: ISS cricket experiment found microgravity-exposed larvae hatched earlier than ground controls
stories.summary: In 2005, scientists examined cricket reproduction on the International Space Station, where embryos grew under microgravity conditions. Interestingly, larvae emerged sooner than those on Earth, suggesting that microgravity affects developmental speed while preserving key neural structures. This research is vital for comprehending how life forms adjust to lesser gravitational forces, expanding our knowledge of development beyond Earth.

stories.title: Freezing liquid inside optical fibre makes light and sound interact 1,000 times more strongly
stories.summary: Scientists have frozen the liquid inside a special optical fibre to -196°C, creating conditions where light and sound interact more than 1,000 times more strongly than in ordinary fibres. The team found that the frozen fibre could still guide light and hypersonic sound waves. The breakthrough also helped researchers demonstrate optoacoustic memory, which could have potential applications in lower-energy photonic computing, quantum information processing and high-precision sensing.

stories.title: Meet Iris Shen, the 17-year-old Texas student who tested potential blood-cancer drugs in clams and her research won $150,000
stories.summary: A talented teen from Texas, Iris Shen, has triumphed in a renowned science contest with her groundbreaking research. By investigating a potential cancer treatment using clams, she discovered that these creatures exhibit effects akin to human cells. Her innovative work highlights marine bivalves as a viable and ethical alternative for animal testing, directly tackling the pressing ethical and financial challenges associated with conventional methods.

Delhi HC summons Iyer-Mitra, media portals over alleged disclosure of Saurav Das's address
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court has issued summons to commentator Abhijit Iyer-Mitra and several media platforms in a plea filed by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leader Saurav Das, alleging that his residential address and other personal details were published online without consent. X told the court that the posts allegedly containing Das's address had been removed and were no longer accessible.

stories.title: Asmongold Considers Twitch Exit: Destiny warns it’s Hasan’s dream; Rumble, Kick and YouTube loom
stories.summary: Asmongold is considering leaving Twitch if he receives another suspension after his recent 14-day ban. Destiny reacted to the possibility by saying it would be “Hasan’s dream,” arguing that Hasan could gain “sole reign” over the platform. Asmongold has mentioned Kick, Rumble and YouTube as possible alternatives, but he has not confirmed that he is leaving Twitch.

stories.title: After Australia, New Zealand proposes social media ban for under 16
stories.summary: New Zealand's Prime Minister Christopher Luxon proposed banning children under sixteen from social media. This legislation aims to protect young people from harmful online content and addictive technologies. However, two coalition parties oppose the bill, which may require opposition support to pass. Australia enacted a similar ban in December 2025, with other nations considering such measures. New Zealand also banned mobile phones in schools for all students during the day.

stories.title: Invasive Argentine ants are defending other pests in California, troubling farmers and leaving natives hungry
stories.summary: Invasive Argentine ants have formed a unique symbiotic relationship with sap-feeding insects, creating challenges for citrus groves and vineyards. First spotted in the U.S. in 1891, their expansion is aided by California's favorable climate and human activity. To effectively manage the situation, it's crucial to tackle both the ant populations and their pest partners as interconnected issues.

He emphasized the significance of constitutional values and the active roles citizens play in fostering national development. The joyous celebration featured flag hoisting and vibrant cultural performances by students, complemented by a disciplined march past from NCC cadets, truly reflecting the essence of unity and patriotism among the youth.

stories.summary: In a thrilling encounter off Cape Cod, a charter captain teamed up with an angler to reel in an astonishing blue marlin that tipped the scales at 1,260 pounds and stretched over eleven feet. This remarkable catch approached the Atlantic blue marlin world record from 1992, prompting researchers to investigate its head to gauge its age. After the impressive capture, the fish was generously shared among several admirers.

stories.title: Henderson Island rats survived a 75-tonne poison campaign and rebounded within two years
stories.summary: Conservationists attempted a large-scale rat eradication on Henderson Island in 2011. About seventy-five tonnes of poisoned bait were spread across the remote South Pacific island. However, a small number of rats survived the intensive campaign. Within two years, the rat population had recovered significantly to former levels. This event underscores the difficulty of achieving complete eradication and the resilience of invasive species.

stories.title: JPSC 'irregularities': Supreme Court issues notice to Centre, state after CBI probe plea

In response, police have filed three FIRs against the demonstrators. Students are calling for accountability concerning irregularities in the Jharkhand civil services examination. Opposition leader Babulal Marandi accused ruling party members of attacking the protesters. The court has also requested responses from the Centre, Jharkhand government, and JPSC.

stories.summary: Astronaut Chiaki Mukai took four medaka fish into space in July 1994 as part of an experiment to study reproduction in microgravity. The fish laid eggs during the mission, with eight of 43 identified eggs hatching in space. After returning to Earth, the adult fish gradually recovered, while the young “space medaka” continued to grow normally.

stories.title: Washington releases 20 lab-raised sunflower stars to restore kelp forests
stories.summary: In a remarkable conservation initiative, twenty lab-raised sunflower sea stars have been released back into the Salish Sea. The project, undertaken in collaboration with the Samish Indian Nation and various researchers, symbolizes hope for restoring ecological balance in the region.

stories.title: Mexico brings back bison 160 years after extinction; 47 animals are restoring the ecosystem
stories.summary: After an absence of 160 years, American bison have made a remarkable comeback to Coahuila, Mexico. These majestic animals have become vital ecosystem engineers, actively rejuvenating worn-out landscapes. Their presence enhances soil quality and promotes water absorption in the dry terrain. Additionally, this return facilitates the resurgence of native predators and other wildlife, reflecting a wider initiative aimed at restoring vital species throughout North America.

The restoration of the island's original name, Hawadax, marks a significant ecological achievement and sets a global benchmark for invasive species management.

World's highest-ranking penguin Sir Nils set to become a dad after partner lays egg at Edinburgh Zoo
stories.summary: The world’s highest-ranking penguin, Major General Sir Nils Olav III, is set to become a father after his partner Connie laid an egg at Edinburgh Zoo. The surprise arrival marks the zoo’s first king penguin egg in 17 years. Keepers are closely monitoring the inexperienced parents as they take turns protecting and warming the egg.

stories.title: In 2021, Alabama students began placing discarded Christmas trees along dunes to trap sand
stories.summary: Alabama's fragile sand dunes are being restored with discarded holiday trees, as students and volunteers team up to plant native vegetation along the coast. After Pigott's passing, the remaining residents departed, leaving the village completely empty. The historic district now serves as a preserved museum of coastal history.

50 years ago, this California sanctuary began saving some of the world’s rarest gibbons
stories.summary: Nestled north of Los Angeles, a gibbon sanctuary has championed the protection of endangered species for five decades. Established in 1976, this facility currently houses roughly forty primates of five diverse species. Beyond managing breeding initiatives, it facilitates animal exchanges and pursues non-invasive research while educating college students about animal husbandry. Looking ahead, the sanctuary seeks funding to enhance living spaces and develop an education center for visitors.

Exhausted owl stranded 70 miles offshore tries to board British Army boat, sailors bring it ashore
stories.summary: A British Army sailing crew found an exhausted barn owl 70 nautical miles from shore during the RORC Round Britain and Ireland Race. The bird fell into the sea three times before managing to reach their boat and collapsing on the deck. The sailors cared for the owl, named Little Regina, until a lifeboat took it back to land for treatment at a wildlife centre.

'There won't be a teleprompter': Sanjay Raut dares PM Modi, Shah to sing full Vande Mataram
stories.summary: Sanjay Raut challenged Prime Minister Modi and Amit Shah to sing Vande Mataram without teleprompters. He also questioned the government's economic record and rising inflation. The BJP condemned the Congress decision to sing only two stanzas of the national song. Congress leaders accused the BJP of politicizing patriotism and nationalism for political gain. Both parties are trading charges over the national song's recitation and its significance.

stories.title: Her ‘picture-perfect’ home has now become a burden
stories.summary: Residents in the Faroe Islands face challenges as tourists treat their homes like exhibits. Visitors often disregard private boundaries, peeking into windows and leaning on fences. This constant intrusion disrupts daily life and erodes personal privacy for homeowners. The article highlights the need for responsible tourism and respecting local residents' lives. Beauty should not become a burden, and visitors must show intention and respect.

stories.title: 'Party of loudmouths': CM Devendra Fadnavis says Rahul Gandhi's Pune event for women a 'showoff'
stories.summary: CM Devendra Fadnavis attacked the Congress, accusing the party of losing touch with voters and relying on public statements to remain politically relevant. "Their job is just to make speeches every day and stay relevant through television; that's all they do. They have lost touch with the ground. This party is limited to merely issuing statements," he claimed.

stories.title: New Zealand removed 200,000 mice from an island; native bird populations more than doubled
stories.summary: New Zealand's 2016 effort to remove an estimated 200,000 mice from Antipodes Island has been followed by a clear recovery in native bird populations. Monitoring confirmed the mice were gone in 2018, while surveys over the next six years found Antipodes Island pipit and snipe numbers had more than doubled.

Pakistan power crisis: Karachi residents riot amid outages lasting hours, block major roads
stories.summary: Residents of Karachi voiced their frustrations over persistent power outages by staging protests that blocked major thoroughfares. These demonstrations, which unfolded in various neighborhoods, led to significant traffic disruptions. Many participants reported enduring daily power cuts that lasted twelve hours or longer, with no prior notice. The ongoing electricity crisis worsened issues with water supply and local businesses.

stories.title: How Texas turned an abandoned golf course into five lakes to control flood
stories.summary: Exploration Green in Clear Lake City, Texas, transformed a former golf course into a 200-acre green space with stormwater detention lakes, wetlands and recreation areas. The project was created to help reduce flooding in the community, with its five planned detention lakes capable of storing 500 million gallons of water.

Apollo 15 astronauts found green glass beads on the Moon; decades later, they revealed evidence of water inside
stories.summary: Apollo 15 astronauts found unusual green flecks on the Moon's surface. These flecks were later identified as volcanic glass beads containing trapped water. Researchers discovered hydrogen within these tiny beads, proving lunar water existed. This finding challenged the long-held belief that the Moon was extremely dry. The discovery revealed significant water presence deep within the Moon's interior.

Hindu family of four found dead in locked home in Bangladesh’s Rangpur; strangulation suspected
stories.summary: A chilling scene unfolded when police discovered the bodies of four members of a Hindu family in their locked home. Initial investigations point to strangulation and a possible robbery. The family's absence since Thursday and the lack of phone activity raised alarm. Following a forced entry, officers located the victims throughout the house. Autopsy results are pending to establish the precise cause of their untimely deaths.

stories.title: Meet John Liu, the student who used corn stalks to recover lithium from water
stories.summary: John Liu has pioneered a remarkable project that utilizes agricultural byproducts like corn stalks and wheat straw to innovate lithium recovery methods. His technique leverages plant-based scaffolds to effectively concentrate lithium from dilute brines. Through his groundbreaking work, Liu garnered accolades at both state and international science fairs, showcasing a sustainable pathway for reclaiming essential battery materials and underscoring the role of agricultural waste in advancing environmental engineering solutions.

A family bought 11 farms and turned them into a big five wildlife haven
stories.summary: A South African couple began restoring the Great Karoo in 1997 by bringing together 11 former livestock farms into a 67,000-acre reserve. After removing fences, clearing invasive plants and allowing the land to recover, they began reintroducing wildlife. Cheetahs returned after 130 years, followed by rhinos, elephants and lions, while leopards later returned naturally.

stories.summary: Prime Minister Modi met with India's space startups, praising their ambition and energy. National Space Day celebrates Chandrayaan-3's successful landing on the Moon's south pole. This achievement marks India's significant progress in space exploration and scientific innovation. ISRO Chairman Narayanan recalled humble beginnings and highlighted global data sharing. The day aims to inspire greater interest in science and technology for all.

stories.title: DMK-BJP secret pact? Vaiko revives allegation as parties spar over delimitation
stories.summary: Vaiko alleges secret preparations for a DMK and BJP agreement in Tamil Nadu. He praised the current Tamil Nadu government for its achievements in its first hundred days. The DMK questioned Chief Minister Vijay's stance on delimitation after meeting Amit Shah. Southern states agreed to resolve water issues through mutual dialogue and constructive solutions. Virginia Beach turned 640,000 tons of garbage into a 60-foot hill, now a 165-acre park
stories.summary: Mount Trashmore Park in Virginia Beach serves as a unique example of transformation, evolving from a large landfill into a vibrant 165-acre recreational area. Opening its gates in 1973, this park now boasts serene lakes, extensive trails, and playgrounds, showcasing innovative landfill reclamation practices. Its picturesque setting attracts visitors who appreciate the blend of nature and community space, highlighting the benefits of repurposing land.

stories.summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan has signaled that the government plans to engage with the anti-reservation protesters who have rallied at Jantar Mantar. These protesters are advocating for an economic basis for reservations rather than a caste-based system. Paswan noted the existing 10 percent reservation for economically weaker sections and criticized the Congress for their protests outside a police station. Tejashwi Yadav’s backing of students' protests aligns with his political stance.

A judicial fellowship will allow young judges to learn best practices from partner countries. This shared jurisprudence repository will connect eleven legal traditions for mutual benefit. The proposal emphasizes building bridges of trust and fostering economic growth through justice.

They implore the Homeland Security Secretary to immediately stop this purchase.

The Association of Indian Medical Device Industry seeks reconsideration of this new labelling requirement. They emphasize ensuring patient safety without hindering export competitiveness.

stories.title: Cold medicines for under-4s face curbs over safety concerns
stories.summary: The Centre has restricted combination cold medicines for young children. Fixed-dose combinations of chlorpheniramine maleate and phenylephrine hydrochloride are now banned. These combinations pose risks and safer alternatives are available for children. Manufacturers must now prominently display warnings on all affected drug labels. This regulatory action follows extensive reviews and recommendations from expert committees.

stories.title: No work, no study, no training: 8.7 crore Indian youth caught in a career gap
stories.summary: With over eight crore Indian youth facing unemployment, a lack of vital skills hampers their job prospects. Financial barriers restrict many students from accessing crucial paid training programs, while graduates frequently settle for low-paying positions to assist their families financially. There is a stark career mismatch, as only a fraction of graduates find appropriate roles, making subsidized training and earn-as-you-learn opportunities essential for career advancement.

stories.summary: Assateague Island was once planned as a major resort community with thousands of homes, roads and commercial areas. Two powerful storms changed that future. A 1933 hurricane split the island, while the 1962 Ash Wednesday storm destroyed roads and structures. The island was later protected as a National Seashore in 1965, preserving its beaches, wildlife and natural coastal habitats.

stories.title: 'You don't belong to anyone else, but yourself': Rahul Gandhi's message to young women
stories.summary: During a dynamic gathering in Pune, Rahul Gandhi championed women's independence and personal identity. The company concealed Rockefeller’s involvement and eventually acquired more than 35,000 acres for $1.4 million. The land was later donated to the US government and became part of Grand Teton National Park.

stories.title: A Swedish hospital stores winter snow and pumps its meltwater through the building in summer
stories.summary: A hospital in Sundsvall, central Sweden, used an unusual cooling system that stored winter snow for use during summer. The snow was kept in a large, insulated storage area and its meltwater was circulated through the hospital to provide cooling. Researchers found that insulation was essential, as unprotected snow would melt by mid-June. The study showed that stored snow could meet the hospital's cooling demand from May to August.

MentalBERT performed best at about 82%, while ChatGPT-4o scored about 74%. Her findings suggest general-purpose LLMs may not be reliable enough for mental health assessment.

By planting thousands of trees and vetiver grass near Sarai Kale Khan, they aim to combat land degradation and curb soil erosion along the riverbank. This initiative, inspired by a successful ecological effort in Dhanbad's mining regions, is part of a larger strategy for restoring and preserving the Yamuna floodplain.

stories.title: No more boarding pass stamps: New immigration rule for international flyers from Sept 1
stories.summary: International travelers will soon need e-boarding passes on smartphones for immigration clearance. Physical boarding passes will no longer be stamped by immigration authorities from September one. This change aims to streamline the process and reduce passenger inconvenience. A pilot project is also underway to eliminate immigration stamping for Indian passport holders. The Bureau of Immigration is implementing these modernization efforts across airports.

stories.summary: In an innovative environmental initiative, a Boeing 737 from Canadian Airlines has been transformed into an artificial reef off the coast of Chemainus, British Columbia. Sunk in 2006, this aircraft has undergone a thorough cleaning by dedicated volunteers before its descent. Now known as Xihwu Reef, it has become a thriving ecosystem, supporting over a hundred different marine species that benefit from the habitat provided by this repurposed aircraft.

stories.title: 'Sometimes dynastic politics has its benefits': Akhilesh on how 5 family MPs helped SP
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav pointed to the presence of multiple members of his family in the SP and suggested that this had helped prevent a split in the party. "Have you ever wondered why the entire party did not split? Because there are five MPs from the same family. We also have several Muslim MPs, and some staunch socialists, so our numbers would not decrease," he said.

In 2021, 20 bonnethead sharks showed they use Earth's magnetic field to navigate
stories.summary: Bonnethead sharks have shown remarkable skills in using Earth's magnetic field for navigation. In controlled laboratory experiments, these young sharks were tested by manipulating magnetic environments. When exposed to southern magnetic fields, they successfully oriented themselves toward their original capture spot. This discovery implies that sharks might use magnetic fields as a navigational tool. Future studies will be essential to unravel how these creatures manage and utilize this magnetic data.

stories.title: Scientists realised 1,200 Starlink satellites could double as a giant scanner for Earth’s atmosphere
stories.summary: Starlink satellites are now helping scientists map Earth's upper atmosphere. Researchers used orbital data from Starlink to estimate thermosphere density. This method creates a two-dimensional map of atmospheric density variations. The findings offer a new way to study this difficult-to-observe region. Commercial satellite data is becoming an unexpected scientific resource.

stories.title: Victorian station used by British royals near Sandringham is on sale for £1.25 million
stories.summary: Wolferton Station, a former royal terminus renowned for its regal service, has been reinvented as a charming family home. For over a hundred years, it welcomed members of the royal family during grand occasions. Following its closure, a dedicated railway employee intervened to prevent its demolition. Now, this unique property is available for purchase at £1.25 million.

stories.summary: Following a contract cancellation with Flock Safety cameras, Hood County officials have initiated a refund request and equipment retrieval. This controversy feeds into a broader discussion across the country regarding the clash between enhanced investigatory methods and the preservation of individual privacy rights.

stories.summary: South Carolina shows the highest future potential for commercial real estate demand. A new index by the National Association of Realtors tracks economic indicators for this growth. St. George, Utah, leads individual metropolitan markets with strong office employment gains. Smaller and midsized markets demonstrate significant momentum compared to major coastal hubs. This index identifies areas where demand may be building based on data.

This move is seen by the BJP as undermining the national song's significance and legacy. The party passed a resolution to protect the honor and national character of the complete Vande Mataram. Union Home Minister Amit Shah also attacked the Congress Working Committee's resolution as anti-national.

IndiGo A321neo grounded after tail impact during Gorakhpur landing

Scratches were observed around the APU inlet during a post-flight inspection. The aircraft remains grounded at Gorakhpur airport for necessary maintenance. Technical and regulatory clearances are awaited before the plane resumes operations.

Asia’s high-mountain ‘water tower’ is losing 24 billion tonnes of groundwater annually, new research finds
stories.summary: Groundwater reserves in High Mountain Asia are experiencing severe depletion annually due to a combination of climate impacts and excessive human water usage. The irrigation needs in the lower basins dramatically exacerbate groundwater storage losses. If current consumption trends continue, projections suggest that depletion will persist. Although temporary glacier melt may provide a short reprieve, this will be followed by a more rapid decline.

stories.title: New snake species named after Guns N’ Roses guitarist Slash; here’s why scientists chose him
stories.summary: In a fascinating discovery, scientists have unveiled a new non-venomous snake species from New Guinea, named Lielaphis slashi. This remarkable naming pays tribute to Guns N' Roses guitarist Slash, also known as Saul Hudson, who has always been captivated by reptiles and the natural world. First encountered during past fieldwork, this small ground-dwelling snake signifies the incredible biodiversity and urgent conservation efforts needed in New Guinea.

stories.title: Logan Paul has listed his 78-acre California ranch with an extraordinary past for sale at $3 million
stories.summary: Logan Paul has put his notorious California ranch on the market for three million dollars. Speculation suggests he may now shift his real estate focus to Puerto Rico.

Its mirrored facade seamlessly merges with the lush forest while reflecting the beauty of each season. Crafted by KieranTimberlake, the design emphasizes harmony with nature. stories.summary: The National Medical Commission is putting forth a new proposal for mandatory re-registration of doctors across the nation. In the past, efforts to modernize the national registry faced significant challenges. This strategic chemical operation was designed to halt the deterioration of the lake's environment. Following the fish removal, biologists introduced native trout to reinvigorate the food web and support recreational fishing. Enhanced barriers and regulations now safeguard this restored aquatic habitat, exemplifying effective freshwater management.

'Can Standard 6 be spared 3-language plan this year?' asks SC

Ex-SC judge Subhash Reddy to lead probe into action on CJP Parliament march

stories.title: Tasmania spent 28 years removing invasive carp from two lakes; after 49,301 fish were...
stories.summary: After a remarkable 28-year campaign, Tasmania's fisheries service has successfully eliminated invasive common carp from Lake Sorell and Lake Crescent. This effort has seen the removal of over 49,000 harmful fish, leading to clearer waters and the revival of native plant life in marsh areas. The resurgence of wild brown trout has also enhanced recreational fishing opportunities for anglers, proving that large lakes can recover from invasive species.

stories.title: 'I am deeply sorry for the harm caused': Indian-origin hospital CEO takes responsibility for massive drug mix-up at a Nashville hospital during routine surgeries
US ambassador Sergio Gor in Ladakh, may meet Dalai Lama in first trip since Galwan clash
Govt announces panchayat poll process in Ladakh to fill ‘democratic vacuum’, district council polls next
Houses damaged in Jammu village subsidence; families take shelter in tents
First time in 100 years, North American river otter spotted in the Bronx River: 'I could hardly believe what I was seeing'
Both pilots fell asleep as a plane carrying 153 passengers drifted off course
stories.summary: In a startling incident, two Batik Air pilots dozed off simultaneously for roughly thirty minutes, causing their aircraft to veer off course. Communications from air traffic control went unanswered during this time. Thankfully, the plane landed without any injuries, prompting Indonesian authorities to reassess protocols regarding pilot fatigue and procedures for night operations to ensure safety.

stories.title: In 2002, New Mexico began one of America’s largest native-fish restoration projects...
stories.summary: A significant conservation initiative has successfully reinstated native trout species across more than 120 miles of streams by eliminating non-native predators and restoring habitats in two states. The reintroduction of the Rio Grande cutthroat trout has led to the establishment of a self-sustaining population, averting the need for federal endangered species status. This successful strategy serves as a blueprint for other western states aiming to restore native fish populations.

stories.title: Manchester synagogue terror attack: Iraqi national charged over failure to disclose information
Find out who your MP is: Canada's Portage College asks protesting Indian students to approach politicians for work permit woes
In 2006, Idaho launched a bounty-and-netting war on invasive lake trout; a decade later...
stories.summary: A vigorous initiative employing commercial nets and angler incentives has successfully diminished the population of invasive lake trout. This management program has fostered a remarkable resurgence of native species such as rainbow trout and sockeye salmon. Hydroacoustic assessments revealed kokanee densities that haven't been observed since the 1970s. The rebound of kokanee has instigated beneficial shifts throughout the broader ecosystem.

stories.title: 68-year-old Sheila Consaul bought Ohio lighthouse for $71,010 in 2011, restored it for over $300K
stories.summary: At 68, Sheila Consaul owns Ohio’s historic Fairport Harbor West Lighthouse, which she bought for $71,010 at auction in 2011. After years of restoration and more than $300,000 in investment, she transformed the abandoned century-old landmark into an off-grid summer home featuring rainwater collection, solar power, historic interiors and stunning views of Lake Erie.

stories.title: Major UK hotel chain CEO Joanna Boydell resigns amid security failings, sexual assault cases
In 1911, Norwegian whalers released 10 reindeer on South Georgia for food and hunting
stories.summary: In 1911, reindeer were introduced to South Georgia by Norwegian whalers. This led to significant ecological issues, as the absence of natural predators allowed their numbers to explode, resulting in harm to delicate coastal ecosystems and native species. A comprehensive eradication initiative was launched, successfully culling almost 7,000 reindeer, thereby aiding the natural recuperation of the damaged habitats, with native flora and seabirds starting to reappear.

stories.title: Iran rejects Trump's Hormuz 'total control' claim, says strait will reopen only on Tehran's terms
Six years after Michigan dam disaster, water returns to Smallwood Lake
stories.summary: Smallwood Lake in Michigan has started refilling after work on Smallwood Dam reached substantial completion in July. The refill began on August 4 and is expected to take eight to 10 weeks. Meanwhile, work continues at Secord and Edenville dams, with Secord facing a delay after crews found a problem with a spillway gate.

stories.title: 2.98 lakh URLs sent for takedown; I4C flags scams, CSAM and other unlawful content
stories.summary: Government departments requested removal of nearly 2.98 lakh URLs from social media platforms. States accounted for the majority of these takedown requests, sending 2.44 lakh URLs. The Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre flagged over 51,000 URLs related to various scams. This action follows widespread student protests and content blocking reports on social media. Government rules were amended to expedite the removal of unlawful online content.

stories.title: Virgin Australia removed a wheelchair user because his mobility device would not fit under his seat
stories.summary: Virgin Australia has issued an apology to Shane Hryhorec after he was removed from a flight due to a misunderstanding regarding the safety of his wheelchair's power add-on motor. Despite Hryhorec's explanation that the device easily detaches, airline staff insisted on his removal. This incident unveils the need for improved accessibility training in airlines. In response, Virgin Australia is reassessing staff procedures and offering Hryhorec a full refund.

stories.title: Parliamentary panel flags critical operational gaps at NGT, suggests measures to improve its efficiency
'Deceived, new fight begins': Jharkhand students after HC stays exam cancellation order
84-year-old woman found alive in rubble three days after Indonesia quake
stories.summary: In an inspiring turn of events, an 84-year-old woman named Paulina Pobi was successfully rescued after enduring three harrowing days trapped under rubble in Nitunglea village on Flores island. Against the odds, she survived without sustenance, while rescue teams faced significant obstacles from landslides and damaged infrastructure. This incredible story of survival emerged as a beacon of hope amid the widespread destruction and displacement caused by the earthquake.

stories.title: 'Must work together': Assam, Meghalaya CMs speak as Shillong violence triggers border tensions
US Waffle House cook's rap praising chain topped 1 mn TikTok views; weeks later, he was fired
stories.summary: Edric Riley, known as “Rockstar Riley” and the “King of Waffle House”, went viral after his rap song “Waffy Options” praising the restaurant chain crossed 1 million TikTok views. Weeks later, Waffle House fired him, citing repeated violations of its rules on filming promotional content on company property. Riley says he was promoting a company he loved.

stories.title: Help us: 4 Indian-origin teens from New Jersey call 911 during Mount Lafayette hike; they will have to pay a hefty fine for 'unprepared' adventure
Separated by Hamas in Oct 7 attack, Israeli couple reunites to marry 10 months after engagement
Why Pakistan’s donkeys are becoming valuable in China: What is driving this surprising demand
stories.summary: Pakistani donkeys are increasingly valuable due to rising Chinese demand for ejiao. China's own donkey population struggles to meet the demand for this traditional product. Pakistan has become a key part of this international supply chain after finalizing export protocols. The rising prices of donkeys impact local families who depend on them for livelihoods. This situation highlights the complex intersection of local needs and global trade.

stories.title: Delimitation, NEET and Cauvery: What Tamil Nadu CM Vijay discussed with Amit Shah
stories.summary: Speaking at the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council chaired by Union home minister Amit Shah, Vijay, who is also the council's vice-chairman, sought an assurance from the Centre that states which have successfully stabilised their populations would not be penalised through a reduction in their parliamentary representation. He said the issue had become particularly important as the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census nears its end.

stories.title: She got her first dolls' house at 8; now, at 101, she runs a museum
stories.summary: Val Ripley, aged 101, continues her lifelong fascination with dolls' houses and their historical significance. Her childhood toy, lost during the war, was rediscovered and inspired a museum. This museum showcases miniature homes as documents of social history and changing lifestyles. The collection features dolls' houses dating back to 1840, reflecting evolving domestic life. Val's enduring connection to these tiny worlds spans nearly a century.

stories.title: Texas woman left 6 acres in 1916; her governor son added 250 acres to create its first park
stories.summary: Isabella Neff's generous donation of six acres to the Leon River marked the beginning of Texas' first state park. Her son, Pat Neff, significantly augmented this by contributing an additional 250 acres. Developed by the Civilian Conservation Corps, the park faced challenges from flooding, necessitating ongoing repairs. Today, Mother Neff State Park is a shining example of familial generosity and commitment to preservation.

stories.title: Car salesman becomes Belgian prince after DNA test confirms royal paternity

Massachusetts police officer accused of using Flock cameras to track her ex-girlfriend
stories.summary: In a significant move, New Bedford police have paused their automated license plate reader system following allegations of misuse by officer Emily Pacheco. Investigations revealed a troubling number of searches for one specific vehicle's license plate. Pacheco is currently on administrative leave while inquiries continue, alongside an extended abuse prevention order from a judge. This incident raises critical issues regarding surveillance practices and the implications for data privacy.

stories.summary: Chairing the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council in Tamil Nadu's Mahabalipuram, the Union home minister said: "The people of South India and the governments have also established many excellent traditions in the fields of innovation and revenue generation." He said that "the whole of India should learn from South India in these two areas," as per the home ministery's statement.

Battle for UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi': Why parties are wooing women voters like never before ahead of 2027 polls
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh elections now prioritize women voters, who are a significant electoral force. Women's turnout has consistently surpassed men's in recent polls. Parties are actively wooing women with welfare schemes and cash transfers. Both the BJP and Samajwadi Party are making substantial promises to female voters. Winning the trust of over six crore women voters will be crucial for electoral success.

NASA offers up to $500,000 to develop technology for tracking atmospheric drag
stories.summary: In an effort to enhance the understanding of upper atmospheric conditions, NASA is inviting proposals for affordable technology solutions. The Orbital Clarity Challenge aims to refine predictions regarding satellite orbit variations caused by atmospheric drag. Participants stand to win up to $500,000 for their innovative concepts, along with the opportunity for a free test flight to test their technologies.

Built in 1913, this 177-foot steam tug survived two world wars but sank after hitting a...
stories.summary: Amidst severe drought, a historic steam tug once lost beneath the Sava River has resurfaced, delighting locals who flock to witness 'Sava's Titanic'. This vessel, which sank in 1945 after a tragic encounter with a mine, revitalizes memories of the Balkans' complex history. Its emergence underscores the grim water shortages plaguing significant European rivers today.

stories.title: America’s favourite vegetable could be hit by California drought: Over 90% of fresh broccoli comes from the state
stories.summary: The ongoing drought in California threatens the broccoli supply of the entire nation. Estimates indicate that shipment reductions could exceed twenty percent if conditions worsen. Experts propose that by growing more broccoli on the East Coast, costs related to supply chains could decrease and food miles reduced, leading to a more robust and dependable broccoli market across the country.

'UGC regulation under reconsideration', govt tells SC on controversial equity rules
stories.summary: The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the top court on January 29. At the time, the court said the provisions were "prima facie vague" and could have "very sweeping consequences", warning that they could potentially divide society and have a "dangerous impact". The court had also asked the Centre and the UGC to respond to three petitions challenging the new framework.

stories.title: Brazilian mother and daughter create seven-bedroom home from more than 8,000 glass bottles
stories.summary: A visionary mother and daughter duo transformed sustainability into an art form, building a seven-room home out of more than 8,000 recycled glass bottles. Incorporating elements like reclaimed wood and toothpaste tubes, this remarkable endeavor addresses the dual challenges of beach pollution and housing shortages in Brazil. Named the Salt House, it stands as a sustainable residence and an inspiring venue for community education on environmental responsibility and innovative reuse.

For over 50 years, Elizabeth Dickens recorded Block Island's birds, creating a historic record
stories.summary: For more than five decades, Elizabeth Dickens kept a detailed account of bird sightings on Block Island. Her comprehensive journals offered insights into local bird populations and their migratory habits while she inspired students through educational efforts about avian life. Dickens' commitment to her craft resulted in invaluable contributions to ornithology, emphasizing how crucial careful observation is for comprehending the natural world.

Germany opened a solar-walled city hall in 2017 that produced surplus energy
stories.summary: The newly constructed city hall in Freiburg exemplifies sustainability, generating excess energy through high-performance solar panels embedded in its roof and walls. Equipped with top-tier insulation and a heat recovery ventilation system, the facility efficiently optimises energy use. It also leverages groundwater for temperature control. Serving as a model for public sector energy initiatives, this striking structure highlights the potential of green technology in urban settings.

stories.title: Quote of the day by Carl Linnaeus: "Human beings, having, above..."
stories.summary: Human reasoning provides us with a special lens through which we can observe and understand nature. This ability to study and reflect upon natural processes imposes an ethical responsibility on us to avoid exploiting the environment. By grasping the intricate connections within ecosystems, we appreciate our place in the natural world. The wisdom of Linnaeus serves as a guiding light for today's pressing ecological issues.

'RSS believes it knows the truth for everyone': Rahul Gandhi attacks Sangh over ideology
stories.summary: Speaking at the "Hara Bhara Swaraj: A Tribute to Rajiv Gandhi's Vision" programme, the Gandhi Scion described the ideological contest in India as a deeper struggle over how people understand themselves, freedom and their place in society. The Congress leader also drew a distinction between the RSS's worldview and Mahatma Gandhi's idea of 'Swaraj', saying no organisation or individual could claim to know what is true for another person.

stories.title: Australian farmer spent three decades restoring land he once cleared; 24 bird species now live there
stories.summary: About three decades ago, King Island farmer Fred Perry began changing the way he managed his land after his children urged him to protect the environment. Once known for clearing native vegetation, Perry and his wife Shona began fencing and replanting parts of their farm. The long-running effort has restored habitat and brought 24 bird species to the property year-round.

EDP445 in trouble as Kern County DA re-examines 2021 "cupcake" incident after new documentary
stories.summary: EDP445 is facing renewed scrutiny after the Kern County District Attorney’s Office reportedly re-examined his 2021 “cupcake” incident following statements featured in Mike Clum’s documentary. The sheriff’s office says it is not actively investigating unless new information emerges. An extended documentary clip also shows Moreland discussing Jeffrey Epstein, Jared Fogle, R Kelly and Michael Jackson.

As 30% of Japan's temples risk disappearance by 2040, monks are using AI to help people speak with Buddha
stories.summary: By 2040, Japanese temples may face closure due to dwindling religious commitment among the populace. In a bid to attract more visitors spiritually, monks are embracing artificial intelligence to improve operational efficiency and enhance communication with worshippers. While some view AI as a useful guide in matters of faith, others argue that the essential human connection is irreplaceable.

stories.title: Doctors gave Seattle shipbuilder months to live; he sold his business, moved to an island and lived another 38 years
stories.summary: Robert Moran, Seattle's former mayor, made a monumental gift of thousands of acres for a state park. Following a serious illness, he relocated to Orcas Island, where he developed picturesque forest lands into a personal estate. His visionary donation led to the establishment of Washington's first state park, named Moran State Park in his honor, which remains a beloved destination to this day.

stories.title: 18-year-old Texas student trains da Vinci robot to remove tumours; succeeds in 3 of 4 tests
stories.summary: A brilliant eighteen-year-old student has engineered a cutting-edge framework designed for surgical robots. Utilizing a simulation strategy, this innovative system instructs robots on autonomous tumor excision. Tested on a da Vinci surgical platform alongside gel models, it achieved success by removing tumors in three out of four trials. This pioneering research paves the way for the future of medical robotics.

stories.title: Manhattan’s traffic-packed Broadway is slowly becoming a 5-mile wildlife corridor
stories.summary: Manhattan’s Broadway medians are being replanted with native Northeast species under a long-term project by the Broadway Mall Association. The Great Green Way covers five miles of Broadway and aims to connect 83 green malls into a corridor that can support birds, bees and other wildlife. Twelve malls have been restored so far, with more planting planned through 2026.

In 1970s, Marty Bluewater bought land on island planned for 800 homes; he is now its only resident
stories.summary: Protection Island in Washington was once planned as a holiday community with 800 homes. Marty Bluewater bought a piece of the island in the 1970s, but conservationists later fought to protect its important wildlife habitat. In 1982, the entire 400-acre island became a National Wildlife Refuge. Bluewater was allowed to stay and eventually became its only human resident.

US Air Force major held again days after arrest for calling for Trump’s impeachment
stories.summary: A US Air Force major, Jason Watson, finds himself detained once more for voicing his criticism of President Trump and advocating for his impeachment. Currently in pretrial confinement, Watson's refusal to wear his military uniform led to this latest arrest. This incident follows his earlier detention on the Capitol steps for expressing political opinions, showcasing his awareness of the repercussions he faces for his stance.

stories.title: Panic in Amethi as 29 copper spheres emerge from ground during house construction; Archaeology (ASI) team examines suspected ammunition
stories.summary: During construction work in Bhanauli village, workers discovered twenty-nine large metal spheres buried deep within the ground. These intriguing copper spheres, each measuring sixty centimeters across, resembled ancient munitions. Local police and the Uttar Pradesh Archaeology Department quickly secured the unusual find. Specialists are now engaged in examining the spheres to determine their historical significance and origin, with plans for additional archaeological research to ascertain their context.

stories.summary: In Tamil Nadu, Union Home Minister Amit Shah presided over a pivotal Southern Zonal Council meeting, gathering representatives from five states alongside three Union Territories. The discussions focused on crucial matters such as water sharing and infrastructure advancements. This council acts as a vital forum for fostering dialogue between state governments and the Centre, demonstrating a commitment to cooperative federalism and effective dispute resolution.

Oldest evidence of life on Earth has been discovered in India in a 3.4 billion-year-old layered rock shows signs of microbial life
stories.summary: Recent discoveries in India have unveiled biological traces that date back approximately 3.5 billion years, indicating a significantly ancient origin of life on Earth. Researchers have confirmed the presence of photosynthetic activity and intricate metabolic processes within these samples, which originated from environments close to underwater hydrothermal vents. This remarkable finding represents the oldest known biological materials found in rock formations.

stories.summary: India urged greater transparency in UN Security Council sanctions decisions. Membership must not legitimize terrorists or pursue narrow political interests. Delays in appointing subsidiary body chairs affect Council effectiveness and credibility. Elected members seek more involvement in key UN processes. The Council's structure needs to reflect global changes since 1945.

stories.title: India makes its vow for longevity: Country's first longevity summit concludes at Fairmont Mumbai
Pulitzer Prize-winning poet bought a barren land in Hawaii and turned it into a 19-acre forest with more than 3,000 palms
stories.summary: W.S. Merwin, a celebrated poet, found solace and seclusion in Maui during the 1970s, where he dedicated himself to creating a lush 19-acre palm forest. This extraordinary project transformed a barren piece of land into a thriving ecological haven, showcasing an impressive array of palm species. Today, the Merwin Conservancy diligently safeguards this rich environmental legacy, ensuring it remains a vital part of our natural heritage.

stories.summary: The Supreme Court has mandated that the Centre set up specialized clinics for captive elephants, ensuring they receive essential periodic health checkups. Additionally, the ruling requires DNA mapping of each captive elephant to combat illegal trade. The court emphasizes the importance of maintaining these animals' welfare, instructing states to complete DNA profiling to thwart unlawful commercial activities and transfers.

stories.summary: In a remarkable discovery, a four-year-old boy stumbled upon a 16th-century gold pendant while metal detecting alongside his father in Essex. This exquisite relic, weighing just 8.68 grams and thought to contain a religious artifact, has been identified as a treasure trove. Valued at an astounding £2.5 million, this find provides fascinating insights into the religious practices and craftsmanship of the 1500s.

stories.title: Valkyrae Defends Thumbnail Artist: streamer says Uncharted art is not AI; warns on artists’ jobs
stories.summary: Valkyrae has addressed AI allegations surrounding her YouTube thumbnails after viewers accused her latest Uncharted artwork of being AI-generated. She defended her longtime artist, Anko, explaining that he creates her livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his creative process. Valkyrae said she understands why people may suspect AI but stressed, “But it’s not AI.” She also expressed concern about AI threatening artists’ jobs and livelihoods.

Owens Questions SD Card Handling: Video shows Terrell pocket card; chain of custody remains debated
stories.summary: Candace Owens’ newly highlighted footage has reignited scrutiny over an SD card removed from a camera positioned behind Charlie Kirk. Owens questions why the card was allegedly taken so quickly and why the person involved appeared to use his phone rather than collect other cards. She stresses that her interpretation is opinion, while raising questions about the footage’s handling, possible communication and why that recording was prioritized.

stories.summary: Millinocket, Maine, once thrived around Great Northern Paper Company, but the mill’s 2008 closure transformed the community. In Peter Santenello’s exploration, longtime residents recall lost jobs, stability and a shared way of life, while local businesses and tourism offer hope. As the town seeks new industry, its resilient residents remain determined to rebuild.

Following court directives, Roy presented himself to the investigation officer but chose not to respond to the questions asked by the authorities. The court had previously granted him interim pre-arrest bail, providing some protection amidst this legal turmoil.

82-year-old Tony Fahey builds ‘walking on water’ machine for charity record
stories.summary: At 82, Tony Fahey embarks on a daring 24-hour world record attempt on water using a unique human-powered vessel named the aqua elliptica. This remarkable challenge seeks to generate funds for Make-A-Wish UK, reflecting his commitment to supporting children with serious health conditions. Following a serious accident years ago, Fahey returns to the water to showcase his remarkable endurance and innovative spirit.

stories.summary: A talented high school student has pioneered a cutting-edge bioengineering method for the early detection of pancreatic cancer. By utilizing magnetic beads to isolate tumor-derived particles from blood samples, her clinical trials demonstrated remarkable accuracy. Her extraordinary research has secured her a spot as a national finalist in a prestigious science competition, offering a promising new avenue for timely diagnosis and improved patient survival outcomes.

In 1961, British scientists stopped farming a 4-hectare barley field and left it alone; 60 years later...
stories.summary: A groundbreaking six-decade study reveals that passive rewilding effectively fosters the development of lush native woodlands. Through protective thorny scrub, young trees thrived, shielded from herbivores, while wind and jays ingeniously spread seeds, outlining the woodlands’ unique patterns. After fifty years, the area began to mirror the characteristics of ancient woodlands, showcasing an eco-friendly and budget-friendly approach to achieving woodland restoration objectives.

In 1963, a California builder made a house that rotates 320 degrees using two washing-machine motors
stories.summary: A remarkable rotating house, built in 1963 by the imaginative Sam Harkleroad, is now available for sale, showcasing a one-of-a-kind design. Overlooking busy Highway 101, this property comprises seven homes, all presently leased, with a total price tag of $3.3 million. Harkleroad's distinctive architectural legacy thrives across Marin County, but his grandson has chosen to list the asset, citing the complexities of maintenance as a challenge.

stories.title: Giant 746lb bluefin tuna caught off Yorkshire after nearly 90 years as scientists explain UK return
stories.summary: A giant 746lb (338kg) Atlantic bluefin tuna has been caught off the Yorkshire coast, around 10 miles from Whitby, after nearly 90 years. Scientists say warming seas, recovering fish stocks and tighter fishing controls may be behind the species’ return. The catch comes near Whitby, where an 851lb British record was set in 1933.

Man and his dog uncover a 3,400-year-old Bronze Age axe in England
stories.summary: In an English forest, a fortunate man and his dog uncovered an astonishing 3,400-year-old axe head emblematic of Britain's Bronze Age. This remarkable find sheds light on the enduring mysteries of our ancient past, revealing the metalworking capabilities of prehistoric communities. Artifacts like this one remind us that hidden treasures await discovery in even the most familiar settings.

stories.title: Missouri engineer hand-built an underground home into a hillside; 50yrs later, it remains leak-free
stories.summary: A Missouri engineer spent years carving an underground home into an Ozarks hillside, building it largely by hand without an architect. Designed to resemble a natural cave, the property features steel-reinforced concrete, an earth-based ventilation system, heavy oak beams and railroad-inspired details. His son Zane now restores the remarkable 50-year-old home and surrounding 225-acre property.

Meet Natalie Muro, 18-year-old Colorado student who used an invasive plant to fight algal blooms
stories.summary: A remarkable eighteen-year-old student has developed an ingenious device aimed at eradicating toxic algal blooms. Utilizing wind-driven waves and invasive plant species, this unique system demonstrated impressive results in field tests, removing nearly all cyanobacteria and trapping decayed cell matter. This groundbreaking solution offers a cost-effective way to restore and revitalize unhealthy freshwater ecosystems.

stories.title: Amit Shah to chair meeting with CMs, top officials of southern states to resolve inter-state issues
stories.summary: In Mahabalipuram, Home Minister Amit Shah will oversee the Southern Zonal Council meeting, where crucial discussions about water sharing and education priorities among states will take place. Following this, he is set to travel to Siliguri to inaugurate new border security projects, and engage with personnel from Sashastra Seema Bal. His visit will wrap up with a comprehensive review meeting on border security.

stories.title: 1958, the US secretly detonated 3 nuclear devices 100–500 km above the South Atlantic
stories.summary: In a clandestine effort, Operation Argus conducted nuclear tests in the stratosphere over the South Atlantic Ocean. These detonations resulted in spectacular artificial auroras and fleeting radiation belts around our planet. The mission’s intent was to shield against Soviet missile threats and radar detection systems. Yet, the swift vanishing of these barriers caused significant communication disturbances, leading to the formulation of international accords banning nuclear experiments in space.

stories.title: Scientists simulate nuclear strike to stop a 160-metre asteroid impact
stories.summary: In a groundbreaking study, scientists conducted simulations showcasing the potential of nuclear warheads to neutralize hazardous asteroids. These experiments focused on strategies for fragmenting large asteroids prior to their collision with Earth. While this approach holds promise for planetary protection, it is viewed as a last resort, especially for threats detected late. Ongoing research is crucial for insights into fragment dynamics and their long-lasting consequences.

Government planning to bring E10 back? Clamour grows after top bureaucrat's remark
stories.summary: E20 is petrol containing 20% ethanol and 80% petrol. The government has promoted higher ethanol blending as a way to reduce crude oil imports, save foreign exchange and improve India's energy security. India also achieved its 20% blending target ahead of the original 2030 deadline. However, the nationwide shift has generated concerns among some vehicle owners, particularly those with older vehicles.

Two Mumbai doctors to receive Pakistan’s highest civilian honour for keeping Jinnah’s illness secret
stories.summary: In a remarkable recognition, two Parsi physicians have been nominated posthumously for Pakistan's prestigious civilian award. They upheld the confidentiality surrounding Muhammad Ali Jinnah's terminal health condition prior to Partition, demonstrating a silent commitment to their professional ethics. This discreet dedication played an inadvertent yet significant role in the formation of Pakistan. The award ceremony is scheduled for March 2027.
